agencyDescription:
The Skills and Workforce Development Agency (SWDA), a statutory board under the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), drives lifelong learning and workforce development to enable Singaporeans to take charge of their careers, learn for life, access good jobs, and grow in fulfilling careers. We enable employers to build a skilled, future-ready workforce, design quality jobs, and adopt skills recognition practices. Together with our partners, we build a trusted, high-quality, industry-relevant, and innovative ecosystem that meets the evolving workforce needs of both businesses and workers.   

Guided by our vision of a Singapore where everyone can grow in fulfilling careers, we live our promise of Building Skills, Growing Careers by nurturing lifelong learning, strengthening employability and enabling career growth for all, including our own officers, through a continuous learning culture and a supportive, flexible, inclusive working environment that fosters innovation, collaboration, and well-being.

So, join us to be part of a dynamic team driving the national SkillsFuture movement and building a strong Singaporean core. Together, we create opportunities, transform lives, and shape the future of work.
jobDescription:
SWDA is a dynamic and forward-thinking organization dedicated to empowering individuals and shaping the future of Singapore's workforce. As the National Skills Authority, SWDA leads the charge in driving the SkillsFuture movement, a national initiative that promotes lifelong learning and skills development. With a strong focus on innovation and collaboration, SWDA works closely with employers, training providers, and individuals to create a vibrant ecosystem of learning and growth. By offering a wide range of initiatives, programs, and funding schemes, SWDA enables individuals to unlock their full potential, acquire new competencies, and stay ahead in a rapidly changing job market.

The National Jobs-Skills Data Office, under the Research & Analytics Division, serves three core functions:
• Data and Algorithms Innovation and R&D: Undertake development of new data models and algorithms to serve whole of government’s jobs-skills intelligence needs;
• Jobs-Skills Product Management, Development and Delivery: Manage and enhance jobs-skills products, which includes UX/UI design and end-to-end product life cycle management;
• Data Management and Operations: Centrally manage data quality, data models and data infrastructure to support internal and external users

Come join this game-changing team in SWDA, where we empower employers, citizens, training providers, and policymakers to make informed decisions by using a user-centered approach, providing trusted source of jobs-skills data and insights, and a common set of jobs-skills taxonomies for a skills-first future!
jobResponsibilities:
As a Data Scientist, you will be a key member of the Data and Algorithms Innovation and R&D team, transforming complex data into meaningful insights that drive strategic decisions, building statistical, machine learning and graph models to solve real-world problems, designing experiments to measure impact and communicating findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. By combining analytical thinking, programming skills and policy understanding, you will help uncover opportunities, solve real-world problems and guide data-informed decision-making across SWDA.

  • Develop and deploy advanced analytical models to extract deeper insights from jobs, skills, and tasks data, applying statistical and machine learning techniques including feature engineering, model selection, and validation using appropriate performance metrics

  • Design and build scalable data infrastructure by creating modular, reusable data pipelines and prototyping advanced analytics solutions that operationalize insights to support evolving stakeholder needs across various partnership levels

  • Translate complex data signals into strategic insights through close collaboration with product and policy teams, ensuring analytical outputs meaningfully inform workforce and industry planning decisions that align with national skills development objectives
  • Drive continuous analytical improvement by evaluating and enhancing existing methodologies, incorporating new data sources, external datasets, and robust model validation frameworks to strengthen the analytical foundation

  • Lead analytical partnerships and collaborations by scoping and supporting projects with internal divisions and external partners, translating stakeholder requirements into well-defined data science problem statements and delivering comprehensive analytical solutions

  • Contribute to national jobs-skills data assets including the development of structured taxonomies, entity extraction pipelines, and knowledge graph representations that support Singapore's skills intelligence ecosystem

  • Champion research-backed innovation by staying current with emerging analytical techniques, tools, and methodologies, ensuring SIPD maintains cutting-edge capabilities in workforce analytics and skills intelligence
jobRequirements:
Experience:

  • Background in data science, statistics, machine learning, or related quantitative disciplines with demonstrated experience applying analytical techniques to both structured and unstructured datasets
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL for data analysis, modeling, and data pipeline development, with experience in machine learning model deployment or productionization
  • Experience with unstructured data processing, particularly text or language data using natural language processing, language models, or text analytics techniques
  • Proven track record in developing, evaluating, and validating statistical or machine learning models using appropriate validation approaches and performance metrics
  • Familiarity with data visualization tools and techniques for presenting complex analytical insights to diverse audiences
  • Knowledge of labour market, workforce, or skills-related data and analytics

Analytical and Problem-Solving Competencies:

  • Strong analytical mindset with ability to break down complex or ambiguous problems into structured analyses and testable hypotheses
  • Experience in translating business requirements into technical solutions and communicating findings effectively to diverse stakeholder groups

Collaboration and Communication Skills:

  • Excellent communication abilities to explain analytical findings and technical concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders, including policy makers and senior leadership
  • Self-driven contributor with strong ownership of analytical workstreams and proven ability to collaborate effectively across product, research, and policy teams
  • Experience in managing multiple projects simultaneously while maintaining high standards of analytical rigor and delivery quality

Successful candidates will be offered a contract in the first instance and may be considered for an extension or be placed on a permanent tenure.


Candidates are encouraged to sign up for a Careers & Skills Passport (CSP) account and include your CSP public profile in your resume. Please check out www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg for details on the CSP

jobDescription:
The Economics Department (ED) in the Ministry of Manpower advances evidence-based and data-driven policymaking through robust labour research, analysis and analytics. ED undertakes economic surveillance and forecasting, ex-ante policy analyses, ex-post impact evaluations, applied economic research and advanced analytics to inform manpower policies that shape Singapore’s labour market, workplaces and retirement outcomes.

Data Analysts work closely with economists, research analysts, policymakers and operational divisions to generate data-driven insights that support policy formulation, implementation and evaluation. ED’s work spans key areas such as labour market dynamics, productivity and human capital development, wages and inequality, labour security and retirement adequacy, and labour market policies and regulations. 

ED is organised into three sub-units:

•	Economic Research Unit (ERU)
Supports manpower policies that optimise workforce allocation, strengthen human capital and drive business outcomes.

•	Socio-Economic Research Unit (SRU)
Supports manpower policies that strengthen workplace outcomes, improve inclusivity and enhance retirement adequacy.

•	Analytics Research Unit (ARU)
Supports manpower policies by leveraging big data and advanced analytics to uncover deeper labour market insights, strengthen policy design and enhance operational effectiveness.
jobResponsibilities:
As a Data Analyst in ED, you will help to shape manpower policies in Singapore through the application of data science, advanced analytics and clear policy communication.

You will use a range of data analytics techniques – including machine learning, natural language processing, text analytics, network analytics, predictive modelling, statistical analysis, data visualisation and other frontier data science approaches – to examine traditional and emerging issues relating to manpower policies and the labour market.

Your work will contribute to strengthening the evidence base for policymaking, uncovering new insights from complex datasets, and supporting better outcomes for workers, businesses and Singapore’s labour market.
Your responsibilities will include:

•	Applying advanced analytics to manpower policy issues
Use data science techniques to analyse a diverse range of manpower issues, including workforce allocation, skills mismatches, job transitions, retirement adequacy, lower-wage workers, vulnerable workforce segments, workplace outcomes and business impacts.

•	Developing new analytical approaches and datasets
Identify, process and analyse novel datasets, including structured and unstructured data, to generate new insights on labour market trends, policy issues and operational challenges.

•	Using frontier data science methods
Apply methods such as machine learning, natural language processing, text analytics, network analytics, predictive modelling and simulation techniques to support policy analysis and decision-making.

•	Supporting economic surveillance and policy monitoring
Develop indicators, dashboards and analytical tools to monitor labour market developments, workforce trends and emerging risks in a timely and policy-relevant manner.

•	Strengthening policy design and operational effectiveness
Work with policymakers and operational divisions to translate data insights into practical recommendations that improve policy design, programme implementation and operational outcomes.

•	Collaborating with economists and researchers
Work closely with economists, research analysts and external partners to combine data science techniques with economic theory, empirical research and policy domain knowledge.

•	Communicating insights clearly and effectively
Translate complex analytical findings into clear, intuitive and policy-relevant insights for senior management, policymakers and other stakeholders.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for candidates who are intellectually curious, analytically rigorous and passionate about using data science to improve public policy.

You should have:
•	A degree, Master’s or PhD in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, Public Policy, or another quantitative discipline.
•	Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to frame policy problems and translate them into data analytics projects.
•	Strong quantitative and technical skills, including experience in statistical analysis, machine learning, predictive modelling, text analytics, network analytics and/or data visualisation.
•	Proficiency in programming and data analytics tools such as Python, R, SQL, Stata or other relevant software.
•	Experience handling large, complex datasets, including structured and/or unstructured data.
•	A strong interest in public policy, labour market issues and applied data science.
•	Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical findings clearly and logically to non-technical audiences.
•	The ability to work collaboratively with economists, researchers, policymakers, data specialists and operational teams.
•	A willingness to learn new methods, data sources and policy areas.

Candidates with experience in machine learning, natural language processing, text analytics, network analytics, causal inference, cloud-based analytics platforms, and/or dashboard development will have an advantage.

We are looking for a curious and driven individual with a passion for emerging technology to lead key initiatives that support STB's tourism innovation efforts. Tcube, or the Tourism Technology Transformation cube, brings STB's digital initiatives, resources and thought-leadership content onto a single platform to support our sector's digital transformation.

In this role, you will be our resident expert on robotics and its application to the tourism sector, with a particular focus on hotels. This means staying deeply informed on robotics developments, understanding the policy landscape, and building the right networks across government agencies and industry partners to ensure STB is well-positioned to support wide-scale robotics adoption in tourism. Beyond robotics, you will lead an experimental track that explores nascent and emerging technologies, working with industry stakeholders and government partners to test new solutions and secure the necessary funding and collaboration agreements to bring these pilots to life.

You will also engage closely with key industry forerunners and internal line units - harnessing the expertise and influence of the former to drive broader technology adoption across the sector, whilst advising the latter on how technology can meaningfully support their plans and priorities.

Success in this role means being the go-to person for robotics and deep technology within the team, building strong relationships across the whole-of-government ecosystem, and translating your knowledge into practical recommendations and pilots that move the needle on tech adoption in tourism. This position requires someone who is intellectually curious, genuinely passionate about technology and its possibilities, proactive in building networks, and comfortable operating across both strategic and operational work.
jobResponsibilities:
Robotics Lead

As STB's robotics lead, you will be the team's resident expert on robotics and its application to the tourism sector, with a particular focus on hotels. This means staying at the forefront of robotics developments both globally and locally, understanding the policy and regulatory landscape that affects robotics implementation, and building strong networks across government agencies and research bodies active in this space. You will identify the gaps and barriers preventing wide-scale robotics adoption in tourism, and develop a clear perspective on where STB can play a meaningful role in addressing them.

Experimental Track

As the lead for the experimental track, you will explore and pilot nascent and emerging technologies with the tourism industry, pushing the boundaries of what is possible beyond STB's existing innovation programmes. You will define the scope and parameters of this track, secure funding and collaboration agreements with industry stakeholders, and manage pilots from conception to delivery. This requires working closely with government partners and staying ahead of developments in the emerging technology space to identify the most promising opportunities for the tourism sector.

Tcube Champions

As the manager of the Tcube Champions programme, you will oversee a curated group of tourism industry leaders who are strong advocates for technology adoption in the sector. Your role is to review and refresh how STB engages with this group, finding new and meaningful ways to harness their expertise, networks, and influence to inspire and drive broader technology transformation across the tourism industry.

Tcube Advisor for Core Industry

As the Tcube Advisor for core tourism industries, you will play a pivotal role in shaping their technology landscape. You will conduct regular scans of the tech landscape to stay informed on the latest trends and solutions, identify key technologies and companies that can address industry pain points, and provide strategic guidance to STB's internal line units to help them adopt and implement new technologies that drive operational efficiency and enhance the visitor experience.

- Genuine passion for technology and its practical applications, with the curiosity and initiative to stay ahead of developments in the field

- Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to translate complex technology concepts into clear and actionable recommendations

MEPS+ serves the entire Singapore financial sector and requires 24/7 operational reliability, strict compliance with government regulatory frameworks, and close coordination with financial institutions and government agencies.

As System Manager, you are the operational and delivery owner for MEPS+ and related systems. You own the outcomes, and coordinate across software engineers, product owners, compliance teams, and external vendors to ensure system reliability, regulatory compliance, and successful delivery of enhancements and patches.
jobResponsibilities:
Operational Delivery & Application Portfolio Management

  • Own operational delivery outcomes for the MEPS+ application portfolio across interbank payments, government securities management, and domestic market infrastructures. Make and recommend strategic decisions on application rationalisation, consolidation, or decommissioning to optimise portfolio efficiency.

  • Coordinate release management and delivery cycles with product owners, ensuring timely and quality deployment of enhancements, patches, and security updates across major (semi-annual) and monthly patch cycles.

  • Own Service Level Objectives (SLOs) for applications under management. Review SLI and SLO performance reports produced by the SRE team, identify trends and deviations, and escalate or drive remediation as appropriate. Set requirements for monitoring coverage and alert quality; hold the SRE team accountable for outcomes.

  • Coordinate verification of monthly and quarterly system patching with the SRE team. Ensure patch outcomes are documented and meet compliance requirements.

Tech Delivery Manager Responsibilities (During Release Cycles)

  • Lead release planning and delivery activities during major enhancement releases (semi-annual). Coordinate with product owners, development teams, testing teams, and vendors to establish release scope, timelines, and deployment readiness criteria.

  • Manage release communication to all stakeholders. Provide status updates, escalate blockers, and maintain stakeholder alignment on release objectives and timelines throughout the cycle.

  • Own release governance and quality standards for MEPS+. Define the release readiness criteria and test governance framework that the Software Engineer executes against. Review and sign off on test outcomes, patch verification results, and release readiness reports before production deployment.

Incident Management

  • Own the incident management framework for MEPS+. Define and maintain incident escalation paths, SLO targets (P1, P2, P3), and communication protocols. During major incidents, lead stakeholder communication and coordinate the response — software engineers provide technical investigation and resolution support.

  • Drive root cause analysis and post-mortems following significant incidents. Own the documentation of lessons learned and track implementation of preventive measures to reduce recurrence.

Vendor Coordination & Procurement

  • Own vendor governance for outsourced components and services. Chair vendor performance reviews, monitor SLA compliance, and make escalation decisions when vendor performance falls short. Coordinate with software engineers for detailed technical review of vendor-delivered code and fixes.

  • Lead MAS's participation in procurement activities for outsourced services, including defining tender specifications, evaluating vendor proposals, and contributing to contract negotiations.

Compliance, Governance & Risk Management

  • Coordinate RFI responses across the team, ensuring accurate and timely submission of supporting documentation.

  • Plan and lead resiliency exercises including Disaster Recovery drills, manual contingency procedures, and CyberEx participation. Validate system failover and recovery capabilities. Maintain compliance with ICT Governance policies and standards specific to government financial infrastructure.

  • 8+ years of progressive experience in managing, operating, or delivering complex mission-critical systems. Minimum 3–4 years in a delivery management, operations management, or technical programme management role with clear accountability for system reliability or release outcomes. Experience with payment systems, securities settlement, or financial infrastructure is advantageous but not required.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead incident response at an organisational level — owning stakeholder communication, driving post-mortems, and implementing systemic improvements. Track record of managing high-stakes operational environments.
  • Proven experience managing vendor relationships, chairing performance reviews, and holding vendors accountable to SLAs. Experience contributing to procurement or contract management activities.
  • Strong experience coordinating release cycles across multiple teams — development, testing, operations, and compliance — with accountability for release readiness decisions.
  • Excellent communication skills. Able to explain technical risks, operational decisions, and compliance requirements clearly to senior leadership, business stakeholders, and regulators. Strong written communication for incident reports, post-mortems, audit RFI responses, and governance documentation.
  • Comfortable working across technical domains without requiring deep hands-on expertise in every platform. Able to engage credibly with software engineers and SRE colleagues, ask the right questions, and make informed decisions based on their input.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams — incident response, release coordination, compliance activities, vendor management — without losing attention to detail or governance rigour.

  • Experience with containerisation technologies (Docker, Kubernetes) or cloud platforms (OpenShift, OpenStack) at a conceptual or governance level.

The Southeast Asia and Oceania Division (SEAO) is a division in the Singapore Economic Development Board. SEAO (i) develops and executes on government-to-government (G2G) partnerships; (ii) actively engages the region’s top private sector players – including major conglomerates, sectoral champions, and high growth startups, and (iii) facilitates the growth of global MNCs in Southeast Asia via Singapore. You will have operational oversight over core cross-border economic initiatives, and support EDB’s corporate engagement in key regional markets including Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines. You will work with both global MNCs and regional conglomerates to best harness Singapore’s strengths and the complementary advantages of our immediate neighbours. You will need to understand and assess Singapore’s strategic interests, needs and develop the right solutions catered to Singapore’s position as a global business centre. You will also cultivate and maintain close ties with key influencers or decision makers in Singapore and the region ranging from government officials, industry leaders and company executives.

  • Bilateral Diplomacy: Work closely with bilateral government counterparts to align economic priorities, address cross-border regulatory frictions, and attract new investments into the region.

  • Portfolio Account Management: Support the management and engagement of strategic corporate relationships in Malaysia and the Philippines.

  • Engagement of key executives: Cultivate trusted relationships with senior company executives and next-generation business leaders to understand their regional expansion roadmaps and long-term priorities.
jobRequirements:

  • Deep Regional Context: Strong understanding of the Southeast Asian macroeconomic landscape, with specific familiarity regarding the corporate governance, regulatory environments, and market dynamics of Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines.

jobDescription:
The Economics Department (ED) in the Ministry of Manpower advances evidence-based and data-driven policymaking through robust labour research, analysis and analytics. ED undertakes economic surveillance and forecasting, ex-ante policy analyses, ex-post impact evaluations, applied economic research and advanced analytics to inform manpower policies that shape Singapore’s labour market, workplaces and retirement outcomes.

Research Analysts work closely with economists, data analysts, policymakers and operational divisions to generate evidence-based insights that support policy formulation, implementation and evaluation. ED’s work spans key areas such as labour market dynamics, productivity and human capital development, wages and inequality, labour security and retirement adequacy, and labour market policies and regulations. 

ED is organised into three sub-units:

•	Economic Research Unit (ERU)
Supports manpower policies that optimise workforce allocation, strengthen human capital and drive business outcomes.

•	Socio-Economic Research Unit (SRU)
Supports manpower policies that strengthen workplace outcomes, improve inclusivity and enhance retirement adequacy.

•	Analytics Research Unit (ARU)
Supports manpower policies by leveraging big data and advanced analytics to uncover deeper labour market insights, strengthen policy design and enhance operational effectiveness.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Conducting policy-relevant research and analysis
Analyse a diverse range of manpower issues, including workforce allocation, foreign and local manpower policies, retirement adequacy, lower-wage workers, vulnerable workforce segments, workplace outcomes and business impacts.

•	Supporting economic surveillance and forecasting
Contribute to ED’s monitoring of labour market developments, workforce trends and economic indicators to support timely policy assessments and decision-making.

•	Undertaking ex-ante and ex-post policy analysis
Assess the likely impact of proposed policies before implementation, and evaluate the actual impact of policies and programmes after implementation.

•	Applying quantitative and empirical methods
Use econometric, statistical, data analytics and modelling techniques to derive insights from administrative data, surveys and other datasets.

•	Building domain expertise in labour economics
Develop specialist knowledge of labour economics, public policy, empirical methods, data sources, analytical frameworks and relevant academic literature.

•	Collaborating across Government and with external researchers
Work with researchers, economists, policymakers and operational teams within and outside MOM to support policy thinking and strengthen evidence-based policymaking.

•	Communicating insights clearly and effectively
Translate complex research findings into clear, policy-relevant insights for senior management, policymakers and other stakeholders.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for candidates who are intellectually curious, analytically rigorous and passionate about using research to improve public policy.

You should have:
•	A degree, Master’s or PhD in Economics, Statistics, Data Analytics, Public Policy, or another quantitative discipline.
•	Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to conduct rigorous research and draw policy-relevant conclusions.
•	Strong quantitative skills, including experience in econometrics, statistical analysis, forecasting, policy modelling, simulations and/or impact evaluation.
•	Proficiency in statistical or programming software such as Stata, R or Python.
•	A strong interest in empirical research and public policy.
•	Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly and logically.
•	The ability to work collaboratively with researchers, policymakers and stakeholders across different domains.
•	A willingness to learn new methods, data sources and policy areas.

Candidates with experience in labour economics, applied microeconomics, programme evaluation, causal inference, data science and/or machine learning will have an advantage.

Our mission is to create sustainable economic growth, with vibrant business and good job opportunities for Singapore.

For more information on EDB, please visit www.edb.gov.sg

About the EDB Associate Programme
The global economy is constantly changing. Technologies are reshaping industries, businesses are rethinking where and how they invest, and competition between economies continues to intensify. For Singapore to stay ahead, we need officers who are versatile, resilient and able to make sense of these shifts to identify opportunities and translate them into meaningful outcomes.

The EDB Associate Programme (AP) is a 10-month programme designed to build the foundations of a career at EDB. Through structured training, personalised mentorship and rotations across different areas of EDB’s work, you will gain first-hand exposure to how we work with companies, industries and partners to shape Singapore’s economic future.

Work alongside colleagues in a high-performing, collaborative environment and be part of a team that cares deeply about Singapore’s success and challenges one another to do better.
jobResponsibilities:
What the Programme Entails

Your Associate journey begins with a structured bootcamp that introduces you to EDB’s mission, work and ways of working, and equips you with foundational skills.

You will then be rotated across multiple divisions. Each rotation will give you opportunities to experience new challenges and work with different colleagues and stakeholders. Through these rotations, you will gain exposure to the core areas of EDB’s work:

1) Investment Promotion – Engage directly with companies to understand their business strategies and make the case for Singapore as an investment destination. This involves building relationships with senior business leaders, analysing industry trends, structuring project proposals, and negotiating with companies on the terms of their commitments to Singapore.

What you develop: Business acumen, relationship management and an understanding of global business dynamics

2) Industry Development – Beyond individual company relationships, EDB works to strengthen our economic sectors. We do so by mapping out an industry’s ecosystem, identifying gaps in capabilities or talent, and working with companies, trade associations, and other agencies to develop strategies that make Singapore a competitive hub.

What you develop: Systems thinking, strategy formulation, partnership building and the ability to translate insights into actionable programmes or initiatives.

3) Policy and Planning – EDB charts Singapore’s long-term economic trajectory – where the economy is headed, what structural shifts are underway globally, and what that means for Singapore’s positioning. You will work on frameworks, policies and incentives that shape how EDB attracts and retains investments.

What you develop: Analytical and research capabilities, skills in policy development and evaluation, and the ability to synthesise complex information

All Associates will also undergo foreign language training, giving you an early foundation to strengthen your ability to engage businesses and partners from around the world.
jobRequirements:
There are two intakes:

  • 16 August 2027 to 15 June 2028

Who are we looking for?

We are seeking individuals who are purpose-driven and eager to make an impact, as well as those who thrive in dynamic, fast-paced environments.

You may be a good fit if you have:

  • Learning agility and curiosity – You are curious, learn quickly, seek feedback and adapt as you learn.

  • Critical thinking and judgement – You make sense of complex information, ask good questions and form considered views, even when information is incomplete.

  • Resilience and adaptability – You stay constructive through change, learn from setbacks and adjust your approach when needed.

  • Resourcefulness – When faced with something unfamiliar, you seek out the information, expertise and people you need to make progress.

  • Initiative and ownership – You take responsibility for your work, act with drive and follow through on your commitments.

Eligibility

The Associate Programme is open to:

  • Fresh graduates and early careerists with less than two years of working experience at the start of the programme in March/ August 2027

  • Graduates from all academic disciplines. You do not need to have studied Economics or Business. We welcome candidates from STEM, humanities, social sciences and other disciplines.

  • Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents

Proficiency in a third language (e.g. Japanese, French, German, Bahasa Indonesia) would be advantageous for engaging international clients, but is not a requirement.

jobDescription:

jobResponsibilities:

User research and stakeholder journey mapping

  • Plan and conduct stakeholder interviews, workshops, observations and user-testing activities with applicants, licensees, healthcare service providers, healthcare professionals and internal officers to understand needs, pain points and service expectations.
  • Map current-state customer and officer journeys, workflows and service blueprints to identify duplication, unnecessary effort, unclear hand-offs, inconsistent experiences and opportunities for improvement.

Future-state service and workflow design

  • Co-design simplified future-state journeys and workflows with process owners and subject-matter experts, including roles, hand-offs, decision points, service principles and information requirements.
  • Develop wireframes, prototypes, interaction flows and other design artefacts to make proposed experiences tangible and testable, while taking account of regulatory, operational, policy and technology constraints.
  • Facilitate design reviews and iterate proposed solutions based on user feedback, usability findings and implementation considerations.

Validation and outcome measurement

  • Define user-centred hypotheses, success measures and test plans for redesigned journeys, workflows and digital solutions.
  • Conduct usability testing, pilots and structured feedback activities to validate proposed solutions and identify improvements before wider implementation.
  • Document findings and translate validated improvements into prioritised requirements, design decisions and reusable patterns for subsequent transformation work.

You will support the delivery of the following transformation initiatives, working closely with the Deputy Director, process owners, regulatory officers, technology partners and other stakeholders. The initiatives may have synergies and are to be delivered over a 2-year period, not necessarily in a linear sequence.


Integrated licensing operating model

  • Conduct stakeholder journey mapping across health products, services, professionals and information to identify common needs, fragmented touchpoints and opportunities to provide a more seamless one-stop experience.
  • Support the design of stakeholder-facing journeys and internal routing, triage and hand-off arrangements that direct applications and enquiries efficiently to the appropriate regulatory teams and subject-matter experts.

Internal workflow redesign and AI-enabled automation

  • Review licensing, certification and enquiry-management workflows with process owners to identify unnecessary steps, bottlenecks, ineffective hand-offs and opportunities to harmonise workflows across products, services and professional licensing.
  • Prototype and test interim digital and AI-enabled solutions, including workflow automation, intelligent guidance and self-service concepts, and translate validated concepts into requirements for implementation.
  • Establish user and operational outcome indicators with relevant teams to measure whether redesigned workflows improve experience, effort, processing time and service responsiveness.
  • Develop reusable journey-mapping, workflow-design and AI/UX patterns and support their adoption across the division to enable transformation at scale.

System design, enhancement and consolidation

  • Translate redesigned journeys and workflows into clear business, user and digital requirements for systems supporting licensing, certification and enquiry-management, including HALP, SHARE and related regulatory systems.

Regulatory analytics

  • Work with regulatory and data teams to identify user and operational questions that can be addressed through analytics, including recurring stakeholder issues, demand patterns, processing bottlenecks and workflow performance.
  • Use insights from stakeholder research, workflow data and analytics to identify opportunities for further service and process improvements and to inform the prioritisation of digital and AI-enabled interventions.

Improving stakeholder experience

  • Design and test clearer ways for stakeholders to discover licensing and certification requirements, understand what is expected of them and receive timely, relevant guidance across their journeys.
  • Support the design and validation of AI-enabled self-service tools, prompts and reminders that help stakeholders identify relevant requirements and complete applications accurately, subject to appropriate governance and implementation considerations.

jobDescription:
The Environmental Health Institute (EHI) is looking for a researcher to join the Arthropod Ecology Section within the Vector Surveillance and Ecology Department, Vector Biology & Control Division.

The Section conducts research and biosurveillance on mosquitoes and other medically important arthropods, including biting midges, sandflies, fleas, ticks and cockroaches. Our work seeks to understand their diversity, abundance, distribution and population dynamics, and the environmental factors that shape these patterns. Taxonomy is an important foundation of this work. We combine classical morphological taxonomy with molecular approaches to identify arthropods, including emerging, invasive and poorly characterised species. We also detect, characterise, and discover pathogens associated with arthropods using next-generation sequencing (NGS) approaches.

Through this work, we generate scientific evidence to support Singapore's surveillance, risk assessment and preparedness for emerging and re-emerging arthropod-related public-health threats.

The position offers opportunities to develop and lead research, build new scientific capabilities and collaborate with researchers and public-health professionals in Singapore and internationally.
jobResponsibilities:
• Lead research and biosurveillance - Design and conduct field and laboratory studies on mosquitoes and other medically important arthropods, from formulating research questions to analysing, interpreting and publishing findings.
  • Advance arthropod ecology and taxonomy - Investigate the diversity, distribution, abundance and ecology of medically important arthropods. Develop and apply classical morphological and molecular approaches for species identification and characterisation.
  • Build laboratory colonisation capability - Establish and maintain colonies of mosquitoes and other biting arthropods to support biological and ecological research.
  • Investigate arthropods and associated pathogens - Apply molecular approaches, including NGS and bioinformatic analysis, to detect, characterise and discover pathogens associated with arthropods, and assess their potential public-health significance.
  • Apply research to public-health needs - Integrate ecological, taxonomic, molecular and pathogen evidence to inform surveillance, risk assessment, and preparedness.
  • Provide scientific leadership and build collaborations - Mentor junior researchers, contribute to research priorities and capability development, collaborate with local and international research partners, and publish and communicate research findings.
jobRequirements:
• Master's degree or PhD in Medical Entomology, Entomology, Ecology, Zoology, Vector Biology, Biological Sciences, or another relevant discipline.
  • A demonstrated research track record, including experience independently leading research projects, supported by peer-reviewed scientific publications.
  • Experience in one or more areas relevant to the Section's work, such as arthropod ecology and field surveillance, arthropod colonisation, molecular biology and pathogen detection, NGS and bioinformatics, or ecological and geospatial analysis.
  • Experience in arthropod taxonomy would be particularly valued, including morphological identification, taxonomic keys, reference collections, DNA barcoding or other approaches for resolving species identity.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to critically evaluate scientific evidence, recognise limitations and uncertainty, and develop scientifically defensible conclusions.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively across scientific disciplines and with research institutions, government agencies and other partners.
  • Good scientific writing and communication skills, with the ability to communicate research findings and their public-health significance to scientific, operational and multidisciplinary audiences.
  • Able to work effectively in field and laboratory environments and comply with applicable biosafety, ethical, regulatory and research-governance requirements.
  • Able to work on weekends or after office hours when required for field surveillance, specimen collection or other time-sensitive research activities.

The Psychological and Social Services (PSS) provides specialised psychological services to children, youth and families in the areas of abuse and trauma recovery, family resilience and parenting, and forensic mental health.

The Centre for Family Resilience and Parenting (CFRP) works to strengthen parenting and family relationships so that children can grow up in safer, more stable, and supportive family environments. We work with families both preventatively and where significant parenting difficulties or relational ruptures have already occurred. 

Through targeted parenting and family interventions, we work with caregivers, children and families to strengthen parenting capacity, improve family functioning, and build or repair parent-child and family relationships. Our work aims to support meaningful and sustainable changes in caregiving and family relationships, while reducing the risk of difficulties recurring or escalating. 

As a specialist centre for parenting and family-focused psychological practice, CFRP contributes to advancing evidence-informed interventions, strengthening clinical practice and building capability across the wider child and family service system.

As a Psychologist in CFRP, you will provide psychological assessments and evidence-informed interventions for individuals and families. Clients may have significant and multifaceted needs, including trauma, abuse and forensic mental health concerns and come from at-risk populations or be involved with the Rehabilitation and Protection systems within MSF. 

This role involves direct clinical work with caregivers, children and families, including home-based sessions, and requires flexibility to work outside conventional hours to accommodate families' schedules and availability. Ongoing clinical training and supervision will be provided, including training in evidence-informed parenting interventions and family therapy approaches, to support your professional development and ensure effective service delivery.

Beyond direct clinical work, you will have opportunities to contribute to clinical programme development and evaluation, consultation, practice development and capability-building in parenting and family-focused work.

jobDescription: As an Identity & AI Security Specialist, you will strengthen HDB’s identity security capabilities and enable the secure adoption of Generative AI and agentic AI. Monitor system health, capacity, availability, performance, security and integration dependencies; perform patching, upgrades, hardening, backup and recovery activities; troubleshoot technical issues; and coordinate maintenance and technology refreshes with internal teams and vendors.

This appointment will directly oversee CR and INV, ensuring that OSC’s processes are fair, robust, trauma-informed, evidence-driven and consistent with the OSRAA, while building a high-performing organisation capable of responding to fast-evolving online harms.

You will translate strategic intent into operational reality: designing and refining complaint handling frameworks, overseeing and developing strategies for investigations and case outcomes, setting service standards, and building strong inter-agency and industry operating relationships to achieve effective victim relief.
jobResponsibilities:
Strategic leadership and organisational set-up

  • Co-develop OSC’s multi-year operational strategy and implementation roadmap with the Commissioner and other members of the OSC’s leadership team, including the OSC’s operating model, resourcing plan and performance measures.
  • Establish the OSC as a trusted authority for online safety victim complaints through transparent standards, consistent decision-making and measurable service quality.
  • Establish the OSC’s as a global thought leader for online harm victim relief.

Oversee the OSC’s case resolution and investigations (core accountability)

  • Lead and partner with Assistant Commissioner (Case Resolution & Investigation) in owning the end-to-end lifecycle for the reporting of online harms, including intake, triage, evidence gathering, investigations, case assessment, outcomes issuance and post-outcome follow-up.
  • Set and enforce casework quality standards (e.g., timeliness, consistency, proportionality, victim-centred practice, record-keeping and audit trails).
  • Develop investigation protocols and escalation pathways for complex, high-risk or high-impact cases (e.g., coordinated or crossfire harassment, high virality online harmful activity, involving highly vulnerable victims).
  • Drive continuous improvement using case data and trend analysis to refine triage logic, prioritisation rules and operational playbooks.

Operational policy, frameworks and controls

  • Architect and maintain OSC’s operational frameworks and internal policies to implement OSRAA effectively (including guidance, decision frameworks, standard operating procedures and training standards).
  • Ensure strong governance, risk management and internal controls across case operations (including information handling, evidentiary integrity, oversight checks and process assurance).

Stakeholder engagement and ecosystem collaboration

  • Build and sustain effective working relationships with relevant government agencies, technology platforms, app stores, industry partners and community organisations to enable timely victim relief and reduce friction in cross-entity case handling.
  • Represent OSC in operational coordination fora, driving shared protocols and clear lines of accountability during incidents and surges.

People leadership, capability building and culture

  • Build, lead and develop multidisciplinary teams (e.g., case resolution officers, investigators, operations policy officers).
  • Establish a culture of professional rigour, empathy, learning and resilience, including strong supervision practices and quality coaching for case resolution officers.
  • Put in place workforce wellbeing measures, including structured debriefs, vicarious trauma support and safe operating norms for exposure to harmful content.

Corporate leadership and organisational management

  • Provide senior oversight of operational planning and resource allocation; partner corporate functions on workforce planning, budgeting, procurement, performance management and internal communications.
  • Support external communications on OSC’s operations (where appropriate), balancing public assurance with confidentiality and operational sensitivity.
jobRequirements:
Experience and domain expertise

  • At least 10 years’ supervisory experience leading operations, investigations, trust & safety, technology policy, regulatory operations, enforcement, or complex service delivery in public or private sectors.
  • Demonstrated experience in designing and running high-volume, high-stakes casework operations with clear service standards and quality controls.
  • Familiarity with how online platforms operate (including content moderation and enforcement processes, reporting tools, recommender systems at a conceptual level, and app ecosystem dynamics). Experience with online trust & safety, public policy, or online content regulation is advantageous.

Leadership and professional competencies

  • Strong judgment and ability to lead decision-making in ambiguous, sensitive and time-critical situations.
  • Excellent stakeholder management—able to build constructive partnerships while holding firm to statutory intent, public interest outcomes and operational integrity.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to craft operational policies, decision rationales, and executive-level briefings.
  • Proven people leader who can build capability, create psychological safety, and enforce high standards of professional conduct and confidentiality.

Resilience and wellbeing

  • You may be exposed to graphic content including (but not limited to) sexual material, minor safety, suicide and self-harm, violent extremism and bullying. Resilience, sound personal coping strategies and commitment to self-care are essential. OSC will support staff through structured wellbeing practices and supervisory safeguards.

Reporting line and working relationship

  • Reports to the Commissioner.
  • Works closely with the Commissioner and other members of the OSC’s leadership team to ensure coherent end-to-end delivery under OSRAA.
  • Supervises and works with Assistant Commissioner (Case Resolution & Investigation) in overseeing the work of CR and INV.

What success looks like (first 12–18 months)

  • A well-functioning complaints and investigations operation with clear triage, service standards and quality assurance.
  • Consistent, defensible case outcomes with strong victim experience and credible stakeholder confidence.
  • A capable team with established playbooks, training pathways, and wellbeing safeguards.
  • Effective operational relationships across government and industry that improve speed and quality of victim relief.

Position will be commensurate with experience.

Only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

agencyDescription:
In Singapore, having the rule of law and advancing people’s access to justice are not just lofty ideals but the backbone of a functioning and a progressive society. At the Ministry of Law, not only do we contribute to developing the legal frameworks and policies that uphold our way of life, but also to providing community legal services that Singaporeans benefit from. jobDescription:
Who we are
The Legal Policy Group (LPG) in the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) plays a critical role in upholding the rule of law, advancing access to justice, and ensuring a sound and progressive legal framework for Singaporeans. 

What the role is
Under LPG, officers at the Criminal Policy Division (CPD) do not just review laws — we play an important role in helping to shape the future of legal policy and governance in Singapore. Our team has driven reforms that keep Singaporeans safe by improving our criminal justice system. Some recent initiatives include:

•	Protecting the public from dangerous offenders: In 2024, CPD worked closely with MHA to introduce the Sentence for Enhanced Public Protection (SEPP) to better protect the public from dangerous offenders. The SEPP applies to offenders who commit serious offences like rape and culpable homicide, and who are assessed to pose a risk of committing similar offences in the future. Under the SEPP, such offenders will only be released from prison if they no longer pose a threat of serious harm to others. This regime came into effect in July 2026.  
•	Promoting inclusive justice: CPD supports the ongoing work of the Inclusive Justice Taskforce, which comprises representatives from the public and private sector. The Taskforce aims to develop recommendations to promote just outcomes and better support persons with disabilities and mental health conditions in their interactions with the criminal justice system. 
•	Promoting consistency and transparency in sentencing: CPD support the Sentencing Advisory Panel, an interagency group which formulates and published guidelines on matters relating to sentencing including, most recently, guidelines on the sentencing of scams-related offences. 
•	Safeguarding the quality of expert evidence in criminal proceedings:  Expert opinion such as psychiatric evidence plays an important role in criminal proceedings. In 2025, CPD introduced a framework to govern expert opinion, including setting up a Panel of Psychiatrists to strengthen the quality and objectivity of psychiatric expert evidence. 
•	Enhancing the victim compensation regime: In 2024, CPD operationalised enhancements to the criminal compensation process to encourage the use of compensation orders in favour of victims, and to increase victim participation in the process.  
•	Safeguarding the administration of justice and the rule of law: In 2024, CPD introduced the amendments to the Administration of Justice (Protection) Act to make clear that egregious cases of abuse of process, such as filing of fictitious claims for purposes of delaying criminal proceedings and persistently commencing manifestly groundless actions, will amount to contempt of court. 

We are a small, multidisciplinary team that values thoughtful debate, moves with gumption, and is unafraid of breaking the mould. Officers will have the space to challenge assumptions and propose new ideas.

This role is ideal for someone who is passionate about making a difference, thrives on intellectual challenge, and enjoys working collaboratively in a dynamic environment — and who wants their work to have tangible, national-level impact.
jobResponsibilities:
You will join us in a variety of ongoing and upcoming policy reviews and reforms for the policy areas set out below:

•	Contribute to legal reform: Work with fellow officers to review laws, propose reforms and pursue new initiatives, tackling both classic and frontier issues. If you ever wanted to rewrite the rulebook (legally, of course), this is your chance.
•	Drive change, turn ideas into reality: Turn complex policy challenges into tangible solutions that improve real lives — take legislation from idea to Parliament, collaborating with legislative drafters, experts, and stakeholders. Become the bridge between policy vision and practical reality.
•	Engage stakeholders: Work with stakeholders and partners to develop creative, practical solutions to issues of national significance. 
•	Drive implementation: Take an active role in implementing policy initiatives —assist with drafting subsidiary legislation, provide policy inputs on operations, and ensure that sound policy design together translates into practical execution.
jobRequirements:

•	[Excellent writing skills] Able to crystallise core issues through clear and concise writing
•	[Deep critical thinking] A sharp and analytical mind capable of distilling critical issues and sense-making from a wide range of information to arrive at effective policy solutions
•	[Domain-specific expertise] Able to develop domain knowledge to collaborate and/or co-create policy solutions with experts and professionals
•	[Design for implementation and communication] Able to contribute to policy thinking that factors in strategic communications considerations upfront, with sensitivity to implementation considerations

agencyDescription:
Established in 2001, the Health Promotion Board’s (HPB) vision is to build a nation of healthy people.

We aim to empower residents in Singapore to attain optimal health, increase the quality and years of healthy life, and prevent illnesses, disability and premature death.

To achieve this, HPB drives national health promotion and disease prevention programmes, spearheads health education initiatives and creates a supportive environment in Singapore where healthy lifestyle options are available and accessible for healthy living every day.
jobDescription:
The Health Promotion Board’s vision is to make Singapore a nation of healthier people.
Come be a part of this journey if you’re passionate about creating boundary-pushing work that drives behavioral change.

You will be part of HPB’s Physical Activity Department, within the Physical Activity and Healthy Ageing Division, dedicated to making active living a cornerstone of daily life. The department empowers residents to stay active by providing the knowledge, opportunities, and support needed to build sustainable habits. The department designs and delivers impactful programmes, from physical activity initiatives to literacy and community-driven efforts, ensuring residents have the knowledge and opportunities to stay active. By partnering with government agencies, industry leaders, and key stakeholders, it expands access to inclusive, high-quality physical activity options across daily routines and leisure time. Grounded in evidence informed, data-driven insights and capability development, the department evolves its strategies and work to drive participation, enhance well-being, and embed active living as a way of life.
jobResponsibilities: As a key member of Physical Activity Division, you will play an integral role in shaping and advancing HPB’s physical activity agenda, ensuring that strategies are evidence-based, coherent, and aligned with national health priorities. You will drive the division's planning cycle end to end, from developing workplans and strategic frameworks to tracking progress and preparing insights that inform senior management decisions. Keeping a close eye on the evolving local and global physical activity landscape, you will surface emerging trends and translate them into actionable recommendations that keep the division's work relevant and impactful. Beyond planning, you will build and sustain meaningful partnerships across government, community, and industry — coordinating joint initiatives, aligning shared priorities, and ensuring that HPB's physical activity programmes reach and resonate with Singaporeans across all walks of life.
jobRequirements:
Join us if you are a detail-oriented and self-motivated individual who enjoys working in a highly matrixed, dynamic and fast-paced environment. You should also possess:

  • Good analytical skills and attention to details, including the ability to structure ambiguous issues, develop practical solutions and improve processes for more efficient delivery.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to effectively manage and address the different needs and expectations of both internal and external stakeholders.
  • Collaborative team player that forges strong partnerships with internal and external stakeholders to drive shared outcomes.
  • Comfortable to navigate ambiguity, with a proactive mindset to identify and implement practical solutions independently

agencyDescription:

jobDescription:
The Deputy Director, Operations Department, provides strategic leadership, command and oversight of HSA’s ground enforcement operations. The role is responsible for developing and directing operational strategies to detect, disrupt and dismantle illegal activities that fall within HSA’s regulatory and enforcement mandate.

The Deputy Director work closley with Intelligence Branch to translate intelligence into operational outcomes, ensuring enforcement priority.
jobResponsibilities:
Reporting to Director (Intelligence and Operations), the Deputy Director (Operations) will lead his Assistant Director (Operations) and his team of operation and enforcement officers in planning and executing broad range of enforcement operations. The Deputy Director (Operations) will ensure that all operations are conducted safely and effectively, and in compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, and operational requirements.


Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:


Strategic Leadership and Operational Direction

  • Provide strategic leadership and direction for HSA’s ground enforcement operations
  • Oversee major, sensitive, complex and intelligence-led enforcement operations
  • Establish appropriate command and structures for major operations
  • Ensure operational readiness and the capability to respond effectively to enforcement requirements
  • Formulate, develop, implement and review enforcement policies and strategies to achieve effective enforcement objectives and outcomes;
  • Communicate and effectively implement SOPs with external agencies, where applicable;
  • Assist the Director in developing and reviewing workflow and collaborations with other Groups, Departments, Divisons;
  • Ensure strategic manpower development, resources allocation and deployment programmes are effectively implemented in the Branch;
  • Manage resources (including overseeing and managing a team of operation and enforcement officers) effectively and efficiently in order to maximise resources and productivity within budgets;
  • Coordinate and support ongoing networking across various forums regionally and internationally to strengthen anti-counterfeiting and enforcement capabilities (INTERPOL, WHO, ASEAN, etc);
  • Take the lead in major operations that happened within Singapore or across jurisdictions
  • Assist CEO and Director in managing media, high profile or complex cases.

Operation Planning and Coordination

  • Strengthen operational linkages between Operations, Intelligence and Investigation teams to support end-to-end enforcement outcomes
  • Translate actionable intelligence into operational plans and enforcement outcomes
  • Ensure timely sharing of operational findings with Intelligence Branch for further analysis, enrichment and follow-up
  • Oversee the planning and execution of major, complex, sensitive and high-risk enforcement operations
  • Coordinate resources and operational capabilities across relevant HSA departments and branches
  • Provide senior-level oversight during critical operations and manage operational contingencies where required

Inter-Agency Collaboration

  • Build rapport and foster good partnership through regular platforms with external stakeholders and law enforcement agencies for joint operations and enforcement initiatives
  • Represent HSA at relevant operational and inter-agency meetings, exercises and working groups.

Capability and Manpower Development

  • Develop the Operations Department's manpower, operational capabilities, equipment and training requirements.
  • Identify capability gaps and introduce appropriate operational practices, technology and equipment.
  • Develop officers' competencies through training, operational exposure, job enlargement and leadership development.

Performance and Resource Management

  • Establish operational priorities and monitor the Department's performance and outcomes.
  • Ensure effective deployment and utilisation of manpower, and other operational resources.
  • Provide timely operational updates, assessments and recommendations to the Director (Intelligence and Operations) and senior management.
  • Develop Ops Team’s long-term manpower, training and capability.
jobRequirements:
• Possess strong strategic and operational leadership capabilities, with proven command and decision-making skills.
  • Have experience in intelligence-led enforcement and be adept at stakeholder and inter-agency management.
  • Have a strong understanding of enforcement and regulatory frameworks, along with critical and analytical thinking abilities.
  • Have demonstrated experience in crisis and incident management, and exhibit a high level of integrity, judgement, and discretion in all matters.
  • Possess strong leadership qualities with the ability to command and motivate a team, as well as the versatility and decisiveness to perform effectively in dynamic and uncertain situations.
  • Be resilient under stress and demonstrate a genuine commitment and passion for protecting public health and safety.

jobDescription:
In EnterpriseSG's role as Whole-of-Government (WOG) Logistics Sector Resilience (LSR) Lead, the LSR unit is responsible for strengthening Singapore logistics sector's preparedness and response capabilities across disruptions and crises. The team's work spans both policy and operations – they identify and develop strategies to mitigate systemic vulnerabilities in Singapore's logistics sector and also develop and stress test activation plans. In an increasingly complex and uncertain environment, the team's work is central to ensuring that Singapore and the stakeholders they support can withstand, respond to, and recover from disruptions effectively.

You will work closely with colleagues across the public service and industry partners to stay up to date on expectations of- and the evolving state of Singapore's logistics sector. In this role, you will analyse complex and emerging risks that could disrupt the logistics ecosystem and translate them into clear, actionable policy recommendations. You will also design and run exercises, develop activation plans with defined triggers and coordination arrangements, and strengthen response readiness across logistics stakeholders and Whole-of-Government partners.

The portfolio is as varied as it is meaningful. No two days look the same, and the work you do will have a direct and tangible impact on Singapore's ability to navigate an increasingly uncertain world.
jobResponsibilities:
• Monitor resilience posture of Singapore's logistics ecosystem through tracking indicators such as capacity in the ecosystem and activation mechanisms
  • Map and develop capabilities required to bridge structural and emerging vulnerabilities in Singapore's logistics ecosystem
  • Curate and maintain relationships with public and private stakeholders to strengthen crisis preparedness of Singapore's logistics ecosystem
jobRequirements:
We welcome candidates at all career stages and from a wide range of academic backgrounds who share a strong passion for Singapore and her logistics ecosystem. We value initiative, curiosity, analytical thinking, creative problem-solving, the ability to work through ambiguity, and a strong collaborative mindset as a team player. Strong written and verbal communication skills are important, as is the ability to manage multiple workstreams and engage diverse stakeholders effectively.


Beyond these qualities, the ideal candidate should bring the following:

  • Degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Public Policy, Economics, Engineering, or a related discipline, though candidates from other academic backgrounds with relevant experience are equally welcome
  • At least 2 years of relevant experience in logistics operations, supply chain management, risk management, crisis management, or public policy, with the ability to quickly develop deep sectoral knowledge
  • Strong analytical and research skills, with the ability to synthesise complex information from multiple sources, identify systemic risks, and translate findings into clear, actionable policy recommendations
  • Experience in stakeholder engagement and relationship management across both public and private sector organisations, with the ability to build trust and influence without direct authority
  • Familiarity with crisis management frameworks, business continuity planning, or emergency response planning, including the design and facilitation of tabletop or live exercises
  • Ability to develop and maintain monitoring frameworks, track leading indicators of sector resilience, and proactively flag emerging vulnerabilities
  • Experience working in or with government agencies, statutory boards, or inter-agency platforms (advantageous)
  • Understanding of Singapore's logistics ecosystem including key players, infrastructure, and regulatory environment (advantageous)
  • Comfortable working with ambiguity and evolving priorities in a fast-paced environment, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams concurrently without compromising quality
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to craft clear policy papers, briefing materials, and presentations for senior audiences

How We Work Together

We value individuals who work well with others, communicate clearly, take ownership of their work, and are open to learning and improvement. You should be comfortable navigating change and contributing positively to a collaborative team environment.

The National Security Coordination Secretariat’s mission is to build a shared picture of cross-cutting national security risks, and mobilise the multi-agency effort needed to mitigate risks. 

We work to secure Singapore against risks in any domain that could compromise Singapore’s survival and success. This includes vulnerabilities to disruptions to day-to-day life, social divisions, and coercion to act against our national interest. Such risks impact multiple sectors and require multi-sector responses to effectively mitigate risks to Singapore.
jobDescription:
The National Security Coordination Secretariat (NSCS) is a unit under the Prime Minister's Office responsible for national security planning and coordination. NSCS works with agencies and stakeholders to develop and co-ordinate strategies to address national security concerns. NSCS also works with agencies to anticipate and identify emergent security risks, and to build up capabilities and resources to deal with these.

The role will give you the opportunity to strengthen:
 
•	Critical Thinking: You will need to keep abreast of national security developments and synthesise information across domains (geopolitical, economic, social, environment, information, etc.) to identify and analyse cross-cutting national security risks. These include economic security risks, digital security risks, concentration risks, and inter-dependency risks. 
•	Systems Thinking: You will need to integrate analysis of external developments with assessments of Singapore’s vulnerabilities and how the latter will change over time. You will recommend the best way to structure the Whole-of-Government response to the risk. This will require you to suggest constructive solutions which balance multiple policy considerations across domains. For specific risks, you could contribute to the full policy value-chain from strategic planning, policy formulation, policy-operations, to comms and implementation (e.g., legislation). 
•	Influence: You will need to mobilise colleagues from a wide range of agencies, with different mandates and policy considerations, to work with you on the overall risk assessment. You will need to build consensus on the risk level Singapore can live with and the Whole-of-Government action needed to mitigate the risks. This would require you to build extensive and deep networks across domains and seniority levels, and develop a deep understanding of their considerations and constraints.
jobResponsibilities:
You will work in a team / lead a team:

•	To hunt out Singapore’s cross-cutting vulnerabilities (e.g., in critical infrastructure, social resilience) that could be exploited/ disrupted and build shared risk pictures (through policy analysis and/ or data analysis) to inform decision-making by public sector leaders.
•	To mobilise collective Whole-of-Government efforts to tackle complex, collective-action problems. This could involve putting forth recommendations to achieve better national outcomes through balancing differing policy objectives.

Depending on your performance and experience, you could be given the opportunity to lead a team (of 2-3 officers) or project, and individually handle complex and sensitive policy pieces that cut across NSCS’s work.

jobDescription: The Segment Marketing and Visitor Experience Division (SMVE) is a division within Marketing Group that champions target segment strategies to support quality tourism. jobResponsibilities:
In this role, your main focus would be on the BTMICE segment. You will need to gain in-depth MICE target segment (MICE event organisers and travellers) understanding to identify gaps and opportunities and develop actionable insights that will inform the formulation of a segment-specific marketing strategy and corresponding workplan.

You will be a key member of the team that plans and executes global MICE marketing activities to profile and drive consideration for Singapore as a top MICE destination.

Target segment analysis and understanding

Develop target segment analysis and regularly track and monitor indicators that can inform and guide global marketing strategy, and where relevant, product and experience development. The target segment understanding includes but is not limited to, analysing data sets from a breadth of sources, and/or conducting in-depth consumer research (quantitative and qualitative) on STB’s target MICE event organiser segments, to understand their demographics, psychographics, booking motivations, decision-making, needs and behaviours and the formulation of actionable insights that can inform the BTMICE marketing strategy and plans.

Development and implementation of MICE marketing activities

  • Develop and execute Board’s MICE global marketing activities across paid and owned touchpoints, ensuring the activities are grounded on target segment’s insights, coordinating with internal and external stakeholders, external agencies and vendors to ensure timely delivery and quality outcomes. The successful candidate should also be able to demonstrate the ability to conceptualise and craft engaging and effective content across digital platforms (including social media, MICE EDM, landing pages, video and written case studies) and below-the-line formats:

a. Content partnerships: Develop and execute strategic media partnerships with key MICE trade and business news media publications to create engaging branded content to drive awareness and consideration as the choice destination among MICE event organisers and attendees. You will be required to work closely with media partners in the conceptualisation and shaping of content angles/structure as well as on the ideal content formats (e.g. web, social, video) for effective delivery of our key messages. agencyDescription:

You will be working with stakeholders including data teams and partnership teams to identify opportunities for data synergies, and you will conduct data analysis to extract insights and identify areas of opportunity. Through data-driven post-implementation review and establishment of improvement plans, you will ensure continuous enhancement of our strategies to improve screening uptake at national-level.
