jobDescription:
The operating environment of the Public Service is undergoing fundamental and rapid change. The issues we face are complex and multi-faceted, which impact the way the Public Service operates and organises itself. Internally, workforce changes require a new approach to workplace design, while technology’s widespread influence has fundamentally changed the way we conduct our business.  

To prepare the Public Service for these changes, we need to transform the Public Service workplace into one that is lean, agile and digital. We also need to build a productive, collaborative and joyful workplace culture to meet the needs and aspirations of public officers. We are looking to redesign the workplace experience and create a stimulating and empowering work environment that supports officers’ growth, development and wellbeing. 

In summary, our objective is to enhance Public Service employee experience, so that we have Public Officers who are inspired, supported, and equipped for the future.
jobResponsibilities:
By joining our #PeoplePurposePossibilities internship, you can play a role in improving the workplace experience of public officers, together with partners across the Whole-of-Government (WOG). You will be part of a team that strategises and implements WOG employee experience initiatives, conducts user research to understand officer needs, and coordinates with stakeholders across agencies to collectively enhance the lived experience of public officers.  

You will have the opportunity to develop yourself in the following areas: 

Programme Development and Implementation – You will assist in implementing employee experience initiatives which may include programmes that strengthen employee well-being, workplace connections, supervisory support, or officers’ experiences at key moments in their careers and life stages. You will support project coordination, progress tracking and basic outcome measurement. This may involve helping to coordinate engagement activities, supporting employee-led networks or communities, preparing project materials, maintaining stakeholder databases, and monitoring participation and feedback. You may also contribute to the development and refinement of selected employee experience projects by conducting research, gathering user insights, supporting stakeholder engagements and helping the team test and improve potential interventions. Through this work, you will contribute to broader efforts to enable purposeful and productive work, foster a flexible, collaborative and caring workplace, and build a diverse, agile and skilled Public Service. 

Research and Insights – You will support user research activities including survey design, focus group facilitation, and basic data analysis to identify officer needs in major seasons and daily moments of their work-life. You will help distil data and insights to identify potential focus areas and contribute to evidence-based solutions. 

Stakeholder Coordination – You will assist in coordinating with public agencies and partners by preparing meeting materials, following up on action items, maintaining communication channels, and supporting cross-agency collaboration efforts. You will learn to work with diverse stakeholders while understanding their unique contexts and business needs. 

Skills You Will Develop – Through this internship, you will gain practical experience in understanding the Public Service HR ecosystem, exposure to user research methodologies, experience with cross-agency collaboration, and basic project management and coordination skills. You will also develop technical capabilities in using tech/AI tools like Copilot and ChatGPT for tasks such as data processing and analysis, process automation, summarisation of meetings and content creation.

jobDescription:

As part of STB’s Digital and Media team, you will play an instrumental role in driving STB's global paid media strategy to ensure that STB is able to reach the right target segments through the right channels effectively and efficiently. You will also support other Marketing Group units in developing activation strategies with our appointed agencies for key marketing campaigns. This has to be closely integrated with STB’s owned media channels, incorporating the use of audience data and insights, a robust experimentation approach and a holistic measurement framework, so that STB can confidently be at the forefront of destination marketing and remain agile in the face of disruptions.

a) Internal: Marketing Activation - Social team, other STB Marketing Group line units and Regional Offices

b) External: STB’s appointed agency partners (Creative and PR), global/ regional media owners and partners

Media Strategy Development

  • Develop paid media strategy aligned to STB’s business and marketing objectives across 15-20 international markets on an always-on basis. This should be supported by an analysis of market performance data and consumer media consumption behaviour.

  • The media approach should include an integrated search strategy that synergizes paid search with owned channel performance (i.e. search engine optimisation and AI search visibility/ generative engine optimisation).

Always-On Media Management & Optimization

  • Closely monitor media performance to refine targeting, channel selection and budgets throughout the year.

  • Work closely with other Marketing Group units in developing activation strategies with our appointed agencies for key marketing campaigns, ensuring synergies with STB’s always-on media plans.

Experimentation

    • Test new parameters where learnings can be scaled from a one-off experiment to always-on; and

    • Make bold choices in uncovering new ways to reach out to our target audiences through innovative channels and formats.

Measurement

  • Connect paid media efforts and integrated search back to key business outcomes, beyond isolated marketing metrics.

  • Put in place tracking and measurement infrastructure to support translation of data into learnings and actionable decisions.

Data Strategy

  • Shape STB’s marketing data strategy, including enhancements to our existing martech ecosystem and establishing a framework that allows us to harness data (across paid media, owned media, third party data partners) and the application of GenAI to derive deeper audience insights and drive data-driven marketing practices.

jobDescription:
Social media today is no longer a supporting channel — it is where culture is made, influence is built, and travel decisions are shaped. For STB, this shift represents a significant opportunity to lead in destination marketing through sharp, insight-driven social strategy that is both creative and commercially grounded.

As the Social Strategist, you will be the resident expert on social strategy within STB's social department — developing the frameworks, playbooks, and strategic direction that the wider team builds upon. This is a role for someone who thinks deeply about where social is heading, translates that thinking into clear and actionable strategy, and is equally comfortable getting hands-on to deliver. You will work across the department and with key external partners to ensure STB's social presence is coherent, forward-looking, and effective.
jobResponsibilities:
Social Strategy Development & Oversight

You will develop, review, and own the overarching social strategy that guides the department's work. This means producing the strategic frameworks and playbooks that team members plug into as they develop strategies for their respective workstreams — ensuring that individual efforts are aligned, coherent, and laddering up to a unified social vision. You will regularly review and evolve the strategy in response to performance data, platform shifts, and broader marketing objectives, serving as the strategic backbone and thought partner for the team.

Performance Measurement & Reporting

You will own the performance for the Visit Singapore (VS) social channels. Working with the in-house social media manager, you will ensure monthly performance reports on VS channels are produced consistently and on time, and that the data is translated into clear insights and recommendations. Beyond the monthly cadence, you will lead quarterly and annual reviews — analysing performance trends, identifying what is working and what needs to change, and presenting findings to relevant stakeholders.

Channel Mix & Platform Planning

A core part of your remit is ensuring STB is investing in the right platforms at the right time. You will conduct yearly reviews of the social channel mix, assessing each platform's performance, audience fit, and strategic relevance — tracking cultural, platform, and algorithm shifts and translating them into a formal set of recommendations that shape how the department allocates its resources going forward.

Emerging Platforms, Experimentation & Prospecting

You will proactively scan for emerging channels, closed communities, and new social spaces that present strategic opportunities for STB. Critically, you will not just identify these opportunities — you will lead and run the pilots, developing go-to-market approaches, executing the test, and producing a clear assessment of viability and scalability. Where a pilot proves successful, you may continue to own and manage that channel as part of your portfolio. This requires a structured yet experimental mindset — knowing how to design a meaningful test, read the results honestly, and make a clear recommendation. You will also take the lead on horizon-scanning for the social department, synthesising signals from across the industry into actionable foresight that informs both near-term strategy and longer-term planning.

Campaign Delivery

You will be involved in developing key campaigns, driving the delivery of social strategy from planning through to execution. This means working across functions to ensure that the strategic intent of a campaign is preserved through to delivery and being hands-on where needed to make it happen.

Paid Social Oversight

Working closely with the Digital and Media team, you will oversee STB's paid social strategy, ensuring that paid efforts are meaningfully integrated with organic activity and aligned to campaign objectives.
jobRequirements:
• Minimum 5 years of experience in social media strategy, with a track record of developing and owning social strategies for brand(s)

  • Strong command of the social media landscape across platforms, formats, audience behaviours, and content trends

  • Experience conducting channel mix reviews and making evidence-based recommendations on platform investment

  • Demonstrated ability to identify, assess, and run pilots on emerging platforms and social spaces — with examples of seeing a pilot through from concept to recommendation

  • Experience with paid social strategy and an understanding of how paid and organic efforts intersect

  • A genuine curiosity about where social is heading, with experience in futures thinking, trend analysis, or horizon-scanning

  • A degree in a related discipline.
  • Strategic thinking, with the ability to turn complex technical, behavioural and evidence-based information into clear, health-literate communication strategies tailored to the audience.
  • Proven programme planning and delivery skills, with the ability to lead integrated communications and engagement initiatives from concept to evaluation while managing resources, agencies and vendors.
  • Effective leadership and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to align diverse stakeholders, balance competing priorities, guide officers and deliver outcomes across multidisciplinary teams.
  • Sound analytical judgement, with the ability to interpret audience insights, research, campaign performance and other evidence to assess effectiveness and recommend improvements.

Under the HDB Internship Programme, you will be attached to the Urban Resilience Research team in HDB Building & Research Institute.

Singapore's public housing stock is one of the largest concrete building portfolios in the region — and it is ageing. Keeping more than a million homes safe, sound and comfortable for generations to come is one of HDB's defining engineering challenges. You will join the team working at the frontier of this mission: understanding why concrete deteriorates in our tropical, coastal, high-density environment, and building the diagnostic tools to stay ahead of it.

- Contributing to the development of an ageing infrastructure dashboard — consolidating, validating and analysing building condition data
- Conducting engineering data analysis and preparing summary reports, visualisations and technical documentation
- Supporting site verification and lab-based testing activities at HDB's research facilities
- Researching emerging materials and repair/retrofit technologies to support HDB's ageing infrastructure roadmap

Upon completing the internship, you will:

- Gain practical experience in concrete durability, forensic failure analysis and infrastructure condition assessment
- Develop skills in engineering data analysis, NDT interpretation, and technical reporting

jobDescription: SENIOR/ MANAGER, DATA PARTNERSHIPS — TRANSPORT AI PROGRAMME, LTA SINGAPORE
jobResponsibilities:
Singapore's land transport network moves millions of people every day. As AI reshapes what's possible in transport operations, the Land Transport Authority is investing in AI capabilities that will meaningfully improve how the network is sensed, managed, and optimised — for commuters, operators, and public officers alike.

AI systems are only as good as the data that powers them. We are looking for a Senior/ Manager to establish and lead our data acquisition and partnership function — the foundational capability that will enable our organisation to develop meaningful, operationally relevant data use cases and AI-enabled applications.

Beyond internal organisational data, operationally relevant datasets may be found across government agencies, industry partners, and contractors — each governed by their own access controls, sharing frameworks, and institutional considerations. You will be required to understand our concept of operations well enough to determine what data is needed, and pursue access to that data through establishing relationships, agreements and organisational infrastructure required to bring the right data in securely and sustainably.

What You Will Be Working On

You will lead a team to translate our concept of operations into a prioritised multi-modal data acquisition roadmap, identifying what data we need and sequencing efforts by operational value and feasibility. Your work also involves stakeholder engagement, negotiating access with government agencies, statutory boards, industries and research institutions.

As part of data acquisition, you will lead your team to define and enforce standards for how data is received — covering file formats, data schemas, metadata requirements, and update cadences. This ensures that datasets from disparate sources can be reliably ingested, integrated, and made ready for analytical and AI workloads. Where partners or contractors are unable to meet these standards natively, you will work with them to find practical solutions or manage the necessary transformation processes internally.

You will also be responsible for identifying and building the right platform for consolidating data from multiple sources, particularly where contractor or sensitive datasets introduce security and classification constraints that may rule out standard environments. You will work with technical, legal, and cybersecurity colleagues to arrive at an appropriate approach.

Underpinning all of this is sound data governance — ensuring that what we acquire is handled compliantly, with appropriate agreements and access controls in place. You will work closely with analytical, AI development and product teams to ensure that acquired data is properly onboarded and ready for use case development.
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge in Computer Science, Infocomm Technology, Engineering, or a related field, with at least 8 years of relevant experience including 3 or more years in a leadership capacity. Experience in data governance, inter-agency coordination, or data strategy is strongly preferred.

  • Prior public service experience or experience working closely with government agencies, government data security and classification frameworks will be a significant advantage.

  • You should bring demonstrated experience in negotiating data access or managing data sharing arrangements in a government or operationally complex environment.

  • Experience building or leading a team of data scientists and engineers to deliver data pipeline, warehouse and data sharing capabilities.

  • Experience in working in cross-functional teams and collaborating with both technical and non-technical stakeholders to translate operational data needs into a prioritised data strategy.

jobResponsibilities:

You will contribute to areas including questionnaire design, data processing, academic collaboration, and data science initiatives to support evidence-based policymaking.

You will undertake the full data quality assurance pipeline — developing validation rules, managing data imputation, and integrating administrative and survey data using tools such as Stata and Python. You will also review and improve the RHS questionnaire from a data quality perspective, ensuring it remains robust, relevant, and well-suited for longitudinal analysis.

Beyond data operations, you will manage academic collaborations with local universities and government agencies, assessing research proposals and reviewing drafts to ensure alignment with data governance requirements and policy objectives. You will also undertake data science and digital initiatives, including building models and automation tools to improve data quality and respondent engagement.

•	Collaborate with cross-functional teams, survey companies, academic institutions, and government agencies to coordinate study planning and execution, and facilitate seamless data sharing as part of these collaborative efforts.
•	Contribute to data science projects aimed at enhancing data quality or supporting the execution of the study.

Working at METI places you at the heart of Singapore’s economic policy-making. We drive productivity-led growth, safeguard and expand our economic space, and build a future-ready economy where firms can thrive. Together, we create a Singapore which is a city of possibilities, a home to great firms, and a place where the world connects — with people at its heart.

When you join METI, you contribute to our mission of creating good jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans, enabling them to improve their lives and secure a better future.
jobDescription:
The Corporate Planning team (CP) is part of METI’s Futures and Planning Division (FPD), which oversees the end-to-end value chain of strategic planning activities within METI and across Government for the economy, with a focus of advancing Singapore’s economic strategies. 

As METI’s de facto “CEO’s Office”, the CP team works closely with senior management to translate strategy intent into action and to steward our resources effectively.  The team plays a central role in driving organisation-wide alignment, ensuring sound governance and enabling the delivery of METI’s Strategic Priorities. 

Key areas of responsibility include:
(i)	Leading corporate planning for the METI family, including the annual work planning process and the planning and management of senior leadership platforms, to promote strategic alignment and coherence across the organisation 
(ii)	Driving strategic resource management for the METI family, including supporting the prioritisation and allocation of budget and manpower resources to key economic projects, in alignment with METI’s Vision and Mission.
(iii)	Strengthening systems governance (i.e. target setting, performance monitoring and progress assurance) within METI and across the Firefly Family, to ensure that strategic objectives are translated into tangible and impactful results.
(iv)	Overseeing Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) within METI.
jobResponsibilities:
The officer will undertake the following key responsibilities: 

•	Design, organise and run robust planning processes across the METI Firefly Family to identify our Strategic Priorities, foster organisation-wide alignment, and ensure disciplined follow through with well-defined implementation plans, including guiding divisions in the formulation of their respective work plans.

•	Drive the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) process within METI to proactively anticipate challenges and support informed decision making.
•	Support the development of agendas and organising frameworks for METI-Exco and senior management meetings and coordinate the implementation of agreed strategies across clusters.
•	Design and implement strategic resource allocation frameworks, principles and tools (e.g. resourcing principles, benchmarks, reporting and evaluation mechanisms), to support the prudent and strategic allocation of budget and manpower resources across the METI family. 
•	Work closely with stakeholders to understand resource requirements and priorities, balance competing demands, and uplift resource management capabilities within METI and the Firefly Family (e.g. conducting robust Cost-Benefit-Analysis).
•	Support the work of key Ministerial-level economic strategy decision making platforms and related work-streams.

You should consider applying for this role if you:

•	Are keen to gain a high-level, whole-of-government perspective on Singapore’s economic goals and challenges, and to understand the strategic, policy and resourcing trade-offs underlying key economic decisions.
•	Are interested in broad-based exposure to core competencies such as corporate planning, strategic resource management, and stakeholder management and engagement.
jobRequirements:
You should possess the following attributes and capabilities:
•	A strong interest in Singapore’s economy and economic strategies.
•	Relevant experience in corporate planning or resource management will be an advantage.
•	Strong analytical skills and ability to deal with complexity and ambiguity.
•	A strong learning orientation including intellectual curiosity, comfort with developing and refining new ideas, and a desire to improve processes and outcomes. 
•	Excellent stakeholder management, communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to navigate diverse and sometimes competing stakeholder interests 
•	Proficiency in Excel is preferred, experience in data analysis or reporting tools would be an added advantage.

agencyDescription:
The Civil Service College (CSC) is a statutory board under the Public Service Division, Prime Minister’s Office. We are the central learning institution for the Singapore Public Service and we partner government ministries and agencies to develop people for a first-class public service.

CSC brings together public officers from diverse backgrounds and provides them with opportunities for learning and skills upgrading. Our service-wide networks enable public officers to build capabilities, develop shared ethos and gain deeper perspectives, creating a collaborative environment for dialogue and knowledge sharing.

Through our programmes and services, CSC aims to strengthen strategic capacity in governance, leadership, public administration and management for the Singapore Public Service.
jobDescription:
The Finance Planning and Reporting function supports Civil Service College (CSC)’s financial governance, reporting, and resource planning to ensure sound financial stewardship and informed decision-making. The team works closely with departments and senior management to provide timely financial insights, ensure regulatory compliance, and strengthen financial management practices across the organisation.

This role plays a key part in delivering accurate financial reporting, coordinating budgeting and forecasting processes, and providing advisory support to stakeholders. By combining accounting expertise with data analytics, the role contributes to enhancing financial transparency, enabling data-driven decisions, and driving continuous improvement in finance processes.
jobResponsibilities:
What you will be working on:
• Prepare monthly and quarterly financial reports, including variance analysis and commentary, to provide senior management with clear insights on financial performance, trends and key risks
• Coordinate the annual external audit process, including preparing statutory financial statements, audit schedules, and liaising with auditors to ensure timely and accurate completion
• Lead the annual budget and forecasting exercise, including consolidation and review of departmental submissions, and provide analysis to support management decision-making
• Prepare and submit quarterly GST returns, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements and accuracy of underlying data
• Partner departments and finance coordinators by providing financial advisory and guidance, including interpreting financial data, recommending improvements and supporting adherence to financial policies
• Analyse financial data using Excel and data visualisation tools (e.g. Power BI, Tableau) to enhance reporting, strengthen insights, and support data-driven decision-making
• Drive process improvements and optimisation of finance workflows, including streamlining reporting procedures and leveraging digital tools to improve efficiency and control
jobRequirements:
What we are looking for:

We are looking for a finance professional with strong analytical capabilities and a solid foundation in financial reporting and planning. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, able to work independently, and confident in engaging stakeholders to deliver meaningful financial insights. A proactive mindset, combined with a commitment to accuracy, governance and continuous improvement, will be critical to success in this role.


[Key Competencies Required]

1. Financial Reporting
Proficiency in preparing and analysing financial statements and reports in accordance with relevant standards, ensuring accuracy, completeness and reliability of financial information. Maintains a strong focus on data integrity and audit readiness.

2. Budget Planning and Administration 
Demonstrates structured thinking in coordinating budgeting and forecasting processes, including consolidation, review and critical evaluation of financial projections. Ensures alignment between financial plans and organisational priorities.

3. Data Analytics and Visualisation
Applies analytical techniques to interpret datasets, derive insights and present information clearly using data visualisation tools to support informed decision-making.

4. Business Partnering 
Collaborates effectively with stakeholders across departments to understand business needs and provide relevant, value-adding financial advice. Communicates complex financial information in a clear and accessible manner.

5. Thinking Clearly and Making Sound Judgements
Exercises sound judgement by evaluating information critically, considering different perspectives and making well-reasoned, evidence-based decisions in complex situations.

Other traits:
• Strong attention to detail and accuracy, with a commitment to maintaining high standards of financial integrity and compliance
• Self-motivated and proactive, able to take ownership of deliverables and work independently in a dynamic environment
• Curious and analytical mindset, with a willingness to question assumptions and continuously improve processes
• Effective communicator, able to present complex financial information in a clear and concise manner to both finance and non-finance stakeholders
• Collaborative team player, with the ability to build strong working relationships across departments
• Adaptable and resilient, able to manage multiple priorities and respond to evolving organisational needs

[What you can expect]
• Growth Opportunities: We champion continuous learning - not just for the public service, but for our officers as well. We actively support our officers’ career growth through:
• Scholarship and sponsorship opportunities for higher education.
• Diverse development opportunities for officers at every career stage.
• Attachment programmes, cross-functional job rotations and gig projects.
• Coaching programmes and leadership development initiatives.
• Work Environment: We provide meaningful work, practise mutual respect and encourage innovation.
• Hybrid & Flexible Work Arrangements: We provide hybrid and flexible work arrangements to support our officers’ work-life needs. We trust that our people will deliver their best, and we strive to provide the support and flexibility they need.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. The appointment grade and actual job title will be commensurate with the candidate’s work experience.

agency: Ministry Of Social And Family Development
agencyDescription:
Join Us at MSF for a Meaningful, People-Centric Career!

At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. We offer meaningful and impactful people-centric careers in the design and delivery of policies, services and programmes. We are an all-inclusive and family friendly workplace where career growth is prioritised through a comprehensive suite of development opportunities to help our officers succeed today as well as be future-ready. We do this through various formal and informal learning and development programmes for officers to build different competencies and gain diverse work experiences within MSF, the Public as well as the Social Service Sectors.
jobDescription: The Customer Experience Division (CXD) plays a vital role in the Ministry of Social and Family Development’s mission by ensuring a positive and consistent service experience for our customers. Our team drives customer experience (CX) initiatives, fosters a strong service culture, and ensures that the quality of services delivered across all channels meets high standards.
jobResponsibilities:
We are looking for a dynamic and independent officer to elevate our customers’ experience and make a difference in the lives of the people we serve. In the Planning and Development team, you will develop end-to-end service policies, using customer and operational insights to identify service issues, and drive evidence-based service improvements across MSF. Depending on the officer’s experience, the officer will support or lead the following areas, working under the guidance of a Team Lead. This includes (a) driving customer experience strategy and service policy; (b) building and applying service intelligence through data and insights; (c) driving service transformation priorities; and (d) providing enterprise service governance. 

Responsibilities

In this role, you will:

Drive customer experience strategy and service policy
•	Develop and review enterprise CX policies, plans and strategies that advance MSF's service goals and lift the customer experience consistently across touchpoints and channels 
•	Translate MSF’s service direction and priorities into implementation plans and initiatives that strengthen service practices and outcomes across divisions 

Build and apply service intelligence through data and insights
•	Plan and implement the annual Voice of Customer (VoC) / customer satisfaction study end-to-end — methodology and questionnaire design, stakeholder engagement, vendor procurement and management, and fieldwork — to produce reliable enterprise level insights on service performance.
•	Integrate customer and operational insights from multiple sources (VoC, Global Services Benchmarking, Contact Centre reports, emails and calls) to diagnose systemic service issues, shape policy and service-development priorities and recommend practical improvements to close service gaps.
•	Develop and review policy parameters to facilitate building of service intelligence, including the comprehensive capture of public-facing correspondence across MSF

Enable service transformation 
•	Develop and support the adoption of enterprise service rules and guardrails to assure service quality, including user service development-stress testing to surface and mitigate service risks and blind spots before launch
•	Partner Operational Groups and stakeholders to map customer journeys, prioritise high-impact journeys for review, and pilot new service models that improve outcomes at enterprise scale. 
Provide enterprise service governance
•	Support the Customer Experience Steering Committee, whose mandate is to provide enterprise leadership, governance and oversight on service experience and performance matters, to enable consistent and citizen-centric service outcomes across MSF.
jobRequirements:
To succeed in this role, you should possess:

a.	At least 1 year of relevant experience. Candidates considered for more senior designations should have commensurately deeper experience in leading complex projects, policy development, research or stakeholder engagement. 
b.	Strong analytical and sensemaking skills, with the ability to synthesise quantitative and qualitative findings into actionable recommendations.
c.	Strong thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify systemic causes and surface service delivery issues.
d.	Ability to engage stakeholders effectively, facilitate collaboration and build alignment.
e.	Strong written and spoken communication skills, with the ability to present insights clearly.
f.	Experience in customer research and satisfaction studies and survey design would be an advantage.
g.	Familiarity with data analytics, dashboarding and visualisation tools would be an advantage.

Join us in making a meaningful impact on the lives of our customers and helping to build a better Singapore. Apply now to join our CXD team and help us shape the future of service delivery at MSF!

agencyDescription:
The Singapore Department of Statistics is the National Statistical Authority responsible for statistics on the Singapore economy and population.

We collect, compile, analyse and disseminate a wide range of economic, business, household and population data, as well as analyse and monitor trends in the economy and population.

With these vital inputs, policymakers, business decision makers and our data users gain valuable insights into current and emerging economic and social trends, enabling them to make calculated and informed decisions in the formulation of policies and strategies for the future. Apart from public agencies and businesses, our users also include researchers, analysts, educators, students, the media and the general public.

Join our team and make a difference by contributing important statistical input to facilitate policy planning and decision-making and support Singapore's present and future economic and social development.
jobDescription:
Redesigning the Statistical Imputation Process for Industry Statistics

Attached to the Business Statistics Division, you will contribute to the redesign of the statistical imputation process for industry statistics of the services sector. This project aims to enhance the robustness, flexibility, and scalability of the imputation framework by leveraging administrative data and the latest statistical methodologies.
jobResponsibilities:
- Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team to understand business and technical requirements for the statistical imputation process, with a particular focus on integrating administrative data to improve the estimation of detailed data items.
- Design and develop a modular and scalable imputation framework that is adaptable to new data sources, evolving data structures and business needs, ensuring long-term maintainability and extensibility.
jobRequirements:
- Knowledge or experience in data science, data analytics, statistical analysis, or computer science.
- Proficiency in Python is essential. Experience with data manipulation, database management, and statistical or data science libraries (e.g. pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn) will be an advantage.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Meticulous, organised, and detail-oriented, with the ability to work effectively with large, complex datasets.
- Self-motivated and able to work independently, with good time management skills to deliver quality outcomes within established project timelines.

Internship Period: 6 months, from Jan to Jun 2027 (flexible start and end dates)

agencyDescription: The Military Security Department (MSD)’s core business is in Counter Intelligence and internal security for MINDEF/SAF.  MSD was formed in 1975 to counter the threats of espionage, subversion and sabotage against MINDEF/SAF. It began with two main entities, namely the Counter Intelligence Branch (CIB) and Field Security Branch (FSB).  Over the years, the department has continued to evolve and our roles expanded in tandem with the changing security environment. Today, our roles also include Counter Terrorism and Cyber Security.
jobDescription: You will lead a small team to drive digitalization in protective security with a focus in physical security. You plan, design and implement the digitalization roadmaps as well as sustain and refresh the technology and introduce technology advancements for continuous improvement in the digitalized systems.
jobResponsibilities: You will be the architect for physical security systems and solutions, and partnering with MINDEF/SAF to formulate a digitalization roadmap for physical security, secure funding and garner organizational support for the roadmap. You will lead your team to  develop and/or procure digital tools and solutions to implement the roadmap. You will keep watch of technology advancement to continuously develop and evolve the roadmap into the future. You will also implement digitalization for protective security, automate work flow and leverage data analytics and AI for proactive protective risk management.
jobRequirements: Past military leadership experience or ex-Government officer with experience in capability development. You should have demonstrated a history of partnering data engineers/business owners to develop and scale business analytics projects. You should display strong ability in managing data and AI projects.

agencyDescription:
The Internal Security Department (ISD) confronts and addresses threats to Singapore’s internal security and stability. For over 75 years, ISD and its predecessor organisations have played a central role in countering threats such as those posed by foreign subversive elements, spies, racial and religious extremists, and terrorists.

agencyDescription:
The Ministry of National Development (MND), the lead government agency responsible for land use planning and infrastructure development, aims to transform Singapore into an endearing home and a distinctive global city. At MND, we aspire to create a quality, vibrant and sustainable living environment for our people. We also strive to shape Singapore into a world-class city of knowledge, culture and excellence – one which keeps pace with global challenges and the rising aspirations of Singaporeans.

Our Vision:

An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City
MND's vision reflects our growing emphasis not just on physical infrastructure, but also on the softer aspects of creating emotional attachment in our people, the global talents and corporations whom we attract here. At the same time, it articulates MND's goal of building upon Singapore’s unique distinguishing characteristics to develop Singapore as a global city of knowledge, culture and excellence.


Our Mission:

Develop World-Class Infrastructure
MND will provide quality physical infrastructure for the nation by working with our partners in the public and private sectors.

Create a Vibrant, Resilient and Sustainable Living Environment
MND will strive to make Singapore a livelier and more exciting city, and ensure our nation is well-prepared to face the growing uncertainties and complexities. MND will also maintain the quality and resilience of our built and natural environment to ensure high standards of living, and carry out development that meets the needs of the present without compromising that of future generations.

Provide Affordable and Accessible Public Housing
MND will commit to support Singaporeans' homeownership aspirations and ensure public housing remains affordable and accessible.

Build Rooted and Cohesive Communities
MND will strive to foster our citizens' attachment and love for our homeland and maintain social cohesiveness in our communities, even as Singapore continues to be an open and globalised society.
jobDescription: In this role, you will have the opportunity to make a meaningful difference to Singapore's greenery enhancement and conservation policies as we transform the nation into a City in Nature.
jobResponsibilities:
You will work with the National Parks Board (NParks) to refresh the longer-term strategic direction for the Landscape and Orchid sectors. This includes reviewing land and procurement policies for nursery farms to encourage better land utilisation, reviewing technology adoption funding scheme to uplift productivity, and reviewing the manpower development plan to nurture talent and ensure sufficient workforce capacity.

You will also work with Gardens by the Bay (GB), a premier urban outdoor recreation space and top tourist attraction, to co-develop infrastructure plans beyond the Bay East Garden and Wetland by the Bay.

To achieve these outcomes, you will drive and coordinate policy and operations matters and co-develop proposals with NParks and GB. You will work with both organisations to monitor and safeguard their operational and financial standing. You will also staff and coordinate meetings on these issues involving MND senior management and other relevant stakeholders.

•	Able to sense-make root causes / drivers and identify key trade-offs, considerations, and options for simple policy issues
•	Able to write in a clear, concise, and organised manner for all types of policy documents, and tailor writing for different target audience and platforms

•	A sense of initiative and dynamism

jobDescription: Reporting to Assistant Director of Internal Audit, the Manager / Senior Manager of Internal Audit plays a key role in providing independent and objective assurance to strengthen governance, risk management, and internal controls within the organisation. You will work across LTA's rich transport data ecosystem — spanning real-time sensor feeds, transit operations data, traffic systems, and road infrastructure — to ensure that data is reliably ingested, transformed, governed, and made available for AI development and production use.

  • Implement data governance practices in line with Singapore Government data classification requirements, including access controls, data masking, anonymisation, and audit logging for sensitive transport and personal data.

  • Work with the AI Architect and Infrastructure Engineer to design data infrastructure that is performant, cost-efficient, and aligned with LTA's cloud and hybrid environment.

  • Collaborate with data scientists and AI developers to understand data requirements for model development, and translate these into reliable, production-grade data products.

  • Support the integration of external data sources from industry partners, ensuring that data exchange meets LTA's standards for security, quality, and interoperability.

You will be part of the Risk Assurance Division within IMDA’s Resilience and Cybersecurity Group. The Holistic Assessment team in this Division assesses the overall cybersecurity risk posture of critical digital networks and systems and the cyber capabilities of organisations operating these networks.

This includes integrating diverse sources of information, across the organisation’s external environment, its internal capabilities and the performance of its networks and systems. The team adopts an evidence-based approach to develop an objective assessment of the organisation and network’s key strengths and vulnerabilities. It also recommends key areas that senior management should track to uplift its cybersecurity risk posture.

The Holistic Assessment team works with teams across IMDA’s Resilience and Cybersecurity Group, and in partnership with industry stakeholders. Through these, the Holistic Assessment team plays a critical role in ensuring that the critical digital networks and systems which underpin Singapore’s Digital Economy remain secure and resilient.

  • Conduct research and sense making of the evolving cybersecurity landscape in relation to Singapore’s digital infrastructure. This includes integrating threat intelligence information as well as international industry best practices for defending against current and emerging cyber threats.

Responsibilities

[Public Service Commission Secretariat]
The Public Service Commission (PSC) was constituted in 1951 as an independent organ of state to appoint, promote, transfer, dismiss and exercise disciplinary control over public officers. The PSC Secretariat provides support to the PSC. This includes formulating conduct and discipline policies, to ensure that officers maintain the highest standards of personal conduct and integrity. One significant non-statutory role of the PSC is the award of PSC scholarships for undergraduate and postgraduate studies. Under the Talent Management arm of the team, we formulate scholarship policies and oversee talent attraction and development of PSC scholarship holders as potential future leaders in the Public Service.

[Specific Job Responsibilities]
Reporting to the Assistant Director (Talent Management), you will be part of the team supporting and facilitating the PSC’s work in developing top-tier talent through PSC scholarships and maintaining oversight of scholarships throughout the Public Service. The role has a strong focus on scholarship and talent management policy, analysis, programme oversight and cross-agency implementation, while supporting selected talent development and outreach initiatives where relevant.

Strategic Planning & Policy
•	Contribute to the formulation, review and implementation of scholarship and talent management policies and frameworks, taking into account Public Service talent needs, implementation considerations and developments in the education and talent landscape.
•	Conduct research, environmental scanning and benchmarking on relevant education, workforce and talent trends, and translate findings into practical policy options and programme enhancements.
•	Support strategic projects and reviews involving PSC scholarship pipelines, scholarship terms and conditions, talent attraction, scholar development and related governance matters.
•	Prepare policy papers, management reports, briefing materials, data analyses and presentations for PSC members, senior management and inter-agency stakeholders.
•	Monitor key scholarship and talent management indicators, respond to emerging data and information requests, and generate insights to support planning and policy decisions.
•	Translate approved policy changes into implementable processes, guidance and communications, and work with stakeholders to support consistent implementation across agencies.

Stakeholder Management & Partnerships
•	Share information and best practices in scholarship policy, talent management and programme administration with Public Service agencies.
•	Partner Public Service agencies to understand emerging talent and capability needs, assess proposals relating to scholarship and talent schemes, and translate these into policy or programme considerations.
•	Provide advice and guidance to agencies on scholarship policy, administration and implementation, including new or revised scholarship arrangements and cross-agency issues.
•	Contribute to inter-agency workgroups and projects relating to scholarships, talent management and workforce development, and facilitate discussions to gather perspectives and build alignment on policy and operational matters.
•	Support the review, governance or transition of selected scholarship and award programmes, including policy and administrative arrangements and handover to partner organisations, where applicable.

Outreach & Engagement
•	Support the review and implementation of scholarship outreach and talent attraction strategies and initiatives.
•	Engage local and overseas tertiary institutions and relevant partners where this supports environmental scanning, policy development or talent attraction objectives.
•	Support key scholarship events and developmental milestone programmes, where relevant.

We are looking for self-motivated individuals who value integrity, teamwork and take pride in going the extra mile to provide excellent service.

•	[Talent Management and Policy] A good understanding of talent management and scholarship issues. Able to support policy reviews and translate strategic objectives into practical policies, programmes and implementation plans.

jobDescription:
Are you ready to build next-generation, sustainable cold chain logistics for life-saving biopharmaceuticals?

Republic Polytechnic's School of Engineering (SEG), in strategic partnership with industry leader SSW Group, is seeking an ambitious full-time Research Staff (12-month contract) to engineer an industrial-scale 1"m" ^3 self-sustained passive cold storage platform under a DGF-funded initiative.

Current biopharmaceutical distribution relies on massive active energy inputs and heavy daily coolant consumption. This project completely disrupts that model by building a zero-power-in-transit, high-performance thermal container (1"m"×1"m"×1"m" ) capable of locking in sub-zero temperatures (2–8°C) for over 72 continuous hours in harsh tropical environments.

Beyond standard transport, this passive design provides critical fail-safe protection against warehouse power outages and opens up new pathways for long-haul air and sea freight to distant international markets without relying on active electrical refrigeration networks.

You will lead the hands-on engineering across two breakthrough technological pillars:
- Active-Passive "Flash-Charging" Cryogenic System: A rapid-charging base station interface utilizing specialized heat exchangers and Liquid Nitrogen (LN_2) bursts to charge high-density Phase Change Material (PCM) cores and Vacuum Insulated Panels (VIP).
- Triple-Vector IoT Telemetry Engine: An ultra-low-power, cloud-connected sensor matrix tracking real-time Temperature, Relative Humidity, and Oxygen (O_2) levels to ensure absolute data transparency and regulatory compliance (HSA/FDA standards).

The successful candidate will contribute to prototype development, laboratory research, system integration, cold box temperature analysis, field validation at mimic cold storage environment, and technology commercialisation.
jobResponsibilities:
- Perform 3D CAD modelling, understand basic fluid dynamics, and heat exchanger design to eliminate thermal dead zones and maximize LN_2 thermodynamic efficiency across a 1"m" ^3 volume.
- Design, route, and balance high-pressure LN_2 cryogenic pipelines, vacuum-jacketed tubings, manifolds, and automated valve safety systems.
- Build IOT, test, and integrate low-power microcontrollers and sensor arrays (Temp,RH,O_2) with live, cloud-based telemetry dashboards.
- Perform laboratory experiments, cold storage environment trials, temperature and humidity monitoring, passive cold storage box testing, and data analysis.
- Develop, integrate, and evaluate prototype systems, sensors, and instrumentation.
- Collaborate with industry partners to support technology validation and deployment.
- Supervise final-year project students and interns involved in the project.
- Support intellectual property (IP) development, technology transfer, and commercialisation activities.
- Prepare technical reports, journal publications, presentations, and research grant proposals.
- Manage laboratory equipment & consumables, procurement, safety compliance, and research products.
jobRequirements:
- Qualification in Mechanical Engineering, Thermal/Fluid Engineering, Mechatronics, Electrical & Electronic Engineering, Systems Engineering, Materials Science, or a related discipline.
- Have basic foundational understanding of thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, heat transfer, or cold-chain storage technologies.
- Proficiency in 3D CAD modelling (Autodesk Fusion 360 or SolidWorks) and Design for Manufacturing (DFM) principles.
- Practical skills in embedded electronics, microcontroller programming (Arduino / ESP32), and IoT sensor integration.
- Experience or have interest in cryogenic fluids (LN_2), heat exchangers, or fluid pipeline design is a major advantage.
- A hands-on, proactive mindset with the drive to build physical prototypes and lead projects independently in a dynamic lab environment.
- Strong technical writing and data presentation skills.

jobResponsibilities:
As a Security Consultant in our Cybersecurity Governance & Assurance team, you will play an important role in safeguarding the systems and information that millions of CPF members rely on for their retirement, healthcare and housing needs.

You will contribute to strengthening CPF Board’s cybersecurity governance, risk management and assurance capabilities, helping to ensure that cybersecurity risks are effectively identified, assessed and managed. Working with stakeholders across the organisation, you will provide cybersecurity advice, conduct security assessments and assurance activities, and support the continuous improvement of the Board’s cybersecurity posture and resilience.

In this role, you will:

• Conduct cybersecurity risk assessments and security assurance activities across systems, applications, infrastructure, cloud environments and technology initiatives to identify security risks, vulnerabilities and control gaps, assess the adequacy and effectiveness of cybersecurity controls and recommend appropriate risk treatment and remediation measures.
• Provide cybersecurity risk and assurance advice to system owners, project teams and other stakeholders, translating findings into practical recommendations and supporting the implementation of appropriate security controls and mitigation measures.
• Assess cybersecurity risks arising from new and emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Generative AI (GenAI), as well as new solutions and changes to existing systems across application, infrastructure, network, cloud and security architecture, and contribute to the development of appropriate security, risk management and assurance measures to strengthen resilience and support secure adoption.
• Plan, coordinate and conduct penetration testing and security testing of applications, infrastructure, networks, cloud environments and other technology solutions, working with relevant stakeholders and external security testing providers, where appropriate, to address relevant cybersecurity risks and attack scenarios, identify vulnerabilities and validate the effectiveness of security controls.
• Analyse and validate penetration testing findings, assess their exploitability and cybersecurity risk, perform or coordinate retesting and validation to ensure identified security vulnerabilities are adequately addressed.
• Leverage penetration testing results together with vulnerability assessments, threat intelligence, External Attack Surface Management (EASM), Adversarial Exposure Validation (AEV) and other technical security assessments to identify systemic security weaknesses and strengthen cybersecurity assurance.
• Explore the use of scripting, automation and data analytics, including Python where appropriate, to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of cybersecurity risk assessment, assurance, monitoring and reporting activities.
• Support and participate in internal and external cybersecurity audits, reviews and regulatory assessments, including the coordination, assessment and remediation of findings.
• Assess compliance with applicable cybersecurity policies, standards, regulatory requirements and industry frameworks, and recommend improvements where necessary.
• Develop, review and enhance cybersecurity policies, standards, procedures and governance frameworks to address evolving cybersecurity risks, regulatory requirements, emerging technologies and organisational needs.
• Contribute to the continuous improvement of cybersecurity governance, risk and assurance methodologies, processes, tools and capabilities, including the adoption of threat-informed and risk-based approaches.
jobRequirements:
We value the diverse talents and experiences that each individual brings to the table. While mastery of every requirement may not be necessary, familiarity and expertise in some of the following areas will position you for success within this team.

Cybersecurity Governance & Assurance

• Relevant experience in cybersecurity, information security, technology risk, security assurance, cybersecurity governance or related areas.
• Experience in conducting cybersecurity risk assessments, security reviews, control assessments and/or other security assurance activities, and recommending appropriate risk treatment and remediation measures.
• Good understanding of cybersecurity risks, threats, vulnerabilities and security controls, with the ability to assess how these may affect systems, applications, infrastructure, network, security architecture and technology environments.
• Ability to assess cybersecurity issues and translate technical findings, vulnerabilities and control weaknesses into clear risk implications and practical recommendations.
• Familiarity with relevant cybersecurity standards, frameworks and regulatory requirements, such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO/IEC 27001, CIS Controls, Singapore Government Instruction Manuals, and applicable cybersecurity legislation, Codes of Practice and regulatory requirements.
• Good analytical, problem-solving and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to evaluate cybersecurity risks and controls in the context of business, technology and operational requirements, and communicate cybersecurity risks and recommendations effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
• Adaptable, inquisitive and keen to broaden cybersecurity expertise through exposure to different areas of cybersecurity risk, assurance, governance and emerging technologies.
• Awareness of emerging cybersecurity threats and technologies, including developments relating to Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Generative AI (GenAI), and an interest in understanding their cybersecurity risks and implications.

Penetration Testing & Security Assessment

• Experience or knowledge in penetration testing, vulnerability assessment or security testing, including the identification, validation and assessment of security vulnerabilities.
• Good understanding of common application, infrastructure, network and cloud security vulnerabilities, attack techniques and security controls, including familiarity with frameworks and references such as the OWASP Top 10, OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (WSTG), MITRE ATT&CK and CVSS.
• Familiarity with penetration testing methodologies and commonly used security testing tools, such as Burp Suite, Nmap, vulnerability scanners and other relevant security assessment tools.
• Ability to analyse penetration testing and vulnerability assessment findings, assess their exploitability, potential impact and cybersecurity risk, and translate technical findings into practical remediation recommendations.
• Ability to document and communicate security testing findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders and work with system owners and technical teams to address identified vulnerabilities.

Experience or knowledge in one or more of the following areas would be an advantage:

• Hands-on experience conducting web application, API, mobile application, infrastructure, network, Active Directory or cloud penetration testing.
• Experience in Red Teaming, Purple Teaming, adversarial security testing or threat-informed security assessments, including the use of realistic attack scenarios to evaluate security controls.
• Experience with External Attack Surface Management (EASM), Adversarial Exposure Validation (AEV), breach and attack simulation or continuous security validation approaches.
• Experience analysing and validating complex vulnerabilities, attack paths and chained security weaknesses beyond automated vulnerability scanning.
• Knowledge of scripting or programming languages such as Python, PowerShell or other relevant languages for security testing, data analysis or automation.
• Relevant offensive security or penetration-testing certifications, such as OSCP, OSWA, OSWE, CREST certifications, GPEN, or equivalent professional certifications.
• Relevant cybersecurity such as CISSP, CCSP, CISM, CRISC, CISA, ISO/IEC 27001, or equivalent certifications, would be advantageous.

The seniority of appointment and actual corporate job title will commensurate with individual work experiences.

Position is on a 2-year full-time contract directly under the payroll of CPF Board with potential for emplacement into a permanent position.

jobDescription:

- Improving the housing market news and sentiment analytics application, including its data processing, retrieval and analytical capabilities.
- Exploring more autonomous AI agents that can plan, execute and validate analyses with human oversight.
- Developing an offline conversational analytics solution using open-weight language models.

These projects build on RSM’s existing conversational data-analysis prototypes and planned integration, orchestration and autonomous-analysis workstreams.

- Good foundation in Python, SQL, data processing and statistical analysis.

jobTitle: Senior/Manager, Healthy Food & Dining (2 years contract)
agencyDescription:
Established in 2001, the Health Promotion Board’s (HPB) vision is to build a nation of healthy people.

We aim to empower residents in Singapore to attain optimal health, increase the quality and years of healthy life, and prevent illnesses, disability and premature death.

To achieve this, HPB drives national health promotion and disease prevention programmes, spearheads health education initiatives and creates a supportive environment in Singapore where healthy lifestyle options are available and accessible for healthy living every day.
jobDescription: You will join the HPB’s Healthy Food & Dining (HFD) Division, which strives to design, develop, and implement various innovative programmes to influence Singaporeans to choose healthier food and drink options. You will work with various food partners to make available healthier options more pervasive and accessible. HPB aims to create a supportive environment through health promotion programmes such as the Healthier Ingredients Development Scheme (HIDS), Healthier Choice Symbol (HCS), Healthier Dining Programme (HDP), and Healthier Meals in School Programme (HMSP). Additionally, HFD aims to influence Singaporeans to adopt healthier eating habits through public education campaigns and promotions, and engagements via offline and online channels, such as the Eat Drink Shop Healthy Challenge.
jobResponsibilities:
As part of Healthy Food & Dining Division, you will drive strategic initiatives to increase the supply, adoption and market reach of healthier ingredients and products to support the food eco-system. Reporting to the Assistant Director, your scope includes

  • Analysing industry and market trends, business performance and programme data to identify growth opportunities, priority segments and strategic partners, and recommending where and how to intervene to accelerate adoption and capture greater market share for healthier offerings.
  • Translating market and business insights into actionable strategies and initiatives, using grants, partnerships and other business levers to achieve win-win industry and public health outcomes.
  • Developing and cultivating strategic relationships with key industry players, identifying and pursuing business development and collaboration opportunities, and developing partnership operating models and value propositions that encourage industry participation and adoption. This includes understanding business needs and barriers and working closely with partners to translate opportunities into concrete initiatives, including healthier product development, adoption and demand-generation efforts.
  • Developing and continuously improve the grants and other interventions to ensure their relevance and effectiveness in meeting industry and programme objectives. Handle end-to-end grant administration, including reviewing grant applications, maintaining up to date grant guide, managing application and approval cycles, presenting to evaluation and approval committee, and overseeing grant awards, governance, compliance and audit, budget forecast and utilization, tracking key performance indicators and regular progress reporting to management. Will need to work closely with the team on grant administration and operational matters, providing guidance and coaching to ensure timely and accurate delivery.
jobRequirements:
Join us if you are a dynamic team player and are enthusiastic to work with other team members and be comfortable working in a matrixed team and fast-changing environment. You should possess strong strategic, analytical, business development, stakeholder management, and project management skills. You are expected to work with members of the Healthy Food and Dining team as well as other teams within HPB on programs, partnerships & initiatives.

You should also possess the followings:

  • Strong business and analytical acumen, with experience analysing market trends, business and programme performance, and data to identify growth opportunities, priority segments and partners, and translate insights into actionable recommendations. Possess excellent interpersonal & relationship building skills to cultivate partnerships and engage effectively with stakeholders at all levels
  • At least 5 years of related experience, preferably in business development, strategic partnership management, strategy/ business planning, F&B industry development, programme management and/or government grant management. Relevant qualifications in a related discipline (e.g. Business Administration, Food & Nutrition, Food Science & Technology) or any health-related discipline/relevant experience will be an added advantage.
  • A good understanding of and interest in the local F&B industry and supply chain, with the ability to understand commercial interests and identify drivers of business adoption.
  • Strong judgement and critical reasoning skills, with the ability to navigate ambiguity, balance business and public health considerations, and make sound decisions using data and market insights.
  • Good quantitative and financial management skills including developing and monitoring budgets, assessing programme or business performance, tracking performance and outcomes, and applying insights to support decision-making.

Successful candidates will be offered a 2-year contract.

jobDescription:
Join a team reimagining the future of our digital services. We are transforming OneMotoring into an intelligent Digital Shopfront that makes every interaction simpler, faster, and more delightful. Powered by AI, it will thoughtfully augment how digital services are designed, delivered and experienced, creating the next-generation platform that keeps your world moving.

As Manager, User Experience, you will shape a platform that citizens and staff use every day. You will turn complex services into elegant, intuitive journeys, lead the research that proves they work, and hold delivery teams to a high bar for design quality.
jobResponsibilities:
What You’ll Do

  • Design the platform, hands-on: Create high-fidelity designs for citizen and staff-facing interfaces, from concepts to interactive prototypes and reusable components. Bring a sharp eye for visual hierarchy, composition, clarity, and the small details.

  • Lead with user insight: Plan and conduct usability testing, interviews, and research with citizens and staff. Turn findings into clear design decisions that inform the design.

  • Run co-design and experiments: Facilitate workshops with system owners and users to surface needs, test concepts, and build shared ownership. Use structured experiments to resolve design questions with evidence.

  • Improve the design system: Work with technology colleagues to continually refine the design system, building a shared design language and component library that exhibits a high standard of craft and aesthetics.

  • Guide vendor design delivery: Review and shape what vendors produce, from concepts to final interfaces. Protect design integrity and work constructively through differences.

  • Design AI into the experience: Shape how AI is introduced to users, endeavouring to make AI clear and useful, with sensible expectations and graceful recovery.

  • Own adoption, not just launch: Track how designs function after launch. Keep improving the experience until the evidence shows it delivers meaningful value for users.
jobRequirements:
• You have 7+ years of experience in UX or product design, with a portfolio that demonstrates strong hands-on work in Figma across complex digital products.

  • You have an exceptional eye for aesthetics. You care about typography, layout, spacing, visual hierarchy, consistency, and know how these details shape ease of use.

  • You have independently planned and conducted usability research - developing discussion guides, engaging users, analysing results and translating them into designs.

  • You have facilitated workshops and co-design sessions with stakeholders who do not always agree and can rally the group towards a clear decision.

  • You can protect design quality while working productively with delivery teams. You know what to protect, when to compromise, and how to persuade others effectively.

  • You understand how AI systems behave, including their limitations, and can design experiences that set the right expectations for when AI gets things wrong.

  • You understand human factors and cognitive load, and design around how people process information specific to land transportation use cases.

  • You have designed for complex platforms with many services, users, and stakeholders, where consistency and buy-in are design problems in their own right.

  • Prior experience in the Singapore public sector or highly regulated environments and familiarity with enterprise platform / product delivery at scale will be an advantage.

As part of the shortlisting process for the role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and / or undergo further assessment.

jobTitle: [NCCS] Snr Mgr/Asst Dir (Climate Change, Sustainability, Science & Tech Office)
agencyDescription: The Strategy Group in the Prime Minister’s Office drives Whole-of-Government strategic planning, and partners government agencies on policy development. It identifies key priorities and emerging issues over the medium to long term, such as population and climate change; it influences strategic resource allocation; and catalyses new functions and capabilities in order to deliver policies that are in the long-term interest of Singapore.
jobDescription:
The Strategy Group leads and organises the Public Service to deliver the Government’s long-term, cross-cutting priorities. The National Climate Change Secretariat (NCCS), under the Strategy Group, develops, coordinates and implements Singapore’s domestic and international climate change strategies.

You will play four key roles:
•	Technology scouting: Identify and uncover emerging climate mitigation and adaptation technologies with potential to be deployed in Singapore. This involves research and extensive engagement with venture capital firms, climate tech start-ups, research institutes, scientists and industry leaders.
•	Technology assessment and deployment: Assess the technical, economic and deployment potential of promising technologies, and work with agencies and partners to chart pathways for adoption, piloting and scale-up in Singapore.
•	R&D ecosystem development: Help shape Singapore's climate technology and innovation ecosystem by identifying gaps in our public R&D landscape and opportunities for strategic R&D investments. Work with partner agencies to address these gaps, seize emerging opportunities and accelerate the development of transformative solutions.
•	Policy analysis and support: Undertake deep technical and scientific analysis to support national climate policies and strategies, including work on emissions pathways, carbon budgets, marginal abatement cost curves and assessments of specific decarbonisation options. This helps ensure that Singapore's climate policies are grounded in rigorous scientific and technical evidence.
jobResponsibilities: You will be part of the Climate Change, Sustainability, Science and Technology Office (CCSSTO) within NCCS. CCSSTO serves as NCCS' technology office, with the mandate of identifying and advancing emerging technologies that can support Singapore's decarbonisation and climate resilience. Working at the intersection of science, technology and policy, you will help shape how Singapore evaluates, develops and deploys climate solutions.
jobRequirements:
•	Experience in a relevant field (e.g. clean energy, built environment, carbon capture, industrial decarbonisation, climate science) would be an advantage.
•	Strong interest in climate technologies and emerging scientific developments, with curiosity and willingness to engage deeply with technical subject matter.
•	Ability to carry out deep research and analyses of the technical and economic feasibility of emerging climate technologies. 
•	Ability to translate technical and scientific analyses into clear policy insights and actionable recommendations.
•	Comfortable engaging diverse external stakeholders, including venture capital firms, climate tech start-ups, corporates and researchers, to identify emerging opportunities, build partnerships and bring the best ideas to Singapore.

Successful candidates will be offered a 2-year contract. We may refer you as a potential candidate for vacancies in other agencies we assessed you to be suitable for. 
By applying for this job, you are aware of, and are also giving PMO-SG consent for the cross referral. If you do not wish to be cross referred, please inform us via this link: https://go.gov.sg/candidateoptout.
