jobDescription:
We are looking for a Senior Manager/Manager (Board Governance, Leadership Engagement & Organisation Development) to anchor three critical enabling functions: Board Governance, Leadership Engagement, and Organisation Development. This is a multifaceted role that demands both strategic thinking and strong execution, suited for someone equally comfortable navigating the rigour of corporate governance and the nuance of people and culture work.

You will serve as the backbone of HSA's board operations, ensuring sound governance and statutory compliance, while also working closely with senior leaders to build organisational alignment and strengthen leadership capability. At the same time, you will design and drive
initiatives that shape culture, deepen employee engagement, and support the organisation through change.

This role offers a rare opportunity to work at the intersection of governance, leadership, and people excellence — with direct exposure to HSA's most senior stakeholders and the chance to make a meaningful impact on how the organisation functions and grows.
jobResponsibilities:
The incumbent will be responsible for the following:

Board Governance & Leadership Engagement

• Serve as Secretariat to the HSA Board, including planning meeting cycles, preparing agendas, board papers and minutes, and ensuring timely follow-up on resolutions.

• Provide advice on corporate governance, statutory compliance, and board policies in accordance with public sector governance codes and standards.

• Manage director appointments, onboarding, annual declarations, and board performance evaluations.

• Design and execute leadership engagement strategies that cascade organisational priorities and foster alignment across functional units.

• Organise and facilitate leadership forums and dialogue sessions to strengthen leaders' capabilities and collective alignment.

Organisation Development

• Develop and implement organisation development interventions spanning internal communications, employee wellness programmes, and corporate social responsibility initiatives to foster a connected and cohesive workforce.

• Drive regular employee engagement and feedback processes, including staff dialogue sessions, organisational diagnostics, and the design and delivery of people practices that shape the desired organisational culture and behaviours.

• Develop and implement change management plans to support staff through organisational transitions, working with diverse stakeholders to translate plans into tangible outcomes.

• Oversee the governance of research activities in accordance with regulatory requirements and the organisation's research policies and guidelines.

• Contribute to the in-house editorial and design team for the production of the staff newsletter.
jobRequirements:
Education & Experience

• Background in Business Administration, Human Resource Management, Communications, or a related discipline.

• At least 5 to 8 years of relevant experience, with demonstrated exposure to at least two of the following areas: board or corporate secretariat work, organisational development, change management, or internal communications.

• Prior experience in the public sector or a regulated environment would be advantageous.

Technical & Functional Competencies

• Sound knowledge of corporate governance principles and public sector governance frameworks, or a demonstrated ability to acquire such knowledge quickly.

• Strong organisational development and change management capabilities, including experience designing and facilitating engagement sessions and culture-building initiatives.

• Excellent writing skills, with the ability to produce clear, well-structured papers, minutes, and communications materials for both board-level and staff audiences.

• Competent project manager who can handle multiple concurrent workstreams with rigour and attention to detail.

Key Attributes & Personality

• High integrity and discretion — this role handles sensitive board, leadership, and staff matters, and the incumbent must be trusted to exercise sound judgement at all times.

• Intellectually curious and adaptable, able to move fluidly between governance work that demands precision and people work that demands empathy and creativity.

• Confident and credible in engaging senior stakeholders, while remaining collaborative and approachable with colleagues at all levels.

• Self-directed and proactive, with the initiative to identify gaps and act on them without waiting to be told.

• Resilient and composed under pressure, particularly when managing tight timelines around board cycles or organisation-wide initiatives.

• Genuine passion for people and culture — not just as a professional interest, but as a personal conviction that organisations thrive when their people do.

jobDescription: The candidate will oversee fire safety and workplace safety and health (WSH) matters across URA's buildings and facilities at the Marina Bay Area and the Common Service Tunnel. •	Registered Fire Safety Manager (FSM) certification is preferred. Registration as a Workplace Safety and Health Officer (WSHO), Occupational First Aid certification, or other relevant safety qualifications will be an advantage.
•	Experience in facilities management and/or managing outsourced service providers, with the ability to assess contractor performance and fire safety and WSH compliance.
•	Good analytical, communication, report writing and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage internal stakeholders, contractors and regulatory agencies effectively.

• Familiarity with AI engineering, including integrations, prompt engineering, and embedding strategies.
• Exposure to advanced search architectures, specifically vector search, semantic search, and RAG patterns.

jobTitle: Senior / Health Policy Analyst (Finance Policy – MediShield Life Benefits)
agencyDescription:
The Ministry of Health’s (MOH) vision is to champion a healthy nation with our people – to live well, live long and with peace of mind. As an open country constantly exposed to an interconnected world, Singapore faces complex issues in public healthcare. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.
jobDescription:
You will be part of the team which formulates, reviews and implements policies to develop Singapore’s healthcare financing framework, with a focus on MediShield Life, to keep healthcare affordable and sustainable for all Singaporeans. This role will require you to work collaboratively with policy and clinical groups within MOH, healthcare institutions and other public agencies to develop and implement MediShield Life policies. 

You will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders.
jobResponsibilities:
As part of the MediShield Life team, you will contribute towards 

•	Reviewing MediShield Life benefits to ensure adequate protection against large healthcare bills and sustainable coverage of innovative high-cost technologies, balancing against impact on premiums.  This may require you to:
     o	Analyse claims and utilisation data from a variety of sources to identify gaps and make recommendations to address them. 
     o	Work with MOH divisions to evaluate new models of care, align on service strategies, or assess clinical and cost-effectiveness of medical interventions 
     o	Work with stakeholders overseeing other mainstream financing schemes and private insurance to develop holistic proposals for extension/review of existing financing coverage;
     o	Work closely with the scheme’s actuaries to determine premium impact of any benefit enhancement 
     o	Consult healthcare institutions and clinicians to understand the impact of changes in financing. 

•	Overseeing the implementation of new or revised policies relating to MediShield Life benefits, including working with internal and external stakeholders to enhance claims systems, assessing appeals for coverage, and resolving operational issues arising from claim management.

•	Working with legal stakeholders to draft and effect amendments to legislation that support changes in coverage policy and safeguard leverage on the MediShield Life fund.


Beyond the above, you will also:

•	Contribute to the policy-ops feedback loop, by addressing parliamentary questions and public queries

•	Work with partner agencies and stakeholders to enhance public communications of healthcare financing schemes

•	Provide secretariat support to the MediShield Life Council and its sub-committees in carrying out their functions
jobRequirements:
Key Competencies Required:
•	Thinking Clearly & Making Sound Judgements – Strong analytical and critical thinking abilities to support the crafting of sound policy recommendations; ability to grasp timelines, operating context and ground realities.
 
•	Learning & Putting Skills into Action - Possesses the drive and curiosity to learn and apply new skills, knowledge and new ways of working. 

•	Improving & Innovating – Ability to seek continual improvements, and to innovate and experiment while managing the risks involved. 

•	Working Effectively with Stakeholders – Ability to mobilise and rally partners and stakeholders towards a collective purpose.

Other

•	Tertiary education in any discipline. Background in economics would be advantageous
•	Excellent writing, presentation and negotiation skills, experience in public policy formulation and/or scheme administration in the social sector would be an advantage

jobDescription: MANAGER/DEPUTY/ASSISTANT MANAGER, AV DATA POLICY, GOVERNANCE & ENGINEERING
jobResponsibilities:
Data is the backbone of how Singapore regulates and assures the safety of autonomous vehicles. The team plays a dual-role shaping the policy of autonomous vehicles (AV) data: what data AV companies must provide – how it can be shared and used, including for Artificial Intelligence applications; and the management of collected AV data – how data flows between systems and teams, and the standards and APIs that keep it usable and trustworthy.

This role is open at two levels — a core set of responsibilities applies to all hires, with additional ownership and leadership expectations for more senior candidates (see section below). Appointment level, title and specific scope of work will be commensurate with relevant experience, and we welcome both early-career and more experienced candidates. As part of the shortlisting, you may be required to complete further assessment for candidates looking to take on a more technical role with the team.

CAM leads Singapore’s national effort to deploy AVs at scale. Doing this safely depends on getting the right data, in the right form, to the right people — from AV developers into our systems, across CAM’s teams, and to partners and the public. You will you will join a fresh but experienced team that will shape the rules for that data and make sure it flows cleanly, securely and responsibly. This is a unique opportunity for laying the foundations of data in an emerging space that would let you appreciate the challenges in an emerging embodied AI space.

Shape data policy and regulation for AVs

  • Develop the data requirements AV companies must meet — what operational and safety data they share with CAM, in what format, at what frequency, and how it may be used.
  • Design data-sharing and responsible-use frameworks — balancing regulatory oversight with industry burden and privacy, and aligning with national data and privacy regulation (e.g. the PDPA) and whole-of-government data governance, including for AI uses.
  • Set the rules of the road for AV data — how it is classified, retained, protected and shared, and how data ownership and disputes are handled.
  • Engage stakeholders — work with AV developers, government agencies and internal teams to align on data standards, agreements and expectations.

Engineer and manage data flows and standards

  • Map and manage how data moves within CAM and LTA — from ingestion through storage to use — and remove the friction and gaps in those flows.
  • Implement good API and data-exchange practices — define data standards, schemas and contracts so systems and partners can integrate cleanly and consistently.
  • Drive data quality and stewardship — cataloguing, lineage and metadata so data is discoverable, trustworthy and well-documented.
  • Work with the Systems team on the plumbing — building the data architecture and data pipelines to help make CAM’s data ready for analytics and AI.

Bridge policy and implementation

  • Translate policy intent into concrete requirements for industry and for internal engineers can build to — and feed implementation realities back into policy.
  • Be the connective tissue between policy, operations, legal and engineering on anything data-related.

If you join as a more senior hire, you will also

  • Own CAM’s data governance framework and data strategy end to end.
  • Set data standards and act as CAM’s data authority with agencies and AV developers.
  • Lead the resolution of complex or sensitive data issues, and mentor others as the function grows.

If you like operating where policy meets engineering — and want your work to shape how a new technology is governed — we want to hear from you.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for someone who:

  • Thinks clearly about data and policy — can reason about how data should be governed, shared and protected, and turn that into workable rules.
  • Has some technical competency — comfortable enough to be hands-on with data analytics and engineering — reading and querying it (e.g. SQL), understanding APIs, schemas and data pipelines, and working credibly with engineers. You should be able to bridge policy and implementation.
  • Communicates and aligns stakeholders — builds consensus across AV developers, agencies, legal, operations and engineering.
  • Takes initiative and cares about the public good — this is new ground, so you will help set the standards rather than inherit them.

Useful, but not essential (though increasingly expected at senior levels)

  • Familiarity with data governance frameworks (e.g. IM8), data management practices, or data privacy regulation (e.g. the PDPA).
  • Hands-on experience with SQL, APIs, data modelling, or data cataloguing / lineage tools.
  • A background in computer science, information systems, data analytics, engineering, public policy, or a related field.
  • Experience bridging policy and technical implementation, or working across IT, legal and business teams.
  • Interest in autonomous vehicles, transport, and data as a regulated asset.

jobTitle: Manager / Senior Manager (Finance Systems Policy - NPHC Policy Development)
agencyDescription:
The Ministry of Health’s (MOH) vision is to champion a healthy nation with our people – to live well, live long and with peace of mind. As an open country constantly exposed to an interconnected world, Singapore faces complex issues in public healthcare. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.
jobDescription:
The Division:
Singapore keeps healthcare affordable through government subsidies and the 3Ms: MediShield Life, MediSave and MediFund. For these schemes to work, every part of the supporting systems must function accurately and reliably. 
The Finance Systems Policy (FSP) division at MOH owns the systems that make this possible. These include the National Platform for Healthcare Claims (NPHC), means-testing systems administering healthcare subsidies such as the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS), and the accreditation framework that governs which institutions and practitioners may participate in financing schemes. Together, these systems process tens of thousands of healthcare finance transactions daily and form the operational backbone of Singapore's healthcare financing architecture.

The Role:
You will begin in NPHC, where MediSave and MediShield Life policies are translated into system rules and operational outcomes. The platform processes over 10 million claims annually from public and private hospitals, clinics and other institutions, and interfaces with the Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB), the National Billing System (NBS) used by the public healthcare clusters, Integrated Shield Plan (IP) insurers, and other MOH systems. Every MediSave deduction and MediShield Life payout and financing computation depends on the system applying the right rules to the right patient at the right time. A rule implemented wrongly means a patient pays the wrong amount and creates downstream reconciliation work for institutions and insurers. Getting the rule right, on the date MOH has committed to publicly, is what this role exists to do.
Over time, as you develop your understanding of FSP's portfolio, there are opportunities to take on other healthcare financing systems. While each system is different, the core responsibilities remain the same: translating policy intent into system behaviour and operational outcomes and ensuring that implementation delivers the intended outcomes for patients, payers and providers. 

You will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time
jobResponsibilities:
Policy Topic Ownership
You will manage a portfolio of healthcare financing policy topics from early policy development through implementation and post-deployment validation. The work starts while the policy is still being formed, not after it is decided. You will work alongside MOH's Healthcare Finance policy divisions to shape policy proposals that can be implemented effectively, then carry the topic through implementation to the point where claims are processed correctly in production. This includes translating policy requirements into system design with vendors and technical teams, refining user stories, testing end-to-end, and confirming the change works before it reaches patients. You will be expected to work independently, surface implementation and operational risks early, and remain accountable for driving each topic through to resolution.

Policy-to-System Translation
Healthcare financing schemes evolve continuously. Claim limits change. New drugs and services become claimable. Deductible, co-insurance and pro-ration parameters are revised. Each change requires someone who understands both the policy intent and constraints and the system behaviour well enough to ensure nothing is lost in translation, and to identify early where a policy cannot be implemented as drafted. A significant part of the role is identifying downstream implementation risks before policy commitments are made. You will be expected to challenge assumptions, surface operational implications, and explain clearly where policy intent and system reality diverge.
You will test business rules against real claims and billing practices, prepare implementation notes that tell institutions, insurers and system partners what is changing and when, and hold that position through consultation. This work is a core responsibility of the role, not a subset of project delivery.

Cross-Party Solutioning
Healthcare financing operates across multiple parties with competing objectives. Policy owners may prioritise policy outcomes. Institutions weigh operational workload and cashflow implications. Insurers focus on claims accuracy and recovery. Technical teams must ensure solutions can be implemented appropriately and sustainably. You will run these consultations directly across public and private institutions, the IP insurers, NBS and its vendors, and CPFB. Your role is not to satisfy every stakeholder. Your role is to structure competing considerations, lead discussions towards workable solutions, and recommend a clear implementation position that balances policy intent, operational feasibility and system integrity, including when that position is not the option stakeholders initially preferred. 

Operational Continuity and Analytics
Implementation does not end at deployment. You will monitor deployed changes after production rollout, investigate production issues, and analyse claims and system data yourself to validate implementation outcomes: how utilisation changed, whether payouts moved as expected, and whether unintended consequences emerged. You will be expected to trace issues to their root causes, validate outcomes using evidence, and use data to inform future policy and system decisions.
This is not a project coordination role. Success is measured by the quality of your judgment, the soundness of your recommendations, and whether the implemented system behaviour reflects the intended policy outcome. The role requires genuine ownership of both the policy intent behind a change and the system logic that carries it out.

The Team:
You will report to an Assistant Director within FSP and work alongside a division of about 14 officers. You are expected to work across NPHC workstreams covering policy development and implementation, as well as the introduction of new system features and capabilities.

FSP runs a structured capability development programme for its officers, built around four areas: product thinking, policy domain knowledge, communications, and technical skills. In practical terms, within 9 months, you should be able to: read a policy proposal and identify implementation risks before development begins, hold your own in a technical design review with vendors and system teams, lead discussions across policy teams, institutions and insurers, analyse claims outcomes and explain what happened, why it happened and whether the result is consistent with policy intent, and produce recommendations that help Senior Management make sound decisions.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for someone with 3 to 5 years of working experience in policy, operations, technology, analytics or a field that requires structured problem solving across multiple domains.

Beyond that, what matters is how you think. You should be able to develop a clear position from incomplete information, test it against evidence, and communicate it clearly, and adjust it when new facts emerge. 

Key competencies required:
•	Thinking Clearly and Making Sound Judgements. In FSP, this means tracing financing outcomes from policy intent through business rules, system logic and claims behaviour, and determining whether the outcomes are correct. You will be expected to develop evidence-based recommendations and advise Senior Management and stakeholders on policy implementation options and trade-offs. You should be comfortable with numbers, as much of the role involves validating the results of financing computations using real operational data.
•	Learning and Putting Skills into Action. Healthcare financing is a domain you build over time. What matters is your willingness to understand it rigorously and to apply what you learn and continue building expertise in an environment where the impact on patients and healthcare providers is real.
•	Improving and Innovating. FSP's systems serve a policy landscape that changes continuously. You should be able to identify where a process or system has not kept pace and propose practical improvements while managing implementation risks.
•	Working Effectively with Stakeholders. NPHC operates across MOH, CPFB, the public healthcare clusters, private medical institutions, insurers and system partners. You should be able to work across these stakeholders to achieve clear, workable and sustainable outcomes.
•	Communicating Clearly: You should have strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex policy and system issues and recommendations clearly

Your background is less important than how you approach problems. That said, the following thinking patterns tend to predict success in this role:
•	You enjoy working across policy development, operations and technical implementation.
•	You are curious about how large systems work and naturally want to understand why something happened rather than accepting that it happened. 
•	You are comfortable working through ambiguity and incomplete information.
•	You prefer owning a problem end-to-end rather than handing it off once a recommendation is made.
•	You build your views from evidence rather than consensus.
•	You see stakeholder complexity as a problem to be structured and solved.
Prior experience in healthcare, the public sector, or a regulated industry is useful but not required. Familiarity with Singapore's healthcare financing schemes (MediSave, MediShield Life, CHAS) is a genuine advantage.

What we can offer you
This role provides exposure to policy development, large-scale system implementation, data-driven decision making and stakeholder engagement within a single posting. You will work with policy divisions, healthcare institutions, insurers and technology vendors while developing the ability to operate across policy, operations and technology domains.

As part of the shortlisting process for this role, candidates may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

jobDescription: LEAD /PRINCIPAL CYBER ENGINEER (SOC PRODUCT LEAD)
jobResponsibilities:
The SOC Product Lead is the strategic owner of the Cybersecurity Operations Centre's detection and monitoring capabilities, treating the SOC as a continuously evolving product rather than a static operational function. This role bridges business risk, stakeholder demands, compliance obligations, and the threat landscape — translating them into a prioritised roadmap that the Tech Lead and analyst teams execute against. The Product Lead does not build detection rules; they ensure the right capabilities are built, in the right order, for the right outcomes.​

SOC Capability Roadmap & Backlog Ownership

  • Define, own, and continuously refine the SOC capability roadmap — encompassing detection use cases, automation workflows, tooling enhancements, and analyst enablement initiatives
  • Maintain a prioritised product backlog that balances immediate operational risk reduction with longer-term platform maturity goals
  • Write clear user stories and acceptance criteria for detection use cases, SOAR playbooks, and dashboard requirements — in a format the Tech Lead and engineering team can act on
  • Facilitate sprint planning, backlog refinement, and sprint review ceremonies in collaboration with the Tech Lead and Design Lead
  • Track and report delivery velocity, sprint outcomes, and roadmap progress to SOC management and security leadership​

Stakeholder Management & Requirements Gathering

  • Act as the primary interface between the SOC and internal stakeholders
  • Conduct regular stakeholder engagement sessions to surface new monitoring requirements, regulatory obligations, and threat concerns
  • Translate ambiguous business risk statements into concrete, actionable SOC capability requirements
  • Manage stakeholder expectations on delivery timelines, scope trade-offs, and prioritisation decisions
  • Represent the SOC's capability roadmap in governance forums, risk committees, and security steering group meetings​

Threat-Informed Prioritisation

  • Maintain a continuous threat landscape assessment — incorporating inputs from threat intelligence feeds, red team findings, incident post-mortems, industry ISACs, and regulatory advisories
  • Prioritise detection use case development based on threat actor relevance, asset criticality, and exploitability — mapped to the MITRE ATT&CK framework
  • Own the detection coverage gap register, working with the Tech Lead to close high-priority gaps within agreed sprint cycles
  • Ensure new and emerging threat vectors (e.g., AI-assisted attacks, supply chain compromise, cloud-native threats) are reflected in the backlog ahead of operational need​

Tool & Vendor Strategy

  • Own the SOC technology portfolio strategy — including SIEM, SOAR, EDR, threat intelligence platforms, and supporting integrations
  • Lead vendor evaluations, RFP processes, and proof-of-concept reviews in collaboration with the Tech Lead, providing business and capability justifications for tooling decisions
  • Manage vendor relationships, contract renewals, and SLA oversight for all SOC platform providers
  • Track the market for emerging security technologies and assess their fit against the SOC's capability roadmap
  • Own the SOC technology budget — forecasting spend, managing renewals, and justifying investment cases to leadership​

Metrics, Reporting & Continuous Improvement

  • Define and own the SOC's key performance indicators (KPIs) and operational metrics — including MTTD, MTTR, alert fidelity, use case coverage, and automation rates
  • Develop and maintain executive-facing dashboards and reports that communicate SOC effectiveness in business risk terms, not purely technical metrics
  • Lead regular operational reviews — identifying trends, persistent gaps, and improvement opportunities across people, process, and technology dimensions
  • Conduct use case lifecycle reviews to retire outdated rules, refresh low-fidelity detections, and ensure the detection library remains current and relevant
  • Drive post-incident reviews from a product improvement perspective — ensuring lessons learned are converted into backlog items and delivered

Compliance & Governance Alignment

  • Ensure SOC monitoring coverage aligns with applicable regulatory frameworks and compliance requirements (e.g., MAS TRM, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, local IM8 guidelines where applicable)
  • Maintain traceability between compliance control requirements and deployed detection use cases
  • Support internal and external audits by providing evidence of SOC capability coverage and operational effectiveness
  • Coordinate with the risk and compliance function to ensure the SOC's roadmap reflects the organisation's broader risk appetite and control objectives​
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, or related technical discipline

• Deep understanding of security monitoring and detection operations — including alert triage workflows, incident response lifecycles, and T1/T2/T3 analyst structures

• Working knowledge of the MITRE ATT&CK framework, common attack vectors, threat actor TTPs, and emerging threat categories

• Functional understanding of SIEM platforms (preferably Microsoft Sentinel), SOAR, EDR and threat intelligence platforms

• Ability to define meaningful SOC KPIs, build reporting frameworks, and communicate operational performance to both technical and non-technical audiences

• Exposure to cloud security monitoring concepts across Azure and AWS

• Experience operating within a regulated financial services, critical infrastructure, or government SOC environment

• At least 5 years in cybersecurity with at least 2 years in a product management, SOC management, or senior security operations role with strategic responsibilities

• Demonstrated experience owning a security capability roadmap or technology portfolio, including vendor management and budget accountability

• Track record of translating business and risk requirements into security monitoring outcomes

• Exceptional communication skills

• Strategic thinker who can balance long-term capability building with short-term operational firefighting

• Data-driven decision-making mindset with the ability to challenge assumptions using evidence from SOC metrics and threat intelligence

As a statutory board of the Ministry of Home Affairs and integral to the Home Team, HTX works at the forefront of science and technology to empower Singapore’s frontline of security. Our shared mission is to amplify, augment and accelerate the Home Team’s advantage and secure Singapore as the safest place on planet earth.

In this post, you will drive the conceptualisation and implementation of Operational Technology (OT) automation solutions as well as oversee the capability sustainment of deployed systems in the Operations and Support (O&S) phase across Home Team Departments (HTDs), focusing on use cases supporting corrections, narcotics enforcement, and rehabilitation operations. The role aims to enhance operational effectiveness, improve officer safety, and achieve manpower savings through the adoption of innovative and practical technologies. In addition, you will also ensure that systems continue to meet operational, availability and compliance requirements and provide the required support to maintain smooth Home Team operations.

The Corrections & Narcotics Programme Management Centre (CNPMC) works closely with the Singapore Prison Service (SPS) and Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB), supporting their visions to be “Captains of Lives” and for “A Singapore Without Drugs, where everyone can work, live and play safely”.

CNPMC leverages science and technology to enforce the secure custody and rehabilitation of offenders, and to prevent the proliferation of drug-related activities.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Support or lead projects involving the adoption of ready S&T solutions or the translation of proof-of-concept (POC) or execution of POC initiatives to deliver systems with view towards operational deployment.
•	Plan and manage project timelines, payment milestones, budgets and deliverables to ensure successful implementation and operationalisation.
•	Develop technical specifications and documentations, including drafting contractual terms.
•	Manage vendors and stakeholders to ensure solutions are delivered on time, within scope, and to required quality standards.
•	Engage HTDs to understand requirements and facilitate discussions for strategic planning and decision-making on automation roadmaps.
•	Conceptualise and work with vendors to develop innovative automation solutions by integrating existing technologies to address HTD operational requirements.

jobRequirements:

•	Preferably 5 – 8 years of relevant working experience in OT automation, engineering, OT-ICT integration or related domains in project, O&S or technical management roles.
•	Strong ability to conceptualise and deliver innovative, feasible, and impactful solutions to operational challenges.
•	Strong fundamentals and interest in science, technology and innovation; self-driven in keeping up with latest developments and willingness to challenge the norms.
•	Good project management skills, including planning, coordination, and execution of projects involving multiple stakeholders. Experience in managing capability sustainment should be indicated.

•	Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a dynamic environment.
•	Good communication and stakeholder engagement skills across a diverse range of stakeholders.

jobDescription:
This is a 2-year contract position with the Digital Services & Technology Office.

The AI Engineer will be instrumental in implementing NP's AI transformation strategy by developing production-ready AI applications and systems that leverage AI tools and Cloud AI services. This role focuses on building robust, scalable AI solutions using GenAI models, deep learning, neural networks, and other AI technologies to improve NP operations through intelligent automation and advanced analytics. Working in close collaboration with the AI Product Manager, data scientists, and cross-functional teams, the AI Engineer will transition AI models from research to production and embed AI capabilities into NP's administrative and academic support workflows.
jobResponsibilities:
AI Solution Development

  • Design, develop, and implement AI/ML models, algorithms, and GenAI-powered applications (including conversational AI, content generation, and intelligent document processing systems) using diverse approaches and platforms such as Microsoft Copilot Studio, Databricks Apps, Azure AI Studio, and custom development frameworks.

  • Deploy and integrate AI solutions with existing enterprise systems, ensuring compatibility with data infrastructure and institutional workflows.

Model Development & Operations

  • Design, build, and train machine learning, deep learning, and neural network models tailored to address specific institutional needs across administrative and operational domains.

  • Collect, analyse, and clean data from various sources to train and test AI models, working closely with data engineering teams to ensure data quality and accessibility.

  • Test, validate, and optimise algorithms to ensure reliability, scalability, and performance across various use cases and production environments

Technical Implementation

  • Configure and utilise AI development environments and tools within the AI platform infrastructure provided by the infrastructure team.

  • Implement MLOps practices including automated model training, testing, deployment pipelines, version control, and continuous integration for AI solutions.

  • Deploy AI models and applications using cloud AI services (Azure, AWS) and platform infrastructure, ensuring optimal performance and resource utilisation.

  • Develop APIs and microservices to serve AI models, enabling robust integration with institutional workflows and applications.

Quality Assurance & Support

  • Ensure AI solutions meet NP's technical standards for scalability, reliability, security, and maintainability while complying with data privacy regulations and ethical AI guidelines.

  • Provide technical support, troubleshooting, and performance optimisation for deployed AI applications and models.

  • Collaborate with Infrastructure team to define requirements for AI platform capabilities and provide feedback on platform performance and functionality.

  • Work closely with data scientists, product teams, and business stakeholders to align AI solutions with institutional goals and embed AI capabilities into workflows.
jobRequirements:
• Degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

  • Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience in AI/ML development with demonstrated expertise in building and managing both AI infrastructure and applications in production environments.

Skills & Certifications

  • Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, R, or Java, with experience in AI/ML frameworks like TensorFlow, PyTorch, scikit-learn, and related ecosystem tools.

  • Experience with cloud platforms (Azure, AWS) including AI services, infrastructure-as-code, containerisation technologies (Docker, Kubernetes), and platform engineering practices.

  • Expertise in MLOps tools and practices, including model lifecycle management, automated deployment pipelines, monitoring, and governance frameworks.

  • Knowledge of data engineering concepts, API development, microservices architecture, and enterprise integration patterns.

  • Experience with enterprise platforms such as Databricks, Microsoft Co-Pilot Studio, Power Platform, and familiarity with Singapore IT governance and security frameworks.

Attributes

  • Detail-focused and methodical.

  • Problem-solver with a performance-driven mindset.

  • Adaptable and collaborative within cross-functional teams.

  • Strong communicator able to work across AI, governance, and business stakeholders.

jobDescription:
You will lead the Applications & Programme Assessment function for the SG Culture Pass, ensuring that programme applications are assessed fairly, consistently and in accordance with policy intent. As the functional lead, you will oversee the integrity of the end-to-end applications framework, provide leadership on complex and precedent-setting cases, drive continuous improvements to assessment processes and systems, and build trusted relationships with sector stakeholders and partner agencies.
Beyond day-to-day operations, you will shape the governance and continuous evolution of the applications regime, ensuring that it remains robust, transparent, auditable and responsive to an evolving arts and heritage landscape.
jobResponsibilities:
Key Responsibilities

1. Lead the Applications Function for Events and Books
•	Lead the end-to-end management of the SG Culture Pass applications framework, from application receipt through assessment, approval, notification and post-approval governance.
•	Ensure applications are assessed consistently, accurately and within service standards.
•	Oversee application workflows and coordinate approval processes to ensure timely and well-supported decisions.
•	Monitor performance via dashboards to ensure service standards, assessment quality and operational targets are consistently met.
•	Exercise judgement on complex, novel and precedent-setting applications.
•	Ensure assessment decisions are properly documented and defensible.

2. Policy, Governance & Quality Assurance
•	Interpret and apply eligibility criteria in accordance with policy intent, maintaining assessment frameworks, rubrics and guidance to ensure consistency. 
•	Review and update policies, SOPs and governance frameworks as needed, and advise management on emerging issues and recommended refinements. 
•	Establish QA processes to maintain programme quality, uphold assessment standards, identify risks and ensure compliance with audit, governance and data management requirements.

3. Operational Excellence & Systems Improvement
•	Design and continuously improve application processes, workflows and operating procedures, identifying bottlenecks and process gaps, and implement practical solutions.
•	Work with Data, Product, Technology and Operations teams to enhance digital systems and workflow automation, balancing improvements to applicant experience with strong governance and controls.


4. Data, Reporting & Knowledge Management
•	Analyse application trends and assessment outcomes to identify emerging issues and opportunities.
•	Prepare management reports, policy papers and briefing materials.
•	Maintain robust assessment records, precedents and institutional knowledge.
•	Ensure documentation is complete, audit-ready and readily retrievable.

5. Stakeholder Engagement
•	Lead engagement with applicants, Arts & Heritage Partners, ticketing partners and government agencies on complex matters.
•	Build trusted relationships with sector stakeholders while safeguarding policy integrity.
•	Manage escalated stakeholder issues with professionalism, maturity and sound judgement.
•	Represent the Applications function at cross-agency and management discussions where required.

6. Team Leadership and Cross-Functional Collaboration
•	Develop and lead a high-performing applications team, fostering a culture of professionalism, fairness, and continuous improvement.
•	Build assessment capability through calibration exercises, systematic documentation of assessment precedents, and maintaining institutional knowledge to ensure consistency and reduce reliance on individual expertise.
•	Serve as the primary liaison with Finance/Governance team to ensure all processes are compliant, auditable, and legally sound.
•	Collaborate with the Marketing team to shape public messaging regarding programme policies, application windows, and success stories.
•	Work with Marketing and Outreach teams on timely updates of programme refresh cycle upon approval, to support curation of high-capacity programmes for marketing and promotion efforts.
•	Guide the Applications team on responses to Level 2 queries from Arts and Heritage Partners, Event Organisers and Book Publishers pertaining to assessment and eligibility queries for live events, books and films. These will be channelled from Outreach/Ops team from Call Centre and Helpdesk after their triaging.
jobRequirements:
Experience Required
•	At least 8 years of relevant experience in policy implementation, programme administration, grants management, regulatory assessment, public sector operations or a related field.
•	Demonstrated experience leading complex operational functions involving structured assessment, approvals or governance processes.
•	Experience supervising and developing teams while maintaining consistent standards and service quality.
•	Proven track record of managing complex stakeholder relationships and problem-solving
•	Experience designing or improving operational processes, governance frameworks and systems.
•	Experience preparing submissions, management papers, policy recommendations and briefing materials for senior management.
•	Experience analysing operational data to drive policy or process improvements.
•	Experience working across multiple agencies or with external stakeholders would be advantageous.
•	Familiarity with Singapore's arts, heritage or literary sectors, or experience assessing programmes within a grants or public funding environment, would be an advantage.

Key Competencies
•	Judgement - Exercises sound judgement in balancing policy intent, operational practicality and stakeholder considerations, particularly when assessing novel or ambiguous applications.
•	Process Excellence - Designs robust, scalable and auditable operational processes.
•	Attention to Detail - Meticulous in reviewing evidence, documentation and assessment decisions.
•	Stakeholder Management - Builds credibility and trust while navigating complex stakeholder relationships with maturity.
•	Problem Solving - Comfortable operating in ambiguity and able to develop practical pathways forward.
•	Continuous Improvement - Proactively improves policies, systems and operational processes to enhance efficiency and service delivery.

Success Profile

A successful candidate will:
•	Lead a high-performing applications function that is fair, consistent and audit-ready.
•	Exercise sound judgement in balancing policy, operational and stakeholder considerations.
•	Build trusted relationships across the arts and heritage ecosystem while safeguarding the integrity of the SG Culture Pass.
•	Drive continuous improvements that enhance efficiency, governance and applicant experience.
•	Develop a capable and collaborative team that upholds high professional standards.

* Successful candidate will be offered 2-year contract in first instance, with potential for extension or confirmation.

jobResponsibilities:
You will be part of the Board’s network security team responsible for protecting systems, networks, and endpoints from cybersecurity threats. As an NDR & EDR Engineer, you will manage and operationalise Network Detection and Response (NDR) and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) platforms, working closely with internal teams to ensure robust threat detection and response capabilities. 

In this role, you will: 
• Deploy, configure, and maintain NDR and EDR solutions across on-premises and cloud environments, in accordance with applicable ICT security policies and standards.
• Develop, tune, and maintain detection rules and alert policies to improve detection accuracy and minimise false positives across networks and endpoints.
• Monitor, triage security alerts and escalate incidents to the SOC or Incident Response team in accordance with established procedures.
• Support incident response and forensic investigations, including analysis of endpoint and network telemetry, evidence handling and reporting. 
• Conduct proactive threat hunting using NDR and EDR telemetry to identify indicators of compromise, suspicious and advanced persistent threats (APTs) targeting government infrastructure.
• Integrate NDR and EDR platforms with SIEM and security orchestration tools to support effective detection, investigation and response workflows.
• Ensure platform configurations and detection logic comply with applicable security frameworks, including the Government Instruction Manual on IT Management (IM8) and relevant cybersecurity guidelines.
• Maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation including platform configurations, standard operating procedures, and incident runbooks.
• Liaise with vendors, GovTech and internal stakeholders on platform updates, threat intelligence sharing, security advisories and related operational matters.
jobRequirements:
We value the diverse talents and experiences that each individual brings to the table. While mastery of every requirement may not be necessary, familiarity and expertise in some of the following areas will position you for success within this team.
• Experience in cybersecurity engineering or security operations, including hands-on experience with EDR and/or NDR platforms such as CrowdStrike Falcon, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Trend Vision One, Darktrace, ExtraHop, Vectra AI or Corelight. 
• Knowledge of network protocols, traffic analysis, and endpoint telemetry and forensic investigation techniques
• Good understanding of Windows and Linux internals, including processes, memory, registry and security models, with experience analysing event logs for threat detection.
• Familiarity with attack and persistence techniques (e.g. Pass-the-Hash, Kerberoasting, LOLBins, privilege escalation, SSH persistent) and their mapping to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, as well as experience deploying EDR agents and telemetry tools like Sysmon, auditd, and osquery.
• Proficiency in using SIEM platforms (e.g. Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, QRadar) for security log analysis and investigation.
• Ability to develop and tune detection rules and queries using languages and formats such as KQL, SPL, Sigma rules. 
• Experience supporting incident response investigations, including evidence handling, analysis and reporting.
• Ability to use scripting languages such as Python, PowerShell or Bash for automation and detection engineering.
• Familiarity with Singapore Government security frameworks including IM8, the Cybersecurity Act, and CSA's Cybersecurity Code of Practice would be advantageous. 
• Exposure to cloud environments (e.g. Azure, AWS or Government Commercial Cloud) and associated security tools would be advantageous. 
• Relevant certifications such as GCFA, GCFE, GCIA, GCED, CEH, or EDR/NDR certifications would be advantageous. 

The seniority of appointment and actual corporate job title will commensurate with individual work experiences.

Position is on a 2-year full-time contract directly under the payroll of CPF Board with potential for emplacement into a permanent position.

This will involve integrating information from various sources to understand emerging risks and needs, undertaking gap analyses across legislation, policy and service delivery, and exercising sound judgement on the appropriate policy and implementation responses. You will also oversee strategy and communications-related matters across these portfolios.

•	Forging partnerships with stakeholders: You will work closely with internal and external stakeholders to understand clients’ needs, assess the suitability of proposed solutions, and support effective policy development and implementation. You may also lead inter-agency workgroups, conduct consultations with stakeholder groups and engage members of the public on matters relating to these portfolios.

You will contribute to the development and oversight of policies that enhance residential support, protection and rehabilitation for vulnerable groups in society.
If you are keen to develop policies that improve outcomes for vulnerable individuals and families, this could be the role for you.

Compensation

The incumbent is responsible for managing the compensation function, ensuring that the organisation's salary structures and pay practices are equitable and aligned with Public Service-wide frameworks and guidelines. This includes administering and supporting the implementation of Public Service-wide salary reviews and adjustments as directed.

The role also involves processing and administering salary changes arising from promotions, regrading, and other employment movements, ensuring that all changes are accurately reflected in the HR and payroll systems. The incumbent works closely with HR business partners to provide compensation-related advice and analysis and ensures that all compensation practices are administered in accordance with established policies, guidelines, and regulatory requirements.

Benefits Administration

The incumbent is responsible for the end-to-end administration of employee benefits, ensuring that all programmes are accurately processed, compliant with relevant legislation and organisational policies, and effectively communicated to employees. This encompasses the administration of medical and dental benefits, including the management of claims and eligibility entitlements. agencyDescription:
Master planner. Developer. Since its inception in 1968, JTC has played a strategic role in ensuring Singapore stays innovative, dynamic, and sensitive to global manufacturing trends.

A government agency under Singapore’s Ministry of Trade and Industry, JTC is paving the way forward for Singapore’s industrial landscape by championing clean, green and smart estates such as one-north, Seletar Aerospace Park, Jurong Innovation District, and Punggol Digital District. It is developing infrastructure, systems and initiatives that bridge cutting-edge technology and human skill to fuel growth.  

JTC is also bringing businesses and communities together through green spaces, cultivating an environment that is not only sustainable but nurtures ideas shaping the future.
jobDescription: Plan, source and manage JTC’s land stock to ensure supply of adequate industrial land to support JTC's short, medium and long term development needs and Singapore’s economic development.
jobResponsibilities:
Land Use Policy Development

Review existing land use policies and recommend new policies to support industrial restructuring or intensify land use that achieve land productivity, taking into account changing economic/business needs and trends while balancing the need to safeguard the resource for future needs.

Land Resource Planning and Management

Manage the JTC land stock to ensure the optimal use of land. This includes:

  • Monitoring JTC land supply and making adjustments to support changes in demand through the various platforms (e.g. long term plan and master plan reviews);
  • Buying land and doing lease top up to meet industrialists’ needs at the appropriate time;
  • Right-siting companies who need land, taking into consideration the different types of land constraints e.g. water catchment, nuisance buffer, etc.;
  • Put vacant land to interim use to optimise use of land and minimise holding cost.

Formulate and track land recycling plan to support the redevelopment of land that optimises its use. This includes conducting regular island-wide land expiry reviews and identifying sites for En-Bloc Redevelopment (EBR)/Selective Buy Back (SBB), as well as replacement sites for affected EBR lessees if necessary.

Geospatial Analyses and tools

Supervise and/or carry out geospatial analyses on various land-related issues to guide land planning strategies and policies, and create new GIS tools/enhance existing GIS tools to improve planning decisions.

Collaboration

Work closely with other divisions in JTC, such as:

  • Engineering and project management colleagues to ensure land is prepared and made available in timely manner to meet industries’ needs;
  • Cluster officers, architects and planners on master plans of new/rejuvenated estates, and to create innovative products and ideas for optimal land use and sustainable development;
  • Cluster officers and policy and research officers to prepare land for iGLS and TOL launches.

Work with other agencies on land use matters to safeguard JTC’s interests, without losing the Whole-of-Government perspective. These range from rezoning cases to more complex land use policies.

Enhancing Productivity

Conduct regular reviews of work processes to ensure relevance and improve productivity including use of technology and automation.

Staff Development

Understand the aspirations and interests of staff and provide them with the support to deal with the challenges or issues that might be holding them back from achieving their goals, and to work with them on career development and progression.
jobRequirements:
• Qualification in Economics, Business, Real Estate, Geography or any related to the built environment sector
  • Training in geospatial analytics is an advantage
  • At least 5 years working experience leading a team
  • Possess strong communication skills with the ability to build effective and strong working relationships at all levels
  • Strong leadership skills
  • Excellent written and presentation skills required

Incident Response Leadership

While most neighbour disputes can and should be resolved through dialogue and mediation, a small minority involve excessive and prolonged noise disturbances that cause significant distress to multiple residents. CRU focuses on these severe neighbour noise cases across public and private housing estates. 

As Team Leader (Investigation and Enforcement), you will lead a team of Community Relations Officers (CROs) and oversee the end-to-end management of investigations and enforcement actions for CRU cases. You will report to the Deputy Director of CRU.
jobResponsibilities:
You will provide operational leadership and oversight for CRU’s investigation and enforcement work, ensuring that cases are managed effectively, consistently and in accordance with established policies and procedures.

Your key responsibilities will include the following:
• Providing direction and supervision to CROs, and ensuring that investigations and enforcement actions are thorough, timely and conducted in accordance with established SOPs.
• Leading engagements with partner agencies, such as HDB, PA, SPF and AIC, to coordinate the effective management of cases.
• Reviewing and clearing CROs’ case submissions, enforcement documents and service replies to ensure their accuracy, quality and compliance with established requirements.
• Providing management with timely updates on case progress, key issues and matters requiring further direction.
• Developing CROs’ capabilities through coaching, appropriate training and regular feedback.

jobResponsibilities:
Perform Digital Forensics examination and analysis into a wide range of devices in support of investigation and prosecution.

  • Conduct thorough digital forensics seizures, preservation and examination of digital evidence from devices, operating systems and/or networks and ensure all forensic processes comply with legal, procedural, and evidentiary standards.
  • Properly identify, collect, label, document, store, and manage digital evidence in accordance with established procedures. Maintain complete chain-of-custody records.
  • Document detailed findings. Provide objective assessment of digital evidence and to recommend appropriate opinion on assessment of evidence to stakeholders.
  • Create comprehensive, court-ready forensic reports and provide expert testimony in court to support investigative teams in evidence presentation.
  • Work closely with investigating officers, legal officers to scope forensic requirements and assist in identifying investigative leads based on digital evidence.

Ensure proper use and maintenance of forensic tools. Ensuring up-to-date SOPs and consistent processes.

  • Manage and maintain forensic laboratory tools, systems, licenses, and inventories.
  • Develop, review and maintain SOPs and investigative processes; recommend and implement process improvements. Support digital evidence handling policies, chain-of-custody protocols and accreditation requirements.

Ensure continuous capability training and development. Keep abreast of emerging technology and threat awareness

  • Keep skills current through training, certification and professional development. Identify training needs and support knowledge transfer within the unit.
  • Contribute to knowledge-sharing, mentoring and training of staff and stakeholders, where appropriate.
  • Monitor developments and identify new trends, stay up-to-date with evolving digital technologies, emerging threats, forensic methods, and legal precedents.
  • Assess implications of new technologies on forensic readiness and investigation approaches.

Establish operational collaboration with other Law Enforcement Agencies, (e.g. Interpol, SPF, HSA, IRAS, CPIB, MOM, CNB, Singapore Customs, and other agencies in DFG).

  • Establish and maintain a network of liaison contacts with other law enforcement agencies to exchange information, best practices, experience and expertise, etc.
  • Collaborate and co-ordinate with other agencies in joint enforcement and investigations, etc.
jobRequirements:
• A background referably in Digital Forensics, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science or any other relevant discipline.
  • Minimum of 2–5 years of professional experience in digital forensics, incident response, or cybersecurity.
  • Proficiency with industry-standard forensic tools such as Cellebrite, Magnet AXIOM, Autopsy/Sleuth Kit, Oxygen Forensic Detective, EnCase, FTK, MSAB XRY etc.
  • Ability to acquire and analyze data from Computers (Windows, macOS, Linux), mobile devices (iOS, Android), cloud environments, network storage, memory dumps, volatile data and IoT devices.

The Health Promotion Board’s vision is to make Singapore a nation of healthier people.

Come be a part of this journey if you’re passionate about creating boundary-pushing work that drives behavioral change.

You will be part of HPB’s Research, Evaluation and Monitoring (REM) division, which drives the development of data-driven insights and analytics to inform health promotion strategies across HPB. The division focuses on translating cutting-edge research and emerging technologies into HPB programmes. By distilling learnings from diverse datasets, applied research, and innovative pilots, REM supports the translation of evidence into practice for delivery in national-scale platforms. The division also plays a key role in strengthening programme design, evaluation, and continuous improvement, ensuring that interventions are evidence-based, outcomes-driven, and relevant for real-world implementation.

As a member of the Analytics and Translation team in the Research, Evaluation and Monitoring division, you will work in a cross-functional, matrix team to contribute to high-impact projects in priority growth areas.


You will generate actionable insights through advanced analytics on diverse datasets (e.g. large longitudinal cohorts, sensors, and combined datasets), applying appropriate statistical and machine learning approaches to support risk prediction, population segmentation, and identification of behavioural patterns.


You will support the development and application of predictive models and segmentation approaches (e.g. clustering) to inform programme targeting, intervention design, and risk stratification, ensuring outputs are robust, interpretable, and relevant for real-world decision-making.


You will set up and support behavioural experiments and programme evaluations, including contributing to study design, data preparation, and analysis to distil research insights and evaluate suitability for translation into programme delivery.


You will develop compelling data-driven narratives for impactful storytelling to both internal and external stakeholders, translating technical findings into clear, concise, and actionable insights that inform programme and policy decisions.


You will work with cross-functional teams and external partners to support collaborations and analytics projects, contributing to delivery of strategic outcomes and facilitating knowledge sharing and learning across teams.

jobDescription:
The operating environment of the Public Service is undergoing fundamental and rapid change. The issues we face are complex and multi-faceted, which impact the way the Public Service operates and organises itself. Internally, the changes in workforce profile has necessitated a new approach in how the workplace is designed, while the pervasiveness of technology has fundamentally changed the way we conduct our business. 

You will be part of the Service Policy and Leadership team in ServiceSG and will report to the Manager (Service Policy and Leadership). 

ServiceSG, a department within PSD, has been set up to champion integrated public service delivery. It works with different agencies across the public service to integrate over 400 services around key moments of life of citizens, and serve citizens in an integrated way, through a central omni-channel service delivery system comprising a digital platform (“LifeSG”), a network of physical service centres at Community Centres and libraries (“Integrated Public Service Centres”) and a central call/contact centre. 

In addition to its core function, ServiceSG also plays a key role in the development of service delivery talents in the domain. This is achieved through various workforce development programmes such as Short-term Immersion Programmes (STIP), GIG programmes, Structured Job Rotations (SJR), and Talent Attachment Programmes (TAP). These programmes are designed to provide officers with exposure to different service delivery environments and equip them with the necessary skills and knowledge to excel in their roles.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Curating progressive, impactful developmental opportunities to level up the workforce capabilities of the Whole-of-Government Service Delivery function and partnering various stakeholders to implement them 

•	Supporting the enhancement of Workforce Development Programmes to achieve operations excellence 

The above learning areas will cut across the initiatives below: 

Short Term Immersion Programmes (STIPs) and Gigs – Short-term development opportunities for public officers to deepen their competencies. STIPs allow officers to gain insights to other agencies’ work and range from half to three days. Gigs require officers to commit 1-1.5 days/week to other public sector projects while staying on top of their core work.   

Talent Attachment Programme (TAP) and Structured Job Rotation (SJR) – Longer-term developmental opportunities that broaden officers’ perspectives and strengthen leadership capabilities through attachments and secondment. TAP develops public officers through attachments of 6 to 12 months in the private sector, while SJR provide developmental secondments to other public agencies, typically lasting 2 to 3 years.  

Public Sector Transformation (PST) Awards – A Whole-of-Government (WOG) pinnacle platform that recognise and reward public officers and agencies for excellence in their work and organisational practices. There are a total of 16 award categories and ServiceSG oversees the administration of two Service Delivery awards. 

[Specific Job Responsibilities]
Support the administration of career development programmes (STIP, Gig, SJR, TAP), PST Awards within the Service Delivery domain, which includes: 
1) Reviewing programme workflows and operational processes, leveraging data and automation to enhance efficiency. 
2) Engaging and coordinating with internal and external stakeholders (such as HR teams, officers, Service Delivery teams and leaders) to ensure the smooth running of the above programmes. 
3) Administering data repository for the above programmes, ensuring accuracy for reporting and analytics capabilities, contributing to strategic talent management decisions and initiatives. 
4) Preparing key reports, presentations, and visualisation dashboards to effectively monitor the efficacy of the development programmes and communicate them to stakeholders.   
5) Planning and generating EDMs (in partnership with PSD Comms) to encourage registrations and curating learning materials for continuous learning. 
6) Collecting, consolidating, and analyzing stakeholder feedback, programmes’ work processes, and data for continuous improvement in programme delivery and workforce development outcomes.

jobDescription:
The Public Service Division (PSD) aims to build a first-class Public Service for a successful and vibrant Singapore. We do this through public sector leadership development, capacity and capability building and the promotion of quality services at all levels of the Public Service. We are looking for outstanding candidates with the vision and passion to contribute to help shape Singapore.

ServiceSG aims to transform the service experience for citizens receiving public services. Our ambition is to transform citizen’s experience of public services from one of having to navigate across different functional agencies to get things done, to an integrated, personalised and seamless one where the public service “Knows and Serve you as one, and with Heart”.  

We work with different agencies across the public service to integrate over 600 services around key moments of life of citizens. Our central omni-channel service delivery system currently comprises a digital platform (“LifeSG”), a network of physical ServiceSG centres and a central contact centre. We are working to join the dots between the government systems and processes to make citizens’ experience smooth, whether online, on the phone, or at our centres.  

The Challenge 

You will join the ServiceSG Insights Practice to turn real-world citizen and service data into actionable recommendations to create a more seamless, personalised, and proactive citizen experience with the Government. Working on analytical projects, you will proactively explore data from channels such as appeals, hotlines, service centres and digital services, identify patterns across citizen archetypes’ end-to-end journey, and develop clear recommendations for service, process and policy improvements. 

You will have the opportunity to experiment responsibly with AI and large language models in the Government’s ecosystem to cluster, classify and summarise large volumes of unstructured text, while learning approaches to review, apply checks, and validate with other data sources. You will also help to improve existing Python- or SQL-based workflows to transform raw data into reliable, analysis-ready datasets and dashboards. This internship is suited to a curious, self-directed learner who enjoys asking good questions, testing new approaches and building practical solutions—and who wants to strengthen an analytics foundation while gaining early exposure to the skills and disciplines used in data engineering.
jobResponsibilities:
By joining our #PeoplePurposePossibilities internship, you will learn by working on meaningful service challenges and gain hands-on experience in: 

•	AI-Assisted Service Analytics and Insight Generation 
- Explore structured and unstructured data from appeals, hotlines, service centres, feedback and digital channels to answer ad hoc business questions and uncover citizen needs. 
- Use statistical methods, text analytics and AI tools to cluster, classify and summarise large datasets, identify emerging themes and generate hypotheses for deeper analysis. 
- Learn to design analytical lenses and categories, test model outputs, and apply human review, sampling and triangulation to produce responsible and defensible insights. 
- Connect patterns across channels and citizen segments to identify service gaps, repeated effort and opportunities for more seamless and inclusive delivery. 

•	Data Preparation, Automation and Engineering Foundations 
- Support the cleaning, joining and transformation of datasets for analysis. 
- Use Python, SQL or similar tools to develop reproducible workflows, automate recurring analytical steps and reduce reliance on manual data preparation. 
- Apply practical data-engineering habits such as clear documentation, modular scripts, version control, quality checks and reusable data structures. 
- Build an understanding of how reliable data pipelines and analysis-ready datasets support dashboards, analytics and AI use cases at scale. 

•	Visualisation, Storytelling and Service Impact 
- Create dashboards and visualisations that make complex findings easy for non-technical stakeholders to understand and act on. 
- Translate analysis into concise narratives, decision-ready presentations and practical recommendations for service, process or policy improvements. 
- Work with colleagues and agency partners to refine questions, validate interpretations and understand how analytical evidence informs real-world service transformation. 

How You Will Grow: You will be encouraged to take initiative, learn unfamiliar tools quickly, seek feedback and progressively own small analytical workstreams. By the end of the internship, you should have a stronger portfolio of applied analytics work, practical experience using AI responsibly, and a clearer foundation for future development in analytics engineering or data engineering.

jobDescription:

As a Software Development Engineer, you will transform complex operational challenges into dependable software, engineer capabilities across the full technology stack, and see your work make a tangible impact on real-world missions.

At DSTA's Command, Control and Communications Development (C3D) Programme Centre, we develop software systems that enable the SAF and government agencies to execute their missions successfully. We are looking for curious, driven and technically strong engineers who enjoy solving complex problems end-to-end, from understanding operational needs and shaping requirements to designing resilient architectures, building software, integrating systems, and validating mission capabilities.

What can the team offer you?

Our Team
Join a multidisciplinary team of developers, architects, product managers and UX designers who are passionate about building meaningful software. Collaborate on high-impact engineering challenges in an environment that values curiosity, technical excellence, rigorous thinking, teamwork and continuous learning.

Career Opportunities
Work across diverse projects ranging from rapid prototyping to operational Command and Control (C2) systems spanning Air, Land, Sea and Whole-of-Government domains. Develop expertise in frontend and backend engineering, GIS, cloud, DevSecOps, data, AI, robotics, cybersecurity, IoT and system integration, while growing into architecture, technical leadership and product-oriented roles. You will be encouraged to take ownership, experiment, share knowledge and collaborate with research and industry partners to transform emerging technologies into operational capabilities.

Professional Development
Benefit from structured onboarding, mentorship, a buddy system and technical training from day one. Through DSTA Academy programmes, industry-led courses, hands-on delivery and peer learning, you will build practical expertise in software engineering, systems engineering, architecture, verification and validation, and responsible use of AI-enabled development tools.

Culture
We believe great software is built by empowered teams. You will have the autonomy to contribute ideas, challenge assumptions, make sound technical decisions and take ownership of outcomes while enjoying a collaborative environment that supports sustainable performance and work-life balance.
jobResponsibilities:

•	Design and build user interfaces, geospatial capabilities, backend services and integration components across web, mobile and thick-client platforms.
•	Plan and execute system integration, verification and testing, troubleshooting issues across software, interfaces, networks and infrastructure to ensure reliable end-to-end operations.
•	Leverage DevSecOps, automation, AI-assisted development and modern engineering practices while maintaining ownership of requirements, architecture, code quality, cybersecurity and testing outcomes.
•	Raise engineering standards through code reviews, design reviews, technical discussions, experimentation and communities of practice while continuously learning and sharing knowledge with fellow engineers.

Software Delivery

Modern Platforms

agencyDescription:
