jobDescription: PRINCIPAL / SENIOR / EXECUTIVE SOFTWARE ENGINEER, SYSTEMS
jobResponsibilities:
Software Engineer, Systems team — Centre for Autonomous Mobility (CAM), Land Transport Authority. You will build the digital products that make safe autonomous vehicle deployments possible in Singapore, at scale. This role is open at two levels — a core set of responsibilities applies to all hires, with additional ownership and leadership expectations for more senior candidates (see section below).

CAM leads Singapore’s national effort to deploy autonomous vehicles (AVs) at scale safely. The Systems team builds the digital tools behind that mission — for instance, developing a monitoring system for AVs to collect and analyse AV operational data to support LTA’s regulatory and safety assurance work. But the role is broader than any single product: wherever software can move AV deployment forward, that is where we will build.

As a software engineer, you will

  • Design and build production-quality digital products end to end: You will be expected to understand and take ownership of problem statements, before designing and architecting systems on cloud infrastructure — owning features from conception through deployment and ongoing maintenance.
  • Build the suite of safety-assurance products LTA needs to regulate AVs reliably: analytics, dashboards and visualisations; implement enforcement and performance tracking, event management and data-anomaly alerts.
  • Identify and address pain points bottlenecking deployment velocity: Work in a tight-knit and cross-functional CAM team, with a clear north-star of driving safe AV deployments at scale — which includes non-passenger vehicles and AVs on public paths (Autonomous Mobile Robots). Talk to users and industry, identify gaps and propose products that move AV deployments forward.
  • Evolve our products to the next bound: Our product portfolio spans several digital products, including the AV Monitoring System that monitors every AV on Singapore’s public roads. We are building for scale so that systems can handle a growing number of AVs and developers amidst evolving needs; strengthening data pipelines and system observability for high-volume telemetry, and potentially integrating with other LTA enterprise platforms for operations and incident management.
  • Keep what we ship healthy: monitor and support production systems that AV operations and regulation depend on, including helping respond to incidents when they arise.

Apply AI, ML and Data Analytics where it adds value

AI is increasingly central to how we build and what our products do. You can expect to apply it in areas such as:

  • Engineering productivity: Safe use of AI tools, including coding assistants and multi-agent workflows, will be expected.
  • Anomaly and risk detection: Automatically surface unsafe patterns found from AV operational telemetry and video data, so issues are caught earlier before scale.
  • Operational intelligence: Address the pain points faced by operations and regulatory colleagues as deployments scale, through natural-language querying and automated summaries of performance and trends.
  • Deployment and planning: Implement tools and optimisation algorithms to inform demand/supply estimation and deployment feasibility.

Because safety assurance is new ground, you will also

  • Help shape what we build, not just how — identify gaps and propose products that strengthen AV safety and drive AV deployments.
  • Work with policy, operations and regulatory colleagues to turn requirements into working software, and explain technical trade-offs to non-technical audiences.
  • Know when to build versus when to adopt open-source or commercial solutions, so effort goes into delivering real value rather than re-solving solved problems.

If you join as a more senior hire, you will also

  • Lead technical discussions, influence architectural decisions, and own technical direction across products.
  • Establish testing, CI/CD and code-quality practices, and balance pragmatic delivery with long-term technical sustainability.
  • Set engineering best practices, mentor other engineers and support recruitment.

If you want your code to shape how a new technology is adopted safely while driving deployment needs at scale, we want to hear from you.
jobRequirements:
● Knowledge preferably in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field.

●We’re generally language-agnostic and will use the most appropriate tool to solve the problem — core competency in at least one language and the ability to learn matter most. We look for someone who:

  • Can build software end to end, and is strong across the stack — demonstrated through prior work, shipped products or personal projects; what you’ve built matters more than specific degrees. You should be comfortable designing and implementing digital products with maintainable data models.
  • Thinks clearly about systems — data pipelines, APIs, data integrity and authentication, and designing for scale and reliability — making technical decisions that balance performance, maintainability and real-world needs.
  • Listens and communicates well — able to listen and distil issues faced by stakeholders into key problem and/or opportunity statements to devise effective solutions, while being able to clearly explain and obtain buy-in from other engineers and key stakeholders.
  • Takes initiative, has pride in their craft, and cares about the public good — writes tests, cares about code quality, maintainability and correctness. Self-directed and curious in picking up new knowledge, and invested in team success beyond individual contributions. Motivated by the mission of driving safe AV deployments at scale.

Useful, but not essential

  • Experience with data-intensive systems, dashboards and data visualisation, or cloud infrastructure.
  • UI/UX sensibility — experience designing usable interfaces, or working closely with designers to craft intuitive user experiences.
  • Familiarity with our stack — we commonly use JavaScript/TypeScript with some Python, React, cloud services and open-source tooling, on relational databases (SQLite and Postgres). Additional familiarity in working with geospatial data and relevant libraries will be a plus.
  • Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Terraform), CI/CD pipelines, and Agile delivery.
  • Interest in autonomous vehicles, transport planning, generative AI, or safety-critical systems.

  • At least 3-5 years of relevant experience in system project implementation and cybersecurity compliance and/or cybersecurity work experiences in ICT infrastructure or network implementation

agencyDescription:
In Singapore, having the rule of law and advancing people’s access to justice are not just lofty ideals but the backbone of a functioning and a progressive society. At the Ministry of Law, not only do we contribute to developing the legal frameworks and policies that uphold our way of life, but also to providing community legal services that Singaporeans benefit from. The key policies we oversee include Singapore’s legal and intellectual property infrastructure, the civil and criminal justice systems as well as land resources.

Our officers are experts from different fields, and enjoy an excellent and challenging career in a fast-paced environment with plenty of opportunity to grow. If you share our vision of shaping the future of Singapore, you will definitely fit right in here at MinLaw.
jobDescription:
Who we are

The Legal Policy Group (LPG) in the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) plays a critical role in upholding the rule of law, advancing access to justice, and ensuring a sound and progressive legal framework for Singaporeans. 

What the role is

Under LPG, officers at the Civil & Legislative Policy Division (CLPD) do not just review laws — we play an important role in helping to shape the future of legal policy and governance in Singapore. Our team has driven reforms that touch the lives of Singaporeans every day. Some recent initiatives include:

•	Relief for victims of harassment: In 2021, we established the Protection from Harassment Court to give victims of harassment faster, more accessible and affordable relief through simplified court processes. 

•	Modernisation of laws: In 2023, we modernised our laws through legislative reforms that make it possible for statutory declarations, oaths, affirmations, and notarisations to be done through electronic means.

•	Strengthening family therapeutic justice: The Maintenance Enforcement Process (MEP) was introduced in May 2023 under the Family Justice Reform Act to improve the enforcement of maintenance orders, deter non-payment, and improve access to justice for maintenance applicants through efficient enforcement procedures and sustainable outcomes. In 2025, the Maintenance Enforcement Division was established within the Insolvency and Public Trustee's Office to administer the MEP, with Maintenance Enforcement Officers working to achieve these objectives.

•	Enhancing the management of community disputes: In 2024, we worked closely with the MND and MCCY on enhancements to our Community Disputes Management Framework. The enhancements strengthen our community mediation framework and court processes to address neighbour disputes. Government agencies also worked together to introduce a Community Relations Unit that has powers to intervene in and address serious neighbour disputes.

•	Safer online spaces for Singaporeans: In November 2025, MinLaw and MDDI passed the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act. The Act strengthens online safety and protects Singaporeans from online harms. It empowers victims to seek timely relief and obtain redress through a new Online Safety Commission, and through new statutory torts that provide clear legal basis for victims of online harms to take action against those responsible for such harms. 

We are a small, multidisciplinary team that values thoughtful debate, moves with gumption, and is unafraid of breaking the mould. Officers will have the space to challenge assumptions and propose new ideas.

This role is ideal for someone who is passionate about making a difference, thrives on intellectual challenge, and enjoys working collaboratively in a dynamic environment — and who wants their work to have tangible, national-level impact.
jobResponsibilities:
You will join us in a variety of ongoing and upcoming policy reviews and reforms for the policy areas set out below:

•	Lead legal reform: Work with fellow officers to review laws, propose reforms and pursue new initiatives, tackling both classic and frontier issues. These include civil, family, and community justice issues, access to justice, criminal law and procedure, and more. If you ever wanted to rewrite the rulebook (legally, of course), this is your chance.

•	Drive change, turn ideas into reality: Turn complex policy challenges into tangible solutions that improve real lives — take legislation from idea to Parliament, collaborating with legislative drafters, experts, and stakeholders. Become the bridge between policy vision and practical reality.

•	Engage stakeholders: Work with stakeholders and partners to develop creative, practical solutions to issues of national significance. 

•	Drive implementation: Take an active role in implementing policy initiatives —assist with drafting subsidiary legislation, provide policy inputs on operations, and ensure that sound policy design together translates into practical execution.
jobRequirements:

•	[Excellent writing skills] Able to crystallise core issues through clear and concise writing
•	[Deep critical thinking] A sharp and analytical mind capable of distilling critical issues and sense-making from a wide range of information to arrive at effective policy solutions
•	[Domain-specific expertise] Have familiarity with law reform work and/or regulatory frameworks; develop domain knowledge to collaborate and/or co-create policy solutions with experts and professionals

agencyDescription:
About the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore 
Established in 2015, the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) seeks to keep Singapore’s cyberspace safe and secure to underpin our Nation Security, power a Digital Economy and protect our Digital Way of Life. It maintains an oversight of national cybersecurity functions and works with sector leads to protect Singapore’s Critical Information Infrastructure. CSA also engages with various stakeholders to heighten cyber security awareness, build a vibrant cybersecurity ecosystem supported by a robust workforce, pursue international partnerships and drive regional cybersecurity capacity building programmes. CSA is part of the Prime Minister’s Office and is managed by the Ministry of Digital Development and Information. For more news and information, please visit www.csa.gov.sg
jobDescription:
Singapore’s push for digitalization coupled with cyber threats that are ever evolving in scale and sophistication paved the way for a continuously growing demand for cybersecurity professionals. As a result, there exists a need to strengthen the pipeline of skilled cybersecurity professionals through identifying and empowering individuals with cybersecurity aptitude and good learning attitude to take on cybersecurity roles. 

CSA’s Cybersecurity Development Programme (CSDP) is a 12-month programme designed to develop both fresh graduates and working professionals into cybersecurity talents in the public sector, with the aim of building cybersecurity capabilities to secure Singapore’s digital economy and infrastructure.
jobResponsibilities:
CSDP is a 12-month programme that consists of two phases: a 1-month classroom training phase, followed by an 11-month job posting.*

*Please note that the programme curriculum may be subject to change (including programme duration/training curriculum, etc). The programme stated below is accurate as of August 2026.

Phase 1: Classroom Training

CSDP officers will undergo a rigorous curriculum in their first month to build both technical and professional capabilities. Officers will undergo courses that will lead to cybersecurity certifications such as:

•	SANS SEC504
•	SANS ICS310
•	Cisco Certified CyberOps Associate

Officers will also receive training in professional skills such as Stakeholder Management and Effective Writing in the Public Service.

Phase 2: Job Posting

After the classroom training phase, CSDP officers will be posted to a CSA division or partner government agency for the remaining 11 months. During their posting, officers will gain hands-on experience in mainly one of these cybersecurity domains:

•	Malware Analysis
•	Digital Forensics & Incident Response
•	Emerging Technologies
•	Penetration Testing
•	Cybersecurity Solutions and Consultancy
•	Cybersecurity Operations Centre
•	Threat Intelligence
•	Governance, Risk and Compliance

Job postings will take into consideration each candidate’s interests, suitability and cybersecurity manpower needs across the Whole-of-Government (WOG). Further assessments may be required to determine a candidate’s suitability for specific roles, and the final posting decision rests with CSA.

Gain Exposure Beyond Your Posting

Throughout the programme, CSDP officers will have opportunities to work on cybersecurity projects at the national level, undergo further technical and non-technical training, and engage with recognised industry partners and the public.

These experiences will enable officers to broaden their cybersecurity expertise, develop valuable professional networks and contribute towards strengthening Singapore’s cybersecurity posture.

Upon successful completion of the 12-month programme, CSDP officers may continue their employment with CSA or be forward deployed to another government agency, subject to satisfactory performance and successful matching to a suitable role across the Whole-of-Government (WOG).

CSA is currently located at the Punggol Digital District.

Looking for a job that actually makes a difference?

The job holder will play an important role in shaping the next generation of health promotion by distilling learnings and insights research, rich data and novel technologies, and translating these into actionable recommendations that inform the development of population‑scale digital health interventions. This includes leading the research and development of health interventions that integrate behavioural science, emerging technologies (including generative AI), and population‑scale digital platforms.

The jobholder will drive and manage high impact projects in priority growth areas by:

  • Distilling complexity across data, behavioural insights, user research and implementation constraints into clear, decision‑ready narratives (in writing and slides) for diverse stakeholders

  • Incorporating behavioural insights in the setup, design, testing and review of human-centric user experiences and digital health interventions

  • Managing the digital product cycle, including ideation, design and execution of feasibility trials, outcome evaluation, and translation of learnings into deployment‑ready insights and recommendations. This includes leading and coordinating a multidisciplinary tech squad (product, engineering, data, design) to support rapid experimentation, prototyping and evaluation of generative AI‑enabled coaching and personalisation concepts.

  • Working with cross-functional teams comprising subject matter experts, data scientists, deployment teams and practitioners to develop innovative and practicable solutions

  • Demonstrating value to citizens in developed solution through quantifiable outputs and outcomes, and developing compelling narratives to convince and secure buy-in from internal and external stakeholders

Required Skills and Competencies:

  • Ability to adopt big picture thinking and distil clarity from complex problems

  • Ability to synthesise insights across multiple, partially‑formed research and product workstreams into coherent decision narratives

  • Ability to connect disparate signals across policy, technology, behavioural science and on‑the‑ground implementation for convergence into solutioning and problem solving

  • Comfortable acting as an integrator across research, technology and policy rather than a depth specialist in a single domain

  • Familiarity with behavioural insights and design thinking

  • Comfortable managing complexity and ambiguity in a fast-paced environment

  • Strong sense of intellectual curiosity and openness to new ideas

  • Demonstrated ability to quickly build working knowledge in new and emerging health or technology domains

  • Strong project management skills to support research, experimentation and cross‑functional coordination

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with ability to engage a wide range of audience

  • Comfortable as an individual contributor or leading a team
jobRequirements:
• Good degree in any discipline

  • At least 8 years of total relevant working experience with 5 years of practical experience overseeing and/or managing end-to-end projects including stakeholder management and 3 years of experience leading cross-functional or multidisciplinary teams to oversee development and implementation of end-to-end product cycles or multi-year projects

  • Practical ground experience and proven track record in applying behavioural insights, with familiarity in design thinking approaches to inform intervention design and testing

  • Prior experience working in the field of public health, health care, health sciences, research or quantitative domains will be an added bonus

  • Experience working with AI‑enabled or data‑driven digital products (including generative AI) is a strong advantage

While this role works closely with AI technologies and tech teams, it remains fundamentally a research‑ and insight‑driven role focused on learning, synthesis and translation, with deployment as an outcome of evidence rather than a starting point.

o Plan and secure resources to ensure our community-based care programmes are accessible and have sufficient capacity to meet future demand.
o Assess the adequacy and effectiveness of existing policies and initiatives to address the needs, challenges, and aspirations of caregivers of PwDs.

Beyond domestic activities, the CDA aims to expand Singapore’s global outreach and foster collaboration with international partners.

We also strive to shape Singapore into a world-class city of knowledge, culture and excellence – one which keeps pace with global challenges and the rising aspirations of Singaporeans.

An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City

Develop World-Class Infrastructure

Build Rooted and Cohesive Communities
MND will strive to foster our citizens' attachment and love for our homeland and maintain social cohesiveness in our communities, even as Singapore continues to be an open and globalised society.

jobResponsibilities:
•	Integrate Fragmented Data: Combine data from diverse sources— OSINT, technical metadata, and specialised feeds
•	Separate Signal from Noise: Filter through large volumes of messy, conflicting information by asking the right questions, and discerning the relevant picture from unrelated noise
•	Map Networks: Map out complex networks of entities and operational infrastructures, and create clear pictures from a large web of disparate clues
•	Tell the Story Behind the Data: Translate complex technical data and convoluted investigative trails into clear and concise executive briefs to provide early warning and strategic support for Singapore's policymakers
•	Build & Innovate: Develop new investigative tools, and refine analytical workflows to keep our team ahead of emerging risks

•	Unmatched Purpose: Contribute directly to the safety, stability, and sovereignty of Singapore
•	Culture of Continuous Learning: We invest heavily in professional training, including advanced OSINT, data analytics, foreign languages, and cutting-edge investigative methods
•	High-Calibre Teams: Work alongside passionate, like-minded analysts, data experts, and domain experts who love what they do
jobRequirements:
•	Singapore Citizens only

We are looking for individuals with an investigative mindset who are able to find clarity in ambiguity and turn fragmented data into clear answers. You would possess the creativity to:
•	Hunt for missing pieces: Develop mastery of the information landscape and know where to find additional data sources when the current picture is incomplete
•	Slice and dice data: Approach data with clear questions to ensure your analysis is relevant, looking for patterns that others miss
•	Connect the dots: Turn disjointed or weak signals into a coherent narrative of “how things fit together”

We will provide the tradecraft training; you bring the curiosity. Your job isn’t to know all the answers today, but to have the drive to uncover them. Desired qualities and attributes include:
•	Keen interest in geopolitical, threat or security-related developments
•	Strong investigative, analytical, and problem-solving skills
•	Willingness to apply new tools and technologies to derive insights from information
•	Interest in mastering a foreign language and culture
•	Both detail-oriented and able to zoom out to see the big picture
•	Strong interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence
•	Strong communication skills
•	Motivated team player and an independent self-starter

•	Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI): Analysts who track threat actors, malware campaigns, or digital indicators
•	Financial Crime & Fraud Investigations: Specialists who follow paper trails, map suspicious transactions, and uncover hidden entity relationships

•	Language Expertise: Mastery of a foreign language

Debt Repayment Scheme Role

a) Assess debtor's application to be placed under the Debt Repayment Scheme (“DRS”)
b) Examine documents submitted by the debtor and verify extent of debtor's assets and liabilities.
c) Conduct meeting of creditors to determine debtor’s repayment plan.
d) Handle both general and case-specific enquiries from debtors and creditors
e) Assist DRS officers to review cases for cessation of the debt repayment plans (completion, failure or inapplicable for DRS)  

Adjudication Role

a) Examine the validity of claims filed by creditors.
b) Correspond with creditors, solicitors and/or bankrupts on request for additional information and/or further documentary evidence in support of the claims filed against the bankruptcy estate – may include resolving disputes between creditors and bankrupts which arise in the adjudication of the Proof of Debt.

Established in 2001, the Health Promotion Board’s (HPB) vision is to build a nation of healthy people.

We aim to empower residents in Singapore to attain optimal health, increase the quality and years of healthy life, and prevent illnesses, disability and premature death.

To achieve this, HPB drives national health promotion and disease prevention programmes, spearheads health education initiatives and creates a supportive environment in Singapore where healthy lifestyle options are available and accessible for healthy living every day.
jobDescription:
Overview of the Chief Data Officer Office (CDOO)
Advance the data-driven, evidence-based and citizen-centric approach to health promotion through state-of-the-art data best practices to maximize data quality and internationally-recognised governance and policies to promote safe usage of data.

Overview of Data Operations & Architecture Department

Recognising the efficacy of big data and artificial intelligence in optimising sharper insights and outcomes for public health, the Data Operations and Architecture Department will take a proactive role to drive the design of a 360-view citizen-centric data architecture and the implementation of data operations to support and facilitate an evidence-based, data-driven approach to programme delivery. The department will set up and implement data architecture and structuring, cleaning and validation of big data from diverse HPB and partners’ data sources (e.g. food transaction data, sports attendance data, screening and sensor data) to facilitate data feature engineering use cases pivotal to downstream data exploitation. The department will also be involved in strategic collaborations with partners (e.g. public healthcare and data science institutions, academics and technology players) to bring in their data and expertise onto the data operations to benefit citizens.

We are looking for dynamic and enthusiastic individuals, with strong data engineering and data science skills and project delivery experience, to join us on this pioneering journey to build a more data-driven HPB. You will be pivotal in helping to set up and implement a robust data engineering pipeline that can integrate the vast wealth of data HPB has through its numerous data sources. A robust data pipeline ensures that changes from the data sources does not impact the timely delivery of high quality data to our business users.

Given the diversity of data collected from our lifestyle programmes, data science approaches such as machine learning will also be deployed to support the data engineering process. For example, we have build and included machine learning ops to help with standardising event names.

Responsibilities

  • Design optimal data structures for strategic datasets and drive data engineering processes related to data ingestion, data imputation, data transformation and integration to facilitate data science and analytics use cases
  • Build optimised, test driven codes to achieve the above mentioned
  • Translate research and analytics questions into data features to facilitate dashboarding, model training, analytics, and data science applications
  • Build test case on code to ensure that all codes are built to perfection
  • Project manage and be the overall lead for engagement to bring together HPB vendors, partners, IT and business teams to plan, set timelines and drive processes that enable timely delivery of the data engineering pipeline guided by business needs
  • Lead internal cross-functional teams to integrate, process and engineer disparate datasets into structured and meaningful variables to facilitate machine learning and data science use cases
  • Lead the preparation of materials to update senior management periodically on progress of the project and surface issues and challenges for collective deliberation and decision-making

Qualifications and skillsets

  • Bachelor/Masters degree in Computer Science, Engineering or Information Systems with major / project experience in data science and/or business analytics from a recognised university. Professional certifications in data engineering from accredited professional bodies will be highly desirable.
  • Minimum 3-5 years of relevant project management and delivery experience. Experience in end-to-end deployment of data engineering projects in production environment preferred.
  • Proficiency in the use of Python and/or Power BI
  • Experience working on data engineering, and/or database architectural work
  • Experience working on a few of the following component in the data pipeline: data ETL, data cleaning, data modelling, and feature engineering.
  • Able to work in a fast-paced matrix environment, overseeing multiple projects at the same time
  • Good communication skills and able to communicate and express complex data/concepts in a clear and simple-to-understand manner
  • Have the drive, commitment, and perseverance to do well and have strong intellectual curiosity to learn and seek continuous improvements in the work assigned
  • Experience in Big Data technologies e.g. Hadoop and Spark Ecosystems will be desirable
  • Experience with test-driven development will be desirable
  • Take an interest in digital health and healthcare

The Public Service values the experiences of mid-career entrants outside of the Public Service and is interested to groom talents with the heart to serve. The Singapore Department of Statistics is the National Statistical Authority responsible for statistics on the Singapore economy and population.

We collect, compile, analyse and disseminate a wide range of economic, business, household and population data, as well as analyse and monitor trends in the economy and population.

With these vital inputs, policymakers, business decision makers and our data users gain valuable insights into current and emerging economic and social trends, enabling them to make calculated and informed decisions in the formulation of policies and strategies for the future. Apart from public agencies and businesses, our users also include researchers, analysts, educators, students, the media and the general public.

Join our team and make a difference by contributing important statistical input to facilitate policy planning and decision-making and support Singapore's present and future economic and social development.

• Good communication and presentation skills
• Able to work well both independently and as a member of a team

This job advertisement does not have a fixed closing date as DOS recruits Statistician on a year-round basis.

•	DOS offers attractive and market competitive benefits which include mid-year & year-end variable payments and market adjustment component.

jobDescription:
Energy security is an existential issue for Singapore. With the growing climate imperative, a global energy transition shifting to low-carbon fuels is underway. At the same time, geopolitical pressures are causing significant stresses in energy markets, leading to risks of supply disruptions and significant price volatility.

The energy transition will be especially challenging for Singapore, given our scarce natural resources and limited renewable energy options. One of Singapore’s biggest challenges over the next few decades is to secure a low-carbon energy supply that is reliable and cost-competitive. The future of Singapore’s energy landscape depends on our ability to harness four switches – natural gas, solar, electricity imports, and low-carbon solutions such as hydrogen, ammonia and carbon capture and storage.
jobResponsibilities:
METI’s Energy and Carbon (E&C) Cluster leads initiatives to reduce emissions and drive the transition to a low-carbon economy, while ensuring energy security and cost-competitiveness, and enabling Singapore to sustain economic growth. Officers in this cluster develop energy and carbon markets, plan energy infrastructure, build Singapore’s capabilities to harness low-carbon energy sources, and manage emission trajectories and carbon budgets. You will collaborate with stakeholders across Government, industry, and international partners to support sustainable economic transformation and green growth through strategic planning, policy analysis, and partnerships.

The Low-Carbon Energy division within the E&C Cluster takes the lead in:
• Developing, implementing and monitoring various alternative energy sources for Singapore, including solar, hydrogen in its various forms, bioenergy, geothermal energy, as well as other promising low-carbon technologies.
• Devising new policies to ensure that new energy solutions can be productively deployed and scaled sufficiently to help meet our 2050 net zero goals.
• Overseeing issues relating to energy, grid, storage and carbon transformation Research & Development in Singapore. This could also entail the development of new climate technology pilot funding scheme, working directly with global climate tech solution providers, academics, and investors.

Your responsibilities may include one or more of the following workstreams:
• Develop strategies and policies to support the implementation of the Singapore National Hydrogen Strategy (published in October 2022), with a focus on:
- Development of commercial industry projects to develop hydrogen supply chains in Singapore
- Long-term infrastructure and land planning
- Competitive monitoring
- Advancement of international collaboration to leverage like-minded partners’ efforts to advance regional hydrogen supply chains and interoperable standards and regulations
- Facilitate collaborations across key stakeholders, involving Government agencies, industry players, academia and international counterparts as appropriate

• Engage with new energy and decarbonization-focused companies and funds to track, monitor and make relevant recommendations with regards to the latest developments in the climate technology realm
• Develop and implement communications and engagement plans with regard to Singapore’s alternative energy policies
• Monitor developments in global energy landscape and analyse implications for domestic energy policies to enable these developments

agency: Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry
agencyDescription:
Working at METI places you at the heart of Singapore’s economic policy-making. We drive productivity-led growth, safeguard and expand our economic space, and build a future-ready economy where firms can thrive. Together, we create a Singapore which is a city of possibilities, a home to great firms, and a place where the world connects — with people at its heart.

When you join METI, you contribute to our mission of creating good jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans, enabling them to improve their lives and secure a better future.
jobDescription:
By joining the Energy Partnerships Division at METI, you will become part of a critical and urgent mission: to support Singapore’s energy transition by securing low-carbon electricity imports from our region and building an interconnected regional grid. Low-carbon electricity imports are one of Singapore’s ‘Four Switches’, alongside natural gas, solar, and low-carbon solutions such as hydrogen, ammonia, and carbon capture and storage.

The climate crisis requires us to quickly transition to low-carbon energy sources to avoid the devastating impact of rising temperatures. Decarbonising our power sector, which contributes 40% of current emissions, is key to realising Singapore’s commitment to achieving net zero emissions by 2050.

Even as we take steps to secure a low-carbon energy supply, we will also need to safeguard our energy security and affordability. Navigating the energy trilemma successfully will be one of the defining policy challenges of our generation and hold far-reaching implications for our economy and society.

In 2027, Singapore will take on the ASEAN Chairmanship. For the energy sectoral track, this will be an important opportunity to advance regional cooperation and drive progress on energy connectivity through the ASEAN Power Grid (APG).
jobResponsibilities:
METI’s Energy and Carbon (E&C) Cluster leads initiatives to reduce emissions and drive the transition to a low-carbon economy, while ensuring energy security and cost-competitiveness, and enabling Singapore to sustain economic growth. Officers in this cluster develop energy and carbon markets, plan energy infrastructure, build Singapore’s capabilities to harness low-carbon energy sources, and manage emission trajectories and carbon budgets. You will collaborate with stakeholders across Government, industry, and international partners to support sustainable economic transformation and green growth through strategic planning, policy analysis, and partnerships.

The Energy Partnerships Division within the E&C cluster formulates Singapore’s energy policies and strategies, together with the Energy Market Authority, other Government agencies, academics, and private sector stakeholders.

The Energy Partnerships Division takes the lead in:
• Driving Singapore’s efforts to import and deploy renewable energy from the region to realise target to import around 6GW of low-carbon electricity by 2035 to decarbonise our power system.
• Advancing energy collaboration with like-minded countries, international organisations, and think tanks to support Singapore and the region’s energy transition and energy resilience, and advocate for the APG.

Your responsibilities include one or more of the following workstreams:

• Drive G2G engagements, including through visits, working groups, dialogues, and instruments of collaboration such as agreements and memoranda of understanding, to advance the realisation of cross-border electricity trading projects.
• Develop policies and strategies to advance the financing of cross-border power transmission infrastructure; the manufacturing, deployment and protection of subsea power cables; and the recognition of cross-border Renewable Energy Certificates to support the implementation of cross-border electricity imports projects.
• Develop and strengthen partnerships with international thought leaders such as the International Energy Agency (IEA), International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), Multilateral Development Banks, as well as local partners such as the Energy Studies Institute and Asia Competitiveness Institute.
• Foster collaborations with like-minded partners at:
(1) Local events such as Singapore International Energy Week (SIEW)
(2) Multilateral international platforms such as ASEAN Ministers on Energy Meeting (AMEM), G20, and Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC).

Develop World-Class Infrastructure

Provide Affordable and Accessible Public Housing
MND will commit to support Singaporeans' homeownership aspirations and ensure public housing remains affordable and accessible.

Build Rooted and Cohesive Communities
MND will strive to foster our citizens' attachment and love for our homeland and maintain social cohesiveness in our communities, even as Singapore continues to be an open and globalised society.

You will go beyond conventional project management to critically examine and improve the built environment at existing MRT stations. Working alongside a multidisciplinary team, you will identify and drive meaningful improvements across our rail network — translating insights into built outcomes that serve our commuters for decades to come.

As part of the Station Rejuvenation Design team, you will design manage consultants to develop preliminary designs that meet the requirements of both internal and external stakeholders, while devising strategies to address overcrowding and enhance station accessibility and vibrancy.

jobTitle: Assistant Director/Senior Assistant Director (Family Policy), FCD/FEC
agency: Ministry Of Social And Family Development
agencyDescription:
Join Us at MSF for a Meaningful, People-Centric Career!

At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. We offer meaningful and impactful people-centric careers in the design and delivery of policies, services and programmes. We are an all-inclusive and family friendly workplace where career growth is prioritised through a comprehensive suite of development opportunities to help our officers succeed today as well as be future-ready. We do this through various formal and informal learning and development programmes for officers to build different competencies and gain diverse work experiences within MSF, the Public as well as the Social Service Sectors.
jobDescription: The Family & Early Childhood (FEC) division sits under the Family and Child Development (FCD) Policy Directorate. The FEC division formulates and reviews policies that promote and strengthen families, in support of MSF’s macro outcomes to support marriage and parenthood actualisation and build strong and resilient marriages and families.
jobResponsibilities:
Families are the bedrock of Singapore society. As Assistant Director (Family Policy), you will shape the policies and strategies that help Singaporeans build strong, resilient families — from supporting marriage and parenthood to ensuring that every child gets a good start in life, and that families are supported to care for elderly members with dignity.
You will lead a team of policy officers across three broad areas of work.

Strengthening Family Ties and Support Structures You will review and develop policies that promote strong family relationships across all life stages, with a particular focus on ensuring that elderly persons are well-supported by their families as they age. This includes identifying gaps in existing frameworks and working with MSF's Family Life Group (FLG) to translate policies into effective programmes and services on the ground.

Strengthening Safeguards for Vulnerable Persons You will lead the review of the Mental Capacity Act and related policies, including those governing professional donees and deputyship, to ensure the legislative framework keeps pace with evolving needs and adequately protects persons who lack mental capacity. You will also drive efforts to encourage Singaporeans, especially the elderly, to plan ahead through instruments such as the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), reviewing policies and strategies to improve awareness and uptake.

Funding and Legislative Review You will review MSF's funding approach for family services to ensure support is well-directed and fiscally sustainable, and lead reviews of key legislation including the Women's Charter, Mental Capacity Act, and Child Development Co-Savings Act to keep them aligned with policy objectives.
Throughout all of this, you will work closely with FLG, NPTD and other stakeholders to implement, monitor, and continuously refine your policies based on evidence and ground feedback.
jobRequirements:
•	Good analytical, written and communication skills 
•	Ability to propose and build support for evidence-based policies and solutions to address multi-faceted issues and perspectives
•	Good interpersonal and stakeholder management skills

jobTitle: Assistant Director, Policy & Strategy Development (2-year contract)

To achieve this, HPB drives national health promotion and disease prevention programmes, spearheads health education initiatives and creates a supportive environment in Singapore where healthy lifestyle options are available and accessible for healthy living every day.

jobDescription:
We are seeking a versatile and forward-thinking Development Engineer/Specialist to join our team in advancing the boundaries of Physical and Embodied AI. In this role, you will bridge the gap between intelligent software and the physical world, transforming AI models into tangible, autonomous capabilities. You will design, prototype, and deploy AI-enabled physical systems—such as robotics, unmanned platforms, and smart automation solutions—utilizing ROS2.0.
You will also act as a bridge between technology, industry partners, and academia, fostering ecosystem growth through knowledge sharing, mentoring student projects, and leading live innovation showcases. If you are passionate about applied research, hands-on hardware-software integration, and inspiring others, we want to hear from you.
jobResponsibilities:
1. Physical & Embodied AI Development
• System Design & Prototyping: Design, develop, and prototype intelligent physical systems, robotics, and advanced automation platforms leveraging ROS2.0.
• Hardware-Software Integration: Integration of advanced AI models, computer vision, and operational systems with sensors, actuators, edge devices, and embedded systems.
• Applied Research & Piloting: Drive feasibility studies and pilot programs involving AI-enabled automation, unmanned systems (UAVs/AGVs), and smart monitoring solutions.
• End-to-End Project Support: Manage the full lifecycle of applied research and proof-of-concept initiatives, including data preparation, rigorous experimentation, performance evaluation, comprehensive documentation, and post-deployment technical support.
• Prototype Commercialization: Assist in translating high-potential AI prototypes into scalable, deployable, or licensable industry solutions.
2. Knowledge Sharing & Ecosystem Enablement
• Educational Mentorship: Support curriculum development and actively mentor student capstone and research projects in robotics and applied AI domains.
• Stakeholder Collaboration: Partner closely with internal researchers and external industry stakeholders on collaborative innovation initiatives.
• Technology Advocacy: Lead and support engaging AI and robotics demonstrations for lab visits, innovation showcases, and executive partner engagements.
• Use Case Curation: Synthesize and curate compelling physical AI use cases to engage, educate, and inspire both academic and industrial audiences.
jobRequirements:
• Qualification in Robotics Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical/Electronic Engineering, Mechatronics, or a closely related quantitative field.
• Robotics Architecture: Proven hands-on experience developing with ROS2 (Robot Operating System). Familiarity with robotic arms and humanoid robots, robot kinematics, dynamics, and simulation tools (e.g., Gazebo, Isaac Sim) is highly valued.
• AI & Computer Vision Integration: Practical experience deploying Machine Learning/Deep Learning models (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) and computer vision frameworks (e.g., OpenCV) onto physical platforms.
• Embedded Software Engineering: Proficiency in C++ and Python, with strong software development best practices (Git, clean architecture, code reviews).
• Hardware & Edge Systems: Experience working with microcontrollers and single-board computers (e.g., NVIDIA Jetson, Raspberry Pi). Solid understanding of hardware communication protocols (I2C, SPI, UART, CAN bus) and sensor fusion (LiDAR, IMUs, cameras).

Soft Skills & Core Attributes
• Collaborative Mindset: Exceptional interpersonal skills with a proven ability to collaborate effectively across diverse teams of engineers, researchers, students, and corporate partners.
• Communication & Presentation: Confident and articulate presenter capable of breaking down complex technical concepts into accessible demonstrations for non-technical audiences.
• Passion in Educational Mentorship: Guiding student learning journeys and contributing to educational frameworks.
• Adaptability: A thriving curiosity for ambiguous, fast-paced R&D environments where troubleshooting physical hardware requires creative problem-solving.

jobDescription:
The Asia Tech x Programme Office (ATxPO) sits within IMDA's International (INTL) Group and manages Asia Tech x Singapore (ATxSG), Singapore's flagship technology event platform that convenes change-makers and thought leaders from government and industry to explore how technology can create meaningful impact.

INTL amplifies Singapore's influence and presence in the global digital economy, enabling the nation to transcend its physical limitations and emerge as a bigger red dot on the international stage. The Group focuses on building robust relationships with countries worldwide and lays essential groundwork for the next phase of development in ASEAN's
digital economy. Through its comprehensive approach to international engagement, INTL creates opportunities for Singapore to capture greater value and strengthen its position in the rapidly evolving digital landscape.

As Assistant Director for Programming and Content, you will lead the team responsible for conceptualising, developing and executing the ATxSummit and ATxInspire series. You will also collaborate with IMDA's industry partner Informa Tech to advance the broader ATxSG agenda, including B2B opportunities through the ATxEnterprise brand.

In this role, you play a central part in shaping the core experience of ATxSummit. Your team drives the development of strategic themes, crafts thought-provoking agendas, and designs engaging sessions that inspire insight and action. You will curate and guide speakers to ensure every session is relevant and impactful. Beyond the main plenary, you will coordinate fringe activities and partner-led programmes to deliver a cohesive and memorable experience across the ATxSG ecosystem. Working closely with internal divisions, senior leadership and global partners, you will help advance Singapore's digital leadership on the world stage.

What You Will Be Exposed To
This role offers a unique vantage point on the issues and actors shaping the global digital economy. You will engage with thought leaders from government and industry, locally and internationally, as well as leading technology companies, research institutions and academia working on next-frontier technologies. Internally, you will work across multiple IMDA divisions and with inter-agency partners, building a broad understanding of Singapore's digital economy priorities.
jobResponsibilities:
You will lead and manage a team to develop and execute the programme, content, partnerships and sponsorships for ATxSG across two key areas:

Programme and Content

You will lead the programming and execution of the agenda for the ATxSummit (Plenary and Village) and ATxInspire series, developing content strategies for panels and sessions in close collaboration with internal and external stakeholders. This includes identifying, engaging and cultivating government and industry speakers, and applying a data-driven approach to programme development and execution.

Sponsorships and Partnerships

You will drive the development and execution of knowledge and event partnerships, serving as the key point of contact for strategic partners including government agencies and key industry organisations. This includes sourcing, developing and executing sponsorship arrangements with industry partners to grow ATxSG as a platform.

You should be a self-motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and is energised by complexity and ambiguity. agencyDescription:
The Ministry of Health’s (MOH) vision is to champion a healthy nation with our people – to live well, live long and with peace of mind. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.
jobDescription:
Shape Singapore’s Health at the National Level

Are you a medical doctor looking to make an impact beyond a clinical setting? Whether you are a junior doctor exploring your career options, or an established clinician contemplating new challenges to contribute at the national level, consider a career at the Ministry of Health (MOH).

Under the MOH Medical Service Scheme employment, you will bring your clinical lens and expertise to national healthcare policies and influence decisions that shape the health of Singapore. You will work at the intersection of medicine and policy to design the healthcare systems and frameworks that aim to improve the health outcomes for the nation, and be part of the national health leadership. 

You will be working in a fast-paced environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time. This is a role for doctors who are energised by complexity, motivated by purpose, and ready to drive healthcare transformation at a national scale.
jobResponsibilities:
You will contribute across four key domain areas:

•	Healthcare Regulation — Safeguarding standards and ensuring the safety, quality, and integrity of Singapore's healthcare system.
•	Manpower Development & Capability Building — Shaping the pipeline and professional development of Singapore's healthcare workforce.
•	Population Health & Health Services — Designing and delivering health programmes and services that keep Singaporeans healthy across their life course.
•	Quality, Value & Informatics — Driving innovation, data-driven decision making, and value in healthcare delivery.

At more senior levels, you may also lead and manage a team.

As part of your development, you may also be rotated to other public sector agencies and organisations within the broader healthcare ecosystem — such as the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Health Promotion Board (HPB), Communicable Diseases Agency (CDA), or the public healthcare clusters. Your postings will be carefully designed to broaden your exposure and deepen your understanding of how policy translates into operations on the ground, equipping you with a well-rounded perspective to grow and contribute meaningfully throughout your career with MOH. 

While you will mostly be involved in healthcare policy work, you may also continue with sessional clinical practice, if you prefer, at the public healthcare institutions, so that you can maintain your clinical currency and familiarity with ground operations.
jobRequirements:
We welcome applications from medical doctors who are registered with the Singapore Medical Council (SMC) and remain in good standing. Beyond your medical qualifications, we are looking for doctors who embody the following:

•	Collaborative Spirit: You work effectively in multidisciplinary teams and are energised by cross-agency initiatives that drive system-wide change.
•	Critical Thinking: You bring your medical perspectives to bear on complex policy questions, evaluating evidence rigorously to inform national healthcare decisions.
•	Capacity for Change: You are adaptable and responsive to evolving health priorities, emerging challenges, and shifting policy landscapes.
•	Commitment to Continuous Learning: You are passionate about growing beyond clinical practice — into the domains of healthcare policy, regulation, and population health strategy.
•	Compassion: You connect with diverse stakeholders with empathy, and understand how policy decisions translate into real outcomes for real people.

We are also looking for doctors who demonstrate strength in systems thinking — the ability to understand complex healthcare ecosystems as a whole— as well as strategic thinking and the leadership capacity to inspire and guide teams through transformation.

jobDescription:

An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City

Develop World-Class Infrastructure

You will join the core team behind the Phoenix LLM – a family of Sovereign AI models trained right here in Singapore. We are an ambitious and dynamic team of Applied AI Scientists building state-of-the-art Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) from the ground up.

In this role, you will have the unique opportunity to push the frontier of Sovereign AI while collaborating on joint Applied R&D projects with global AI labs. You will have access to large GPU clusters for distributed AI training

jobResponsibilities:
About the role:
•	Design and implement scalable architectures for pre-training and post-training large-scale LLMs and LMMs on distributed GPU clusters
•	Architect data curation pipelines, including data curation and synthetic data generation, for textual and multimodal training datasets
•	Develop custom evaluation metrics and automated pipelines to assess model performance and alignment
•	Leverage SLURM for efficient job scheduling and compute resource management in high-performance computing environments
•	Implement advanced model optimisation techniques, including mixed-precision training and model parallelism 
•	Partner with cross-functional teams to integrate foundational models into agentic workflows and downstream applications
•	Co-author research publications and collaborate closely with academic and industry partners to push the frontier of Sovereign AI

You may specialise in one or more areas in the team:
•	Data: Build scalable data curation pipelines for large-scale textual, multimodal, and agentic training datasets. Perform data ablations, build synthetic generation engines, and design novel curation techniques
•	Training: Build robust distributed training pipelines. Run pre-training and post-training (e.g., SFT, DPO, GRPO) experiments for LLMs / LMMs, and design large scale Reinforcement Learning frameworks for agentic model development
•	Evaluation: Design custom LLM/LMM evaluation metrics. Build and integrate continuous evaluation pipelines into the training framework for testing model checkpoints
•	Alignment and Constitution: Develop frameworks for model alignment and safety. Research scalable oversight, constitutional AI, and preference tuning methodologies to align agentic models with human intent
•	Science: Drive foundational research on emerging topics, such as domain adaptation, language transfer, efficient AI architectures, and constitutional agentic AI
jobRequirements:
You may be a good fit if you:

You will be a part of HPB’s Healthy Ageing Programmes which strives to help seniors lead healthier and longer lives by improving and maintaining their functional ability through healthy lifestyle practices and social connectedness. With transformation to the healthcare and the aged care system brought about by national directives such as Healthier SG and Age Well SG, HPB will need to foster closer collaborations with other parts of the healthcare system including General Practitioners (GPs), Active Ageing Centres (AACs) and Regional Health Systems (RHSes) to encourage seniors to participate in active ageing initiatives, adopt and sustain healthy habits on their own and stay healthy and active.

This will include working with partners to develop and operationalise meaningful volunteer opportunities that enable seniors to conduct community-based AAPs across Active Ageing Centres (AACs) nationwide, and progressively building capability of AACs to independently design, implement and sustain physical activity initiatives of their own.

You will support the development of practical training curriculum, learning resources and implementation guides for senior volunteers to be equipped with the skills and confidence to support volunteer-led low-barrier physical activities like brisk walking activities and simple exercise workouts. The training approach will be informed by the competencies required for various volunteer opportunities and designed to accommodate the diverse backgrounds and capabilities of senior volunteers, ensuring they are implementable by seniors with varying levels of experience.

You will collaborate with stakeholders like AACs, local Institutes of Higher Learning (IHL) and Regional Health Clusters — to co-develop volunteer opportunities and access capability requirements to support the implementation of volunteer-led programmes in the community, aligned with national senior volunteering initiatives and roll out plans. You will also work with partners to identify future capability needs and implementation models that would enable AACs to independently recruit, train and deploy volunteer-led physical activity programmes.

You will contribute to capability development efforts by translating policy intent into practical and meaningful volunteer opportunities in the community, whilst enabling AACs and community partners with capabilities to independently design and sustain physical activity initiatives. Through this, you will support HPB’s mission to extend healthy life years through national directives under Age Well SG and Healthier SG, enabling residents to age-in-place and enjoy better quality of life.

jobDescription:
We're looking for accounting professionals who are genuinely curious about where the profession is heading - not necessarily experts in AI or blockchain, but people who recognise these technologies matter and want to understand why.

You'll join a team exploring what accounting education looks like when automation handles the bookkeeping, AI flags anomalies, and blockchain creates immutable audit trails. Your role isn't to have all the answers - it's to help students develop the accounting judgment that matters more when technology handles the technical execution.

If you've found yourself wondering which accounting tasks will still require human expertise in five years, or if you've started experimenting with AI tools in your own practice and discovered both their potential and their limitations, you already have the mindset we're building on.
jobResponsibilities:
• Teaching accounting fundamentals with an eye toward their application in technology-enabled environments. You'll help students understand why accounting principles matter, not just how to apply them manually—because manual application increasingly isn't what employers need.
  • Designing learning experiences where students use emerging technologies (AI, data analytics tools, automation platforms) as part of their accounting work, discovering through practice when these tools help and when human judgment remains essential.
  • Supervising student projects that explore technology applications in accounting contexts. You'll guide students through ambiguous problems where the answer isn't in a textbook—projects that require both accounting knowledge and willingness to experiment with unfamiliar tools.
  • Collaborating with industry partners on initiatives that explore digital transformation in accounting practice. This is learning alongside students and colleagues, not lecturing from established expertise.
  • Coaching diverse learners across Pre-Employment Training (PET) and Continuing Education & Training (CET) programmes - from school leavers building foundations to experienced accountants updating their skills for changing practice environments.
  • Engaging in curriculum development that keeps pace with professional evolution. You'll work with colleagues to determine which traditional content remains essential and where emerging capabilities should reshape what we teach.
  • Contributing to outreach and student development activities that connect classroom learning with professional practice and performing academic and administrative duties as required.
jobRequirements:
• Accounting Credentials: Relevant qualification in Accountancy with professional certification (or progress toward certification) from recognised accounting bodies such as ISCA, ACCA, CPA Australia, or equivalent.
  • Professional Experience: Substantive work experience in accounting contexts - financial accounting, assurance, internal controls, cost accounting, or related areas.
  • Technology Curiosity: You don't need to be a data scientist or blockchain developer, but you should be genuinely interested in how technology is reshaping accounting work. Perhaps you've:
    • Started experimenting with AI tools for accounting tasks and discovered interesting limitations
    • Wondered which parts of your current role could be automated and which couldn't
    • Found yourself in conversations about RPA, data analytics, or emerging technologies and wanted to understand more
    • Recognised that "this is how we've always done it" increasingly isn't sufficient justification
  • Learning Orientation: Comfortable navigating ambiguity and learning alongside students rather than having to be the expert in everything. When faced with unfamiliar technology, your instinct is curiosity rather than resistance.
  • Teaching Capability: Ability to explain complex accounting concepts clearly and make connections between theory and practice. This might be formal teaching experience, training colleagues, or helping others understand accounting implications in business contexts.
  • Digital Comfort: Proficient with digital tools for productivity and communication. If you've explored tools like Power BI, UiPath, or AI platforms, that's valuable—but more important is willingness to engage with new technologies as they emerge.
  • Communication Skills: Ability to work effectively with young adults, adult learners, industry partners, and academic colleagues. You can translate between accounting language and everyday understanding.
  • Collaborative Mindset: Enthusiasm for working with colleagues exploring similar questions about accounting education's future, and with industry partners navigating their own digital transformation journeys.

jobTitle: Deputy/Assistant Director, Payments Development, Scheme & Governance (Contract)
agencyDescription: MAS is the central bank of Singapore. Our mission is to promote sustained non-inflationary economic growth, and a sound and progressive financial centre.
jobDescription: You will be part of a dynamic team driving the next generation of digital payment solutions and enhancements to Singapore's national payment schemes. Through policy and scheme governance and infrastructure projects with the industry, you will help anchor Singapore's position as a global payments hub.
jobResponsibilities:
You will work at the centre of Singapore's national payments policy, scheme governance, and infrastructure — shaping how Singapore pays locally and across borders:

  • Shape the rules and architecture of Singapore's national payment schemes — You will work on the establishment of Singapore Payments Network (SPaN), the single entity consolidating the governance and administration of schemes such as PayNow, FAST and SGQR. This includes developing risk and governance frameworks and refining scheme rules. In practice, this means consulting key stakeholders such as industry working groups, banks and payment service providers, and translating policy intent into operational scheme requirements that the ecosystem can implement.

  • Contribute to a significant chapter in Singapore's payments evolution — The PayNow Generation 2 project is exploring enhancements that will improve how consumers, merchants, businesses, and government agencies pay and receive payments. You will work on initiatives spanning PayNow-NETS QR interoperability, deep-linking within PayNow QR codes for smoother online checkout, larger-value public sector PayNow transactions, and expanded payment capabilities such as request-to-pay, structured data fields for automated reconciliation, and a micropayments rail.

  • Help shape Singapore's approach to the future of payments — AI-driven commerce is beginning to reshape how payments are initiated globally. Singapore is taking a deliberate approach to this shift: laying the groundwork for these capabilities while putting the right governance, consumer safeguards, and scheme rules in place first. You will contribute to frameworks, scheme rule amendments and pilot designs to explore how Singapore's national payment rails can best harness agentic payments.

  • Drive scheme initiatives from policy to implementation — You will manage end-to-end delivery of payment scheme projects. A significant part of this is stakeholder management: aligning banks, payment service providers, and merchants on scheme changes (e.g. bringing acquirers and issuers around a common QR interoperability standard), and resolving competing commercial and policy interests to reach outcomes that work for the ecosystem.
jobRequirements:
Education and Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Technology, or a related discipline

Experience

  • Experience in payments, financial services, fintech, or a related field — whether in a bank, payment service provider, scheme operator, or regulator

  • Hands-on exposure to payment scheme operations, product development, policy, or infrastructure projects is advantageous

  • Familiarity with instant payment systems, QR payment schemes, or cross-border payment corridors is a plus

Knowledge and Skills

  • Strong understanding of local and global payments landscape, financial technology and infrastructure, and banking industry trends would be an advantage

  • Ability to translate complex technical and commercial payment concepts into clear policy positions, scheme rules, and stakeholder communications

  • Strong written communication skills — you will be writing policy papers, briefing senior leadership, and engaging external stakeholders regularly

  • Proven stakeholder management skills, with the ability to engage and influence across technical teams, senior leadership, and external industry participants

Attributes

  • Comfortable operating with autonomy and owning outcomes, while working collaboratively within a broader team

  • Intellectually curious about where payments are heading — you follow global developments, form views, and bring them to the table

  • Motivated by public impact: you want the work you do to matter to the people and businesses that use Singapore's payment system every day

  • Able to navigate the rigour of a regulatory environment, while maintaining a drive and commercial instinct on par with the industry

You will be working in a fast-paced environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and needs of stakeholders, as well as the agility to respond to changes and developments. agencyDescription:

To achieve this, HPB drives national health promotion and disease prevention programmes, spearheads health education initiatives and creates a supportive environment in Singapore where healthy lifestyle options are available and accessible for healthy living every day.
jobDescription:
The Health Promotion Board’s vision is to make Singapore a nation of healthier people.
Come be a part of this journey if you’re passionate about creating boundary-pushing work that drives behavioral change.

You will be a part of HPB’s Healthy Ageing Programme Department, which strives to help seniors aged 60 years and over to improve and maintain their functional ability through healthy lifestyle practices and increase the quality and years of healthy life. As Singapore’s healthcare and aged care systems transform under national directives such as Healthier SG and Age Well SG, HPB drives the national implementation of the Active Ageing Programme (AAP) strategy in close collaboration with Active Ageing Centres (AACs), Regional Health Systems (RHSes), and whole-of-government agencies to initiate, encourage and empower seniors to adopt and sustain healthy habits, and age well independently in the community.
jobResponsibilities:
As a key member of the Healthy Ageing Programmes Department, you will lead the creation of new physical activity programmes addressing critical gap areas in seniors health, particularly falls prevention, while developing accessible entry-level programmes for inactive seniors.

You will work closely with clinical experts and healthcare clusters to spearhead new programme creation in National Frailty Strategy gap areas, developing robust protocols, implementation guidelines, and screening tools for at-risk seniors.

You will adapt and integrate training content to align with national standards and guidelines.

You will establish comprehensive safety protocols and conduct pilot studies to validate programme effectiveness, designing measurement tools to track participant progress and programme impact for continuous improvement.

You will ensure all programmes meet clinical excellence standards while remaining practical and scalable for community implementation across diverse settings.
jobRequirements:
An ideal candidate will be a dynamic and self-motivated individual with at least 3 years of working experience in programme development or design. Experience within healthcare organizations, training or research institutions, or public health agencies is preferred. The candidate should also possess:

  • A Bachelor's degree in public health-related domains, with relevant certifications in programme design/development, or programme evaluation is preferred.
  • Knowledge of healthy ageing, falls prevention, frailty management, and evidence-based exercise prescription would be beneficial.
  • Able to execute health programme development, pilot study implementation, and safety protocol establishment.
  • Strong analytical capabilities with ability to design measurement tools and validate programme effectiveness.
  • Results-driven with ability to translate research into practical community programmes.
  • Self-directed, comfortable with working across multi-disciplinary clinical and community environments in fast-moving situations.

Successful candidates will be offered a 1-year contract
