jobTitle: Manager/Senior Manager (Systems Governance & Operations Policy), SIR/CCPO
agency: Ministry Of Social And Family Development
agencyDescription:
Join Us at MSF for a Meaningful, People-Centric Career!

At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. We offer meaningful and impactful people-centric careers in the design and delivery of policies, services and programmes. We are an all-inclusive and family friendly workplace where career growth is prioritised through a comprehensive suite of development opportunities to help our officers succeed today as well as be future-ready. We do this through various formal and informal learning and development programmes for officers to build different competencies and gain diverse work experiences within MSF, the Public as well as the Social Service Sectors.
jobDescription:
Within the Strategy, International & Research (SIR) Directorate, the Systems Governance & Operations Policy (SGP) Branch under the CaseCentral Product Office (CCPO) is responsible for establishing robust governance frameworks, operational policies, and ICT system enablers that underpin MSF's frontline social service delivery.

CaseCentral is a case management platform, which aims to empower caseworkers from the social service sector to deliver holistic, coordinated, and efficient support – driving better client and family outcomes. This role plays a critical part in ensuring the system is well-governed, operationally ready, and continuously improved to meet evolving service delivery needs.

You will support ops policy development and governance to change management, stakeholder engagement, inter-agency coordination, and product operations. Working at the intersection of policy, operations, and technology, you will partner closely with internal teams, social service agencies, and ICT stakeholders. You may also be required to supervise and guide contract, temporary, or junior staff, providing day-to-day direction and quality assurance, as well as contribute to the team's capability building through knowledge sharing, coaching peers, and supporting a learning culture.
jobResponsibilities:
1. Governance and Ops Policy Framework Development
•	Co-develop or support the review of ops policies, governance frameworks, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure CaseCentral operates within MSF's and Whole-of-Government (WOG) Information Management (IM) and data governance standards.
•	Translate policy intent into clear, implementable operational workflows and process documentation.
•	Proactively identify governance gaps and propose solutions to strengthen accountability and compliance across the system lifecycle.

2. System Change Governance and Prioritisation
•	Manage the end-to-end intake, assessment, and prioritisation of system enhancement requests from business owners and operational stakeholders.
•	Facilitate structured stakeholder discussions to surface needs, resolve competing priorities, and build alignment across divisions and agencies.
•	Ensure policy and operational decisions are systematically documented to support traceability, auditability and governance oversight.

3. Operationalisation and Implementation Readiness
•	Develop and refine onboarding frameworks, rollout playbooks, and SOPs to prepare agencies and users for system transitions.
•	Support data migration planning and system transition and handover activities, coordinating across technical, operational, and business teams.
•	Conduct pre-go-live risk assessments and develop mitigation plans to ensure smooth operational launches with minimal service disruption.

4. Change Management and Stakeholder Engagement 
•	Design and execute change management (CM) strategies that address people, process, and technology dimensions for CaseCentral rollouts and enhancements.
•	Build, sustain and coordinate Change Champion networks across agencies to embed ownership, drive adoption, and enable peer-to-peer support.
•	Plan, coordinate and support communications, briefings, training, and engagement sessions tailored to diverse stakeholder groups.
•	Gather systematic user feedback through surveys, focus groups, and operational reviews; synthesise insights to inform product roadmap and system improvements.

5. Cross-Agency Coordination and Data Sharing
•	Develop, operationalise and maintain the consent framework to facilitate data sharing between MSF and partner agencies.
•	Advise on data governance considerations, including data standards and flows, to support interface and integration planning across CaseCentral and partner systems.

6. System Operations and Product Operations Management
•	Oversee or manage issue triage, escalation workflows, and resolution tracking to ensure timely and effective response to operational incidents.
•	Support system performance monitoring and service review processes, working with ICT partners to maintain service levels.
•	Identify recurring operational pain points and recommend systemic improvements to enhance system reliability and user experience.

7. Documentation and Knowledge Management 
•	Develop and maintain comprehensive SOPs, user guides, process maps, and governance documentation to support consistent system operations.
•	Establish and maintain knowledge transfer frameworks to ensure institutional knowledge is preserved and accessible across teams.

8. Project and Implementation Coordination
•	Contribute to project planning, milestone tracking, and delivery coordination across workstreams involving CaseCentral and related systems.
•	Manage project risks and issues, ensuring compliance with MSF and whole-of-government project governance frameworks.
jobRequirements:
•	Strong systems thinking with the ability to connect policy intent, operational realities, and technology enablers.
•	Analytical and structured, with a disciplined approach to problem framing, documentation, and decision-making.
•	Strong stakeholder engagement skills — able to communicate with clarity and influence across diverse audiences, from frontline workers to senior management.
•	Collaborative, adaptable, and comfortable operating in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment with competing priorities.
•	Proactive self-starter with a high degree of initiative and ownership over assigned workstreams.

Qualifications and Experience
•	Relevant qualifications in any discipline. Candidates with backgrounds in Public Policy, Social Sciences, Business, Information Systems, or related fields are welcome.
•	At least 3–5 years of relevant experience in policy development, operations management, change management, or ICT governance — preferably in a public sector or social services context.
•	Experience working with case management systems, social service platforms, or government ICT projects is an advantage.
•	Familiarity with WOG governance frameworks, IM8, or data governance practices is a plus.

Only shortlisted candidates will be notified within 4 weeks from the closing date of this position.

Established in 2001, the Health Promotion Board’s (HPB) vision is to build a nation of healthy people.

To achieve this, HPB drives national health promotion and disease prevention programmes, spearheads health education initiatives and creates a supportive environment in Singapore where healthy lifestyle options are available and accessible for healthy living every day.
jobDescription:
The Health Promotion Board’s vision is to make Singapore a nation of healthier people.

Come be a part of this journey if you’re passionate about creating boundary-pushing work that drives behavioral change.

You will be part of HPB’s Integrated Outreach team, which aims to create a Health Living Environment (HLE) where we make healthy living as part of every day life in Singapore. We aim to do so by place making, activating communities and empowering community leaders to play a role in health promotion. This transformative project shifts HPB's role from traditional programme provider to community enabler, embedding health promotion into citizens' lived environments across entire neighbourhoods. We are seeking a dynamic and strategic Manager/Senior Manager to spearhead community activation and drive sustainable behavioural change together with healthcare cluster (SingHealth, National University Hospital Systems, National Healthcare Group) and other community partners at the town level.
jobResponsibilities:
As a core member of the HLE initiative, you will be responsible for operationalising an innovative approach to community health that reaches the unreached and transforms neighbourhoods into health-promoting ecosystems. This role represents HPB's strategic pivot towards citizen-centric, place-based health interventions that integrate clinical care with lifestyle support anchored in local communities. You will develop skills in translating data insights into clear strategies and practical actions, data storytelling, stakeholder engagement and negotiation, project management, and cross-agency coordination.

Key Responsibilities

Regional Roll out and Coordination of HLE

  • Support the rollout of the HLE initiative within the assigned region(s), ensuring consistency with national direction while allowing for regional/local adaptations

  • Apply HLE standards (e.g. digital wayfinding standard, engagement playbook, and collaboration manual) during initiative rollout and guide grassroot leaders and community partners (e.g. AACs) in using these resources effectively

  • Utilise community health dashboards and local data insights to empower grassroots and community leaders in identifying priority health needs and co-creating targeted interventions that address specific neighbourhood health gaps

  • Coordinate and support HLE implementation, including meeting facilitation and general project management tasks

Stakeholder Partnership and Capability Building

  • Work with grassroot advisors/leaders, clusters, and community partners to co-create and coordinate neighbourhood-level activities and strengthen community-led health agendas, building community ownership and optimising community spaces into vibrant, health-promoting environments

  • Deliver training sessions and provide practical support to grassroot leaders and community partners (e.g. AACs) in applying the playbook, message house, menu of actions, wayfinding guides, and dashboards

  • Support the team in collaborating with key healthcare partners in their planning and implementation of regional health promotion activities

Programme Activation and Targeted Outreach

  • Coordinate community and regional health programmes, ensuring they are relevant to residents and responsive to their needs

  • Utilise data to prioritise high-need groups, working with GRAs to apply targeted outreach models, outreach quadrants, and activation toolkits in local contexts

  • Connect residents to healthy living assets and programmes by enlivening the lived environment and the Healthy 365 online-offline resident journey, through local mapping that guides them from discovery to sustained participation.

Monitoring, Feedback and Continuous Improvement

  • Track ground-level progress of HLE initiatives, consolidate feedback from residents, local stakeholders, and share insights with the project team and data teams to strengthen impact measurement

  • Collate, utilise and evaluate data from other sources where required, to create a comprehensive picture of the precinct's health profile and its target segments
jobRequirements:
An ideal candidate will be a collaborative leader with a passion for community health promotion transformation and systems thinking. You should have experience in community engagement, partnership management, or public health programme implementation, with the ability to work effectively across diverse stakeholder groups.

While a degree in a specific field is not mandatory, candidates with backgrounds in business administration/management, public health/public policy/public administration, sociology/psychology, health sciences, communications/media, or related field often possess relevant skills. Trained in project or account management is an added advantage.

The candidate should also possess:

  • A driven and resilient nature; comfortable with challenges and able to work effectively under pressure, both independently and as part of a team

  • Strong collaborative and interpersonal skills with the ability to build rapport with diverse stakeholders

  • Adaptability and the ability to work cohesively in fast-paced teams whilst navigating complex, ambiguous situations positively

  • Analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a result-oriented mindset

  • Comfort working effectively in matrix and highly dynamic team environments

  • Basic data analysis and evaluation capabilities

Successful candidates will be offered a 1-year contract.

jobDescription:

You will be part of a team focused on building technical capabilities for high-level feasibility assessments and the research of infrastructure requirements for advanced nuclear energy systems. You will develop expertise in researching the technical requirements and physical constraints associated with emerging nuclear energy technologies, ensuring that all theoretical frameworks align with international guidelines (e.g., IAEA) and contribute to national land-use efficiency studies.
jobResponsibilities:
What you will be working on:

1. Developing Technical Capabilities for Site Hazard Research

  • Methodology Development: Contribute to the development of technical frameworks for studying site suitability and resilience, including geological, geophysical, geotechnical, and seismological (GGGS) research.

  • Hazard Analysis Research: Assist in developing analytical models to study external natural and human-induced hazards to understand long-term infrastructure resilience.

  • Safety & Security: Nuclear Safety, Security, Safeguards, and Radiation Protection.

  • Lifecycle Management: Nuclear Fuel Cycle and Radioactive Waste Management.

  • Crisis Readiness: Comprehensive Emergency Planning and Preparedness.

3. Infrastructure & Urban Integration Planning

  • Systems Integration Research: Collaborate with relevant agencies to study the physical requirements for integrating advanced nuclear energy facilities into urban environments, including cooling water systems and grid connectivity.

  • Spatial Constraint Mapping: Develop models to understand land-use trade-offs for various technology classes.

  • Civil / Environmental Engineering or Geosciences; Urban Planning.

  • Geology or Geotechnical Engineering;

  • Environmental Science, Marine Biology, or Ecology.

  • Engineering or other related technical fields.

  • Supply chain management

agencyDescription:
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.

•	Employee Welfare benefits

agencyDescription:
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.

agencyDescription:

jobDescription:
The Radiation Protection and Nuclear Science Group in the National Environment Agency (NEA) is the national authority for radiation protection in Singapore and serves to protect the public, radiation workers and the environment from the harmful effects of radiation. Its Nuclear Safety Division is responsible for developing capabilities, plans and ecosystems to support national nuclear safety & security assessment, radiological emergency response, and nuclear regulatory development efforts. The division is also responsible for ensuring that Singapore fulfils its obligations to international conventions and agreements with respect to the safe and peaceful use of nuclear material and technology.

Singapore is studying the potential deployment of nuclear energy as part of its long-term energy strategy. Singapore will also need to prepare for the possibility of nuclear power deployment by other countries in the region. These endeavours involve conducting comprehensive studies and developing technical capabilities with respect to nuclear safety, security and safeguards (3S).

You will be a key member of the team that will play a pivotal role in developing core capabilities necessary to (i) assess the safety and security performance of advanced nuclear energy technologies, (ii) develop drawer plans for 3S requirements, standards and acceptance criteria for a potential nuclear power programme, and (iii) ensure that Singapore adheres to international nuclear 3S obligations.

This is a rare opportunity to be at the forefront of Singapore’s nuclear energy journey.
jobResponsibilities:
Nuclear is a complex and emotive topic, and requires a diverse range of expertise to fully assess its implications for Singapore.

By joining this team, you will have the opportunity to shape Singapore’s nuclear regulatory landscape, collaborate with international experts, and contribute to nuclear safety, security, safeguards and radiation protection capability building efforts domestically and regionally.

Functional Responsibilities

Capability development. As the head of N3SD, you will be responsible for leading a team to conduct studies and build capabilities in the following areas:

  • Safety. Conduct safety analysis, and develop technical competencies to potentially assess, license and inspect nuclear installations; Develop and translate safety criteria into regulatory requirements; and perform regulatory safety studies and reviews for advanced nuclear energy technologies of interest.

  • Security. Develop technical requirements with respect to the security of nuclear materials and installations; and fulfil existing international security obligations. Assess and advance Singapore’s nuclear security-related interests at international, regional (including ASEAN) and bilateral platforms.

  • Safeguards. Develop drawer plans, processes and tools for safeguards enhancements, including building capabilities in safeguards inspections and accountancy; and fulfil existing international safeguards obligations.

Department Management Responsibilities

Department Head. As the Head of the N3SD, you will be required to:

  • Manage overall operations, budget and welfare of the department. This includes planning and allocating resources to fulfil the team’s goals efficiently and effectively.

  • Supervise your teammates to ensure projects are delivered within budget, on schedule and of high standards. This includes planning, implementing and maintaining work processes that would enable the optimum performance of the team.

  • Motivating your teammates and developing the team’s capabilities. This includes (1) developing and communicating professional career development and training plans for teammates, (2) setting clear goals and expectations, (3) engaging, coaching, guiding and providing constructive feedback to encourage personal and professional growth, (4) fostering strong teamwork among teammates and (5) translating management directives and visions into actionable tasks for the team.

jobTitle: SCDF Fire and Rescue Officer (Direct-Entry Lieutenant)
agencyDescription:
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.

GovTech supports various Government Agencies in carrying out ICT delivery services and appoints Agency Chief Information Security Officers (ACISO) to oversee information security management within these agencies. The ACISO is a leadership role that requires technical proficiency demonstrated in multiple cybersecurity domains. The role demands knowledge and/or practical experience in most of the domains below:

  • Cybersecurity Governance frameworks,
  • Security Operations including incident response,
  • Architecture design and threat risk assessment,
  • Security Testing.

The ACISO must possess technical understanding of both on-premises infrastructure security and cloud security architectures across major platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, and GCP), including their native security features, identity management systems, and security control implementations.

[What you will be working on]

Emplaced in public agencies and reporting to the agency’s Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Ministry Family CISO, you will collaborate with various stakeholders (GovTech HQ teams, Agency management, Agency project teams, and outsourced vendors) and will be responsible to:

  • Lead the agency-level cybersecurity function in supporting agency digital transformation initiatives whilst ensuring digital resilience of agency systems.
  • Formulate and implement agency cybersecurity strategies, policies and work plans, ensuring continuous alignment with Ministry Family's business strategic goals
  • Review and enhance risk management through threat-based risk assessments, risk mitigations, risk monitoring and reporting.
  • Provide consultation and endorse risk management and mitigation plans from agency’s project teams.
  • Govern and enhance the agency's security posture by maintaining visibility and oversight of ICT assets, security architectures, and cybersecurity operations code of practices.
  • Develop and maintain incident response plan and playbooks. This involves planning, designing and conduct of security incident response workshops and exercises (table-top exercises, simulation and drills) as well as lead the investigation and management of ICT security incidents.
  • Provide advisory and recommendations on appropriate cybersecurity technologies to be deployed that meets agency’s business requirements and aligned with WOG-wide advisories and practices.
  • Ensure secure by design ICT product development, and that security controls implementations comply with the defined security policies, standards and guidelines.
  • Develop and maintain effective cybersecurity awareness and training programmes


[What we are looking for]

  • Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering or related Technology field
  • At least 8-10 years of management experience related to information security and solid grasp of ICT operations, security policies, business processes and the relationship between them.
  • Ability to work with multi-functional, multi-disciplined teams to formulate, institute real time awareness of security posture and baseline among end users.
  • Good interpersonal and partner/executive leadership skills.
  • Demonstrate knowledge and experience in security by design implementations, review of system architecture, devsecops practices, Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools and securing CI/CD pipelines 
  • Demonstrate understanding of cloud service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), coupled with a strong understanding of core cloud services and modern cloud-native architectures (serverless, containers, microservices)
  • Identify on-premises and cloud-specific cybersecurity risks and threats, demonstrating skills to thoroughly assess their impact and likelihood. This assessment encompasses, but is not limited to, secure configurations, insider threats, vendor risks, data leakage, malwares including ransomware, account hijacking, and compliance risks.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness of existing controls and recommending appropriate mitigation strategies for on-premises and cloud-related cybersecurity and data security issues.
  • Display understanding of emerging threats and technologies, and the ability to translate risk into business impact
  • Strong understanding of compliance requirements and the ability to identify potential violations in on-premises or cloud environments.
  • Able to communicate cyber security topics effectively to senior stakeholders.
  • Minimally possess CISSP certification, preferably with other related certifications, e.g. CISM, CCSP, GCIH that demonstrates continuous learning and knowledge of industry best practices.
  • We believe in being Agile, Bold and Collaborative, and are looking for people who identify with these values.
  • Singaporeans only.

Strategic Architect & Change Catalyst
Transform ambiguous executive visions into strategies that shape Singapore's digital government landscape. You'll be the strategic translator who takes high-level directives from senior leadership and GDT Exco and crafts them into compelling, actionable roadmaps that drive nationwide digital transformation.
Programme Orchestrator for Nation-Scale Initiatives
Lead the strategic orchestration of Singapore's key digital transformation programmes, including the groundbreaking CIO Teams of the Future and Ministry Family Digitalisation Plan. You'll be at the helm of initiatives that reshape how government leverage technology, with direct visibility into their impact across the entire public sector ecosystem.
Cross-Government Collaboration Architect
Design and execute the strategic frameworks that unite Singapore's government agencies in their digital journey. You'll orchestrate cross-divisional planning sessions, craft compelling strategic narratives, and identify breakthrough synergies that amplify transformation impact across the whole-of-government landscape.

Leverage your digital transformation expertise to shape the future of government operations. You'll define meaningful success metrics through OKRs, architect workforce transformation strategies, and chart realistic yet ambitious pathways that push the boundaries of what's possible in digital government.
Leadership Development Champion
Cultivate the next generation of digital transformation leaders by mentoring high-potential Managers and Senior Managers. You'll guide them in strategic thinking, stakeholder mastery, and initiative execution whilst building SPO's capability pipeline for sustained impact.
Senior Stakeholder Influencer & Alliance Builder
Engage directly with Singapore's most senior digital leaders—Cluster Directors and CIOs—to co-create strategies that drive cross-agency transformation. You'll be the strategic bridge-builder who secures buy-in for ambitious initiatives that span the entire government ecosystem.

  • Strategic Thinking: Ability to approach challenges and opportunities with a high-level, analytical mindset—synthesising information, anticipating implications, and developing effective ways of organising work, clarifying accountabilities, and guiding both planned strategies and ad hoc initiatives.
  • Stakeholder Management: Proven ability to identify, engage, and build strong relationships with key stakeholders—both internal and external—while effectively facilitating discussions to foster alignment, trust, and collaboration across all levels.
  • Effective Communication: Good written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to clearly articulate complex ideas, facilitate productive conversations, and deliver impactful presentations to diverse audiences.
  • Collaboration: Strong aptitude for working across divisions and multidisciplinary teams, driving unified efforts and achieving consensus on shared organisational objectives.
  • Leadership & Programme Oversight: Skilled at managing a programme office, coordinating workstreams, and coaching staff
  • Digital Transformation Experience: Understanding of digital transformation challenges, including technology adoption, operational challenges and workforce capability development.
  • Experience: At least 4 years in strategy, planning and/or digital transformation, ideally with exposure to public-sector transformation or enterprise change.

[Learning Opportunities]

  • Develop advanced strategic thinking skills by tackling both planned strategies and ad hoc initiatives, learning how to organise team efforts, clarify roles, and address complex organisational challenges.
  • Enhance stakeholder management abilities by engaging with senior leaders and diverse teams, building proficiency in facilitating discussions and navigating different perspectives to achieve alignment.
  • Refine communication skills through opportunities to lead meetings, deliver presentations, and prepare communication materials for a variety of audiences.
  • Strengthen collaborative skills by participating in and facilitating cross-functional initiatives, fostering synergy and cooperation among multiple stakeholders.

About TradeNet

TradeNet is Singapore’s National Single Window for trade permit processing. It processes over 9 million permit applications annually across import, export and transshipment. As one of Singapore’s key trade systems, TradeNet is being brought in-house to strengthen technology ownership and long-term sustainability.

How we build

Designated as critical IT infrastructure, we favor simple, durable technology choices over the latest trends. We prioritize systems that are easy to reason about, operate, and maintain for the long term.

We operate with high autonomy. Engineers are expected to think deeply, exercise sound judgement, and take ownership of technical decisions. You own the code from technical design through to production. We practice and value honest feedback, practical decision-making and real impact.

We are replacing the decades-old legacy system with a modern, cloud-native platform.The rebuild touches everything: decomposing a monolithic Java/J2EE application into cloud-native services, reconstructing undocumented business logic from incomplete legacy code, clearing compliance and data-governance constraints, and delivering a platform that multiple government agencies depend on daily.

The Chief Architect owns the technical coherence of this effort. You define how the system is structured, how teams interface with each other, and where the hard boundaries are. You work across product squads, TechOps, and programme leadership — but your authority is technical, not managerial.

Teams here use AI-assisted development workflows daily, including LLM/agentic-AI tooling for spec building, code generation, and test automation. You are expected to push the boundaries of what's possible with these tools.

Architecture & technical direction

  • Set the overall system architecture for the TradeNet platform — service decomposition, data architecture, API contracts, infrastructure patterns.
  • Make binding technical decisions across teams. Resolve cross-squad technical disputes. Own the architecture decision record.
  • Design for resilience: fault isolation, blast-radius containment, defensive API contracts, and graceful degradation across a system that cannot go down.
  • Define the architectural guardrails, contracts, and patterns that teams build on — enabling independent delivery without architectural drift.

Legacy modernisation

  • Lead the technical strategy for decomposing and replacing the legacy monolith, including where to strangle, where to rewrite, and where to leave alone.
  • Reconstruct undocumented business logic from incomplete legacy codebases — using source analysis, documentation archaeology, dependency tracing, and AI-assisted reverse-engineering.
  • Navigate compliance and data-governance constraints that shape what can be migrated, how, and when.

Hands-on technical work

  • Write architecture documents, design specs, and technical RFCs that teams implement against.
  • Review code and designs across squads — particularly at integration boundaries and in foundational components.
  • Prototype and prove out critical technical approaches before committing teams to them.
  • Lead root-cause analysis on hard production and programme-level technical problems.

AI-assisted engineering

  • Pioneer and refine AI/LLM-assisted approaches to legacy analysis, code generation, test creation, and documentation.
  • Set the technical standards for how AI-generated output is evaluated, attributed, and held to quality.
  • Push the programme's use of agentic AI beyond basic code completion into architectural and analytical workflows.

Technical leadership

  • Earn trust with engineering teams through technical credibility — you lead by being right and being helpful, not by title. Your authority comes from the quality of your decisions and your willingness to get into the details.
  • Resolve technical disputes across squads. People will disagree on approach, and you are the one who makes the call and gets buy-in from both sides.

The Data Practice drives innovation and sets best practices for the effective and responsible use of data across the Whole-of-Government (WOG). We work at the intersection of data engineering, AI, privacy, and governance - developing standards, platforms, and tools that enable agencies to build high-quality data products and unlock the value of data for public good.

Today, most organisations still struggle with data that is fragmented, inconsistent, and hard to use, alongside AI that is powerful but brittle without strong data foundations, and privacy policies that are difficult to operationalise. We are changing that at a national scale.

Multi-Domain Operational Leadership

jobTitle: Deputy Director, ICT & SS Risk Specialist
jobDescription:

The challenge

What happens when technology, delivery and threats move faster than an organisation’s ability to see and respond to risk?

And what could become possible if risk management moved just as quickly?

Every organisation needs a way to detect warning signs, connect the dots and act before problems spread.

That is the role of governance, risk and control.

Think of it as the organisation’s nervous system. It picks up signals from across the organisation, helps leaders make sense of them and enables a timely response.

When that system works well, teams can move faster, take smarter risks and deliver with greater confidence. When it does not, warning signs are missed, decisions slow down and governance becomes a barrier rather than an enabler.

GovTech has strong platforms, talented people and an important mission. As our role and public impact grow, the risks we manage are becoming more interconnected, fast-moving and consequential.

We are looking for Deputy Directors and Assistant Directors in Enterprise Risk Management who want to help build what comes next.

You will have the opportunity to challenge established practices, experiment with data and AI, influence senior decisions and shape how one of Singapore’s most important technology organisations manages risk.

[What you will be working on]

This is a role for people who want more than a steady portfolio. It is for those who want to build, push boundaries and leave the system better than they found it.

What you will have the chance to change. We want to move enterprise risk management:

  • from periodic reporting to more continuous risk visibility

  • from manual collation to data and AI-enabled insight

  • from risk registers to clearer decisions and action

  • from unclear accountability to risks with active owners

  • from retrospective assurance to earlier intervention

  • from compliance activity to practical support for delivery


This is not simply a reporting role. You will help shape how risk is understood, discussed, owned and acted upon across GovTech.

Your mandate

Your job is to make enterprise risk management useful.

You will work with senior leaders, risk owners and teams across GovTech to identify what matters, make trade-offs visible and support action before issues become incidents.

Depending on your experience and appointment level, you will lead or take ownership of significant ERM portfolios and initiatives.

You will have room to test ideas, challenge established practices and build better approaches. You will also need to influence people you do not manage and create clarity where risks, priorities or accountabilities are contested.

That is part of the job.

Break the Frame

Modern risk management cannot rely only on inherited frameworks, templates and periodic reporting.

We want people who are prepared to question established practices, test better approaches and rethink how risk management should work in a technology organisation.

You will explore how data, AI and automation can help GovTech:

  • detect weak signals and emerging risks earlier

  • connect information across the organisation

  • reduce manual reporting and administrative work

  • give leaders more timely and useful risk insight

  • strengthen judgement without removing human accountability

This requires an experimental mindset. You should be comfortable testing ideas, learning from what does not work and turning successful experiments into practical capabilities.

The aim is not to use AI to perform old processes faster. It is to ask whether those processes are still needed and design better ones where they are not.

We call this Break the Frame: looking beyond established ways of working, pushing boundaries responsibly and building an ERM function that can keep pace with modern technology.

What you will do

Strengthen our ERM approach

Develop and improve GovTech’s enterprise risk framework, methodology and governance arrangements.

Clarify who owns each risk, how issues should be escalated and where decisions should sit.

Make sure the approach works for a modern technology organisation rather than forcing teams into processes that add little value.

Build a forward-looking view of risk

Maintain a current view of GovTech’s key risks across strategy, technology, operations, delivery, vendors, regulation, data, reputation and organisational capability.

Look beyond known issues and past incidents. Identify emerging threats, dependencies and concentrations of risk before they become larger problems.

Keep GovTech’s enterprise risk profile, register and monitoring approach relevant and useful to decision-makers.

Support better leadership decisions

Provide clear and practical advice to senior leadership, Board-level committees, auditors and oversight bodies, including SNDGO and relevant central agencies.

Turn complex risk issues into straightforward choices, trade-offs and recommendations.

Help leaders understand what matters most, what needs to be done, who should act and where attention is required.

Modernise how risk management is done

Improve processes that are too manual, retrospective or disconnected from day-to-day operations.

Use data, AI, automation and emerging technologies to improve the timeliness and quality of risk information.

Run practical experiments, test new approaches and turn successful ideas into reusable capabilities.

Develop tools and guidance that help teams manage risk as part of their work, not as a separate compliance exercise.

Work across GovTech

Partner with product, engineering, cybersecurity, operations, policy, procurement and corporate functions.

Help leaders balance delivery speed, resilience, governance and risk appetite.

Build trusted relationships and support honest conversations, especially where risks or accountabilities are unclear or contested.

Represent GovTech in relevant cross-agency risk and governance forums.


What good looks like

Success will not be measured by the number of reports produced.

You will know the role is making a difference when:

  • leadership has a clearer view of GovTech’s most important risks

  • risks are surfaced earlier and acted on faster

  • ownership and accountability are clear

  • risk insight improves strategic and operational decisions

  • governance supports responsible delivery rather than slowing it down

  • manual reporting is reduced

  • successful experiments lead to better ways of working

  • teams see ERM as a practical partner

  • GovTech is better prepared for disruption and emerging risks

[What we are looking for]

We are looking for people who want to improve how things work, not simply maintain existing processes. You should bring:

  • relevant experience in enterprise risk, governance, assurance or a related field

  • experience in a technology-intensive, operationally complex or regulated organisation

  • a strong understanding of risk appetite, governance, accountability and assurance

  • sound judgement and the confidence to challenge constructively

  • the ability to turn complex issues into clear choices and actions

  • credibility with senior leaders, auditors, regulators and technical teams

  • experience influencing across organisational boundaries

  • curiosity about how data, AI and automation can improve risk management

  • a willingness to experiment, learn and challenge the status quo

Candidates considered for the Deputy Director level should have substantial leadership experience, enterprise-wide influence and the confidence to advise senior leaders and oversight bodies on complex risk matters.

Candidates considered for the Assistant Director level should have strong delivery capability, sound risk judgement and the ability to lead significant portfolios and stakeholder engagements.

What would be useful

Experience or strength in one or more of the following would be valuable:

  • government technology

  • critical digital infrastructure

  • large-scale platforms or digital services

  • technology or operational resilience

  • digital transformation

  • risk analytics, automation or AI-enabled risk management

  • systems thinking, including the ability to see dependencies, feedback loops and second-order effects

  • narrative competence, including the ability to turn complex risk issues into clear and persuasive stories that support decisions


You do not need to tick every box. Relevant experience matters, but so do judgement, curiosity and the ability to make change happen.

  • Drive Shared Technical Victories: Build deep team spirit by establishing peer-review structures, collaborative hackathons, and collective post-operation debriefs. Ensure that a breakthrough by one operator (e.g., a novel C2 bypass or custom malware variant) is celebrated and adopted as a collective win for the entire unit.
  • Foster an Environment of Mutual Respect: Lead with the technical credibility required to earn the respect of deeply analytical engineers, creating a flat, open culture where the best technical argument wins, regardless of hierarchy.
  • Unite Around a Common Adversary: Foster high morale and collective purpose by aligning the team against a clear, shared mission—outsmarting real-world threat actors and securing complex ecosystems through elite, unified offensive tradecraft.

[What you will be working on]

Some problems are easy to walk past. Others keep nagging at you.
Why are we still doing this manually?
Why does sensible policy become painful when it meets the real world?
Why do we discover risks after the fact when the signals were already there?

How should government govern AI systems that increasingly make decisions and take actions for themselves? And why, when technology can change in minutes, does governance sometimes still move in months?

If questions like these bother you enough that you want to get underneath them, experiment with better answers and solve the real-world problem, we should talk.

We are rethinking what modern governance, risk and assurance could look like across GovTech and, ultimately, the wider Singapore Government.

GovTech is where we can design, build, test and learn. The ambition is bigger.

Why this matters

We are modernising Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) so government can use technology and AI with greater confidence, improve services faster, and keep the essential systems people rely on dependable and resilient.

Ultimately, the test is bigger than GRC: Can government use technology better, serve citizens better, and retain their trust when things go wrong?

That is the problem behind this role. And we do not expect to solve it by designing the perfect framework in a room.

We expect to work on real systems, with real users and real constraints. To experiment. Test assumptions. Prototype, understand behavior and incentives. Learn from what does not work.

And turn what does into something that can work at government scale. One role. Multiple archetypes. This is one modern GRC role, not six separate jobs or six career tracks.

The six archetypes below describe different capabilities a Modern GRC Practitioner can develop and create a problem.

You might begin with strength in one. Over time, you can acquire additional archetypes without giving up the ones you already have. An engineer might combine GRC Platform Engineering with Policy Engineering and AI Governance. An assurance practitioner might bring together Threat-Informed Risk Intelligence, Enterprise Risk Management and Systems Architecture. A policy practitioner might combine Policy Engineering with behavioral insights, systems thinking and platform capability.

Which archetypes you draw on depends on the problem. Some practitioners will build deep expertise in one or two. Others will develop a broader combination across several. Neither is a prescribed progression. The archetypes are not boxes to move between. They are capabilities you can accumulate, combine and apply. The ambition is to build practitioners with an increasingly powerful repertoire for understanding and solving difficult problems. Six capabilities you could build and combine.

Make policy work in the real world

Policy Engineering

How do we design policy that survives contact with engineers, users and actual organisational behavior?

Bring together domain expertise, behavioral insights, human-centered design and technology to create controls that people can understand, systems can implement and organisations can actually operate.

A technically correct policy that everyone works around is not a successful policy.

Turn uncertainty into decisions

Enterprise Risk Management

How do we help leaders decide which risks matter, what needs intervention and what we can deliberately live with? Connect signals across the organisation, expose dependencies and concentration risks, translate risk appetite into practical choices and bring better analysis to difficult decisions.

The output is not another register. It is a better decision.

Build assurance into the technology

GRC Platform Engineering

How do we make governance and assurance part of the delivery environment rather than another checkpoint around it? Build Policy-as-Code, automated evidence, continuous control verification and other infrastructure that makes safer behavior easier and assurance more timely.

Sometimes the answer is automation. Sometimes the smarter answer is removing the process first.

Govern systems that increasingly act for themselves

AI & Agentic Governance

What can an AI agent decide? Where must humans intervene? How should decision boundaries, accountability and assurance work when autonomous systems act at scale?

How do we govern model drift, changing behavior and GRC's own use of AI? Some answers exist. Many do not. You could help develop them.

Find the signal before it becomes the incident

Threat-Informed Risk Intelligence

How do we understand what is changing now rather than explain months later what went wrong? Connect cyber, data, resilience, platform, supply-chain and operational signals to identify patterns and emerging risks earlier.

Less: “Did the control pass?” More: “Is it working now, what changed, and what does that tell us?”

See the system everyone else sees in pieces

GRC Systems Architecture

How do policy, risk, controls, evidence, engineering and assurance fit together?

Design the taxonomies, information flows, feedback loops and operating models that allow them to work as one system. Ask some people about one control and they will explain the other three things it affects.

We like those people.

[What we are looking for]

Break the Frame

We are not looking for people to make yesterday's processes 10% faster. We want people willing to ask:

  • Why does this exist?

  • What risk are we actually managing?

  • What evidence says it works?

  • What behavior are we creating?

  • Could technology remove this step?

  • Could we design the problem away?

Sometimes the answer is better policy. Sometimes automation. Sometimes a different operating model. Occasionally, the right answer is to stop doing something altogether.

The expectation is not to challenge everything. It is to know what deserves to be challenged, why, and what should replace it.

What working here may feel like:

  • You will not always inherit a neatly defined problem.

  • Evidence may be incomplete. People may disagree about what is wrong.

  • A process may have existed so long that nobody quite remembers why.

  • Sometimes the problem you were asked to solve will turn out not to be the real problem.

That is part of the work.

Investigate before recommending. Prototype before standardising. Sit with engineers and users before writing policy. Use evidence before forming conclusions. Connect signals that others have not put together. And be willing to change your mind when your first hypothesis is wrong. We consider that progress.

What good looks like

Success is not the number of policies, findings, reports or dashboards produced. We are making progress when:

  • important risks are seen earlier

  • leaders make difficult decisions with better evidence

  • teams encounter fewer unnecessary governance touchpoints

  • policy is easier to understand, implement and verify

  • more assurance comes from live evidence

  • recurring problems are solved at system level

  • safer behavior happens increasingly by design

  • government can adopt AI and emerging technologies with greater confidence

  • governance helps delivery move faster rather than becoming the reason it slows down

And ultimately: Government uses technology better, essential services remain dependable, and citizens experience better public services without sacrificing trust. That is the measure that matters.

Who might find this interesting

There is no single background we are looking for.

You may come from engineering, cybersecurity, risk, assurance, resilience, AI, architecture, digital policy, product delivery, behavioural science, service design, design research, or somewhere less obvious.

Depth matters. But so does what happens when you reach the edge of what you know.

  • Do you get curious?

  • Can you make sense of messy information?

  • Can you work with people who see the problem differently?

  • Can you connect technical, organisational and human factors?

  • Can you turn an idea into something testable?

  • And when something clearly could work better, do you find it difficult to simply walk past?

For some of the problems we are tackling, the answer does not exist yet. That is precisely what makes them worth working on.

This may not be for everyone

If you are looking for a mature playbook, tightly defined boundaries and a portfolio that mainly needs maintaining, there are probably better roles. This work involves ambiguity, experimentation, difficult trade-offs and the occasional failed idea. But if a stubborn problem bothers you enough that you want to understand it, challenge assumptions and build something better, we should probably have a conversation.

Why GovTech

GovTech is in an unusual position. We help shape government technology policy. We build and operate major digital platforms. We can engineer governance and assurance into real delivery environments. We can test ideas against real-world problems and see whether they actually work. And what works here can become capability that benefits the wider Singapore Government.

So, this is not simply a chance to practice GRC differently. It is a chance to help discover what modern governance, risk and assurance needs to become.

Singpass is Singapore’s national digital identity platform, enabling citizens and businesses to securely access digital services across government and the private sector.

As part of Singapore’s critical digital infrastructure, Singpass must remain trusted, resilient and well-governed. As Singpass evolves in scale and complexity, our approach to governance and risk management must evolve alongside it. At Singpass, we believe governance should enable delivery, not slow it down. It should be embedded into how we design, build and operate our products and systems, rather than imposed as a final gate.

We are looking for a Head of Governance & Risk to build and lead this capability.

The Opportunity

This is not a traditional Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) role.

You will lead Singpass’ governance, enterprise risk and operational resilience capability, partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Security and Operations teams to help Singpass move fast with confidence.

Your mission is to ensure Singpass is:

  • Well-governed.
  • Operationally resilient.
  • Continuously audit-ready.
  • Crisis-prepared.

You will champion a shift from reactive compliance to continuous assurance, where governance is embedded into delivery, risks are identified and monitored early, and audit readiness is an outcome of strong daily practices rather than periodic preparation.

You will also help shape the future of governance by using automation, data and AI to modernise how risk, compliance and assurance are managed.

What you will be working on:

1. Governance & Enterprise Risk.

  • Develop and continuously improve Singpass’ governance frameworks, decision rights and enterprise risk management practices..
  • Maintain a holistic view of Singpass’ risk posture across operational, technology, vendor, policy, regulatory, compliance, data, delivery and reputational domains..
  • Ensure risks are identified early, clearly understood, actively managed and owned by the appropriate leaders..
  • Support leadership in making informed decisions where risk, control and delivery priorities must be balanced..

2. Operational Resilience & Crisis Management

  • Lead Singpass’ business continuity, operational resilience and crisis management programmes..
  • Develop and maintain business continuity plans, crisis playbooks, escalation structures and recovery strategies..
  • Plan and conduct crisis simulations and resilience exercises to strengthen organisational readiness..
  • Ensure lessons from incidents and exercises are translated into sustained operational improvements..

3. Continuous Assurance & Governance Transformation

  • Build an organisation that is continuously audit-ready rather than periodically audit-prepared..
  • Establish near-real-time visibility into risks, compliance status and control effectiveness through automation, data and modern tooling..
  • Use AI and emerging technologies to improve risk detection, control monitoring, assurance and operational oversight..
  • Reduce manual processes and recurring compliance effort through automation and reusable controls..

4. Governance Enablement

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Security and Operations teams to embed governance and risk management throughout the product lifecycle..
  • Drive a shift-left approach where governance, controls and compliance requirements are considered from design through operations..
  • Build governance capability through practical guidance, coaching, standards and reusable patterns..
  • Develop a forward-deployed governance model that keeps governance close to delivery while maintaining consistency with GovTech-wide standards

5. Stakeholder Assurance

  • Provide clear and credible governance and risk reporting to senior leadership, auditors, regulators and oversight bodies..
  • Translate complex risk matters into practical options and recommendations for technical and non-technical stakeholders..
  • Build confidence that Singpass is responsibly governed, operationally resilient and managing its risks effectively.

We are looking for a builder who believes that a modern governance and risk team should enable innovation rather than constrain it.

You should have:

  • Significant experience leading governance, enterprise risk, operational resilience or related functions within a technology-driven organisation..
  • Experience working with large-scale digital platforms, critical services or infrastructure..
  • Strong understanding of enterprise governance, risk management, business continuity, crisis management and assurance..
  • The ability to communicate complex governance and risk matters effectively and accurately with executives, engineers, auditors and regulators..
  • Strong judgement and the ability to balance rigour, pragmatism and delivery speed..
  • An interest in modernising governance through automation, data and AI..

Experience in government technology, digital identity, cloud platforms, agile development or continuous compliance will be an advantage.

Why Join Us

This is an opportunity to build a modern governance and risk capability for one of Singapore’s most important digital platforms.

You will do more than write policies or coordinate audits.

You will help redefine how governance is practised by embedding it into everyday delivery, strengthening operational resilience, and enabling Singpass to innovate with confidence while maintaining the trust placed in it by its users and partners.

If you are excited by the opportunity to build the next generation of governance and risk capabilities for critical digital infrastructure, we would like to hear from you.

Government Commercial Cloud (GCC) is a key platform within Singapore Government Technology Stacks that enables government agencies to build and operate digital services on commercial cloud. The GCC Engineering team develops platform automations, landing zones, and security tooling across AWS, Azure, and GCP — serving thousands of government systems and thousands of public officers.

Security at GCC is not a side function — it's core to the platform's value proposition. Government agencies trust GCC to be secure by default.

You are the single named owner of security outcomes across all engineering teams in GCC. You define how security works — the standards, processes, escalation paths, and technical approaches — and drive adoption through influence, not authority. You operate through a Security Champions network: persistent, named engineers in each product team who own security judgment locally, coordinated by you. Your accountability is whether GCC is actually secure — measured through process health, incident response quality, and security posture metrics you define.

This role is part of the organisation's domain leadership structure — you join alongside Engineering Managers as a peer, not as a report to any EM. The Security domain is being stood up fresh. The previous model (centralised security team gatekeeping all decisions) has been retired. You inherit a Champions network in early stages, documented runbooks, and interim coverage from a senior security advisor. Your job is to take it from "interim bridge" to "sustainable, scalable security function."

The domain scope will evolve. Today it centres on the areas listed above — but we expect the role to grow into adjacent areas (AI security, detection engineering) as the organisation's needs develop. Adaptability and willingness to define your own frontier matters more than deep expertise in every area on day one.

Security Architecture & Posture

  • Own the organisation's security posture across all product teams and cloud environments
  • Architect security frameworks that integrate into engineering workflows without creating bottlenecks
  • Design and evolve threat modelling methodologies adapted to the organisation's multi-cloud, multi-tenant context
  • Define escalation paths, severity frameworks, and incident response playbooks
  • Own the relationship with GCSOC, shaping how external security signals translate into internal action
  • Drive security tooling strategy — selecting, configuring, and setting alert thresholds that distinguish signal from noise

Standards & Process Design

  • Define security standards, runbooks, and compliance approaches that teams can self-serve against
  • Design the Security Champions model: training curriculum, forum cadence, escalation criteria, and what "good" looks like for a champion
  • Replace gatekeeping with enablement — move from "security reviews everything" to "teams self-certify against clear criteria, you spot-check and consult"
  • Own security decision records: all posture choices documented, auditable, and transferable
  • Reform compliance processes (e.g. IMR8) to reduce ceremony while maintaining assurance

Cross-Org Influence

  • Drive security adoption across 5-6 engineering teams through the Champions network
  • Run a regular cross-org security forum: shared learning, emerging threats, pattern reviews
  • Consult on high-risk designs and architectural trade-offs when teams escalate
  • Handle genuine security incidents personally, with Champions as informed participants
  • Build security judgment across the engineering organisation — not by centralising decisions, but by raising the floor
  • Serve as the organisation's authoritative security voice on technical matters — advising on vendor evaluations, platform-level policy design, and cross-programme security decisions that require deep domain expertise beyond any single team's scope

Technical Depth

  • Maintain hands-on capability in at least two of: cloud security architecture, application security, supply chain security, detection engineering
  • Evaluate and prototype security tooling; make build-vs-buy recommendations grounded in the org's actual threat model
  • Contribute to or lead security incident post-mortems with root cause analysis that drives systemic improvement
  • Stay current on emerging threats and translate external signals into organisational action

Must-Have

  • Deep security engineering expertise (architecture, not just operations) — you've designed security frameworks, not just followed them
  • Demonstrated ability to influence without authority across multiple engineering teams
  • Experience designing security processes that scale through enablement rather than gatekeeping
  • Strong enough as an engineer to review designs, read code, and earn credibility with senior SWEs
  • Clear, structured communication — you'll write strategies, runbooks, and decision records that outlive you
  • Comfort operating with ambiguity: this role is being stood up for the first time, and you'll shape what it becomes
  • Proficiency in scripting (Python, Bash) and working with APIs — you'll build and review automation, not just specify it
  • Solid understanding of identity, networking, logging, monitoring, and data security in cloud environments

Strong Signals

  • Experience with cloud security across multiple CSPs — ideally hands-on with native security services, not just console-level familiarity
  • Background in both offensive (threat modelling, VAPT, red team) and defensive (SIEM, detection engineering, incident response) security
  • Track record of building security champion or embedded security programs

As a Lead Product Manager, you will shape the strategy and roadmap of the fCMS. This role is not about managing a fixed set of requirements. It is about helping the Judiciary modernise critical systems in a way that delivers value incrementally, reduces delivery risk and creates long-term adaptability. You will help the platform respond to new legislation, policies and judicial processes, while improving the experience of those who use and operate the courts.

Shape the future of justice in Singapore

Justice is one of Singapore's most important public services. Every year, almost 200,000 cases pass through our courts, involving individuals, families, businesses, lawyers and public agencies. Behind every case is someone seeking a fair, timely and accessible resolution.

The Judiciary's transformation into One Judiciary brought together the Supreme Court, State Courts and Family Justice Courts under a shared vision of delivering justice that is trusted, accessible and ready for the future.

Realising this vision requires more than organisational change. It requires rethinking the digital systems, processes and services that underpin how justice is delivered.

The Future Courts Management System (fCMS) is the Judiciary's flagship digital transformation programme, developed in close partnership with GovTech. You will join GovTech's product management community while working deeply with the Judiciary to shape products that support the administration of justice across Singapore's Courts.

This is not simply a like-for-like replacement of legacy systems. It is an opportunity to reimagine how court services should work: making them easier to use, more responsive to changing legislation and policies, and better able to serve everyone who depends on them.

This is a rare opportunity to help shape how justice will be delivered in Singapore for years to come.

In this role, you will:

  • Shape product strategy for fCMS domains, translating Judiciary priorities, user needs, operational complexity and legislative changes into clear roadmaps and measurable outcomes.

  • Work in a product trio with Engineering and Design leads to discover, prioritise and deliver solutions that are valuable, usable, feasible, secure and scalable.

  • Understand users and court operations by working with judges, judicial officers, lawyers, court administrators, partner agencies and members of the public to identify where digital products can make the greatest difference.

  • Deliver value incrementally using modern product and engineering practices that reduce delivery risk, support learning from real usage and avoid big-bang replacement.

  • Shape a secure and adaptable platform that can support evolving court processes, new government policies, integrations, data needs and long-term operational resilience.

  • Build alignment and product capability by communicating product direction clearly, influencing through evidence, and coaching or guiding Product Managers where appropriate.

You'll Thrive in This Role If...

  • You bring clarity to ambiguity — framing complex user, operational, legal and policy problems into clear product opportunities.

  • You think strategically and systemically — understanding how court processes, technology, legislation, data and organisational change connect across One Judiciary.

  • You make thoughtful product trade-offs — balancing user value, operational needs, technical sustainability, security, compliance and delivery risk.

  • You lead through influence — building alignment across senior stakeholders, court operations, legal, policy, design, engineering and technology partners.

  • You are comfortable with modern digital delivery — working with multidisciplinary teams, Agile delivery, cloud platforms, APIs, integrations, enterprise systems, product analytics and secure-by-design practices.

  • You raise the bar for product practice — coaching Product Managers where appropriate, contributing to GovTech's product community and strengthening a culture of discovery, evidence and continuous improvement.

Experience leading complex digital products, platforms or enterprise workflows is important. Experience in government, justice, regulated environments or large-scale transformation programmes will be advantageous, but not essential.

What Success Looks Like

In this role, you will help the Judiciary:

  • Improve access to justice by shaping digital services that are easier to use, more inclusive and better aligned to the needs of court users.

  • Modernise critical court operations by streamlining workflows across courts, case types and user groups.

  • Respond faster to change by enabling new legislation, policies and judicial processes to be implemented more quickly and consistently.

  • Build a resilient, adaptable platform that is secure, scalable and able to evolve with the Judiciary's long-term needs.

  • Strengthen product maturity across fCMS by helping teams make better decisions through discovery, data, outcome measurement and continuous improvement.

Why This Role Is Different

Few product management roles offer the opportunity to redesign digital systems that underpin an entire national institution.

As part of GovTech, you will bring modern product, design and engineering practices to one of the Judiciary's most important transformation programmes. As part of the fCMS, you will help shape how justice is delivered in Singapore — not just by building better technology, but by helping create a Judiciary that is more accessible, more responsive and better prepared for the future.

[What you will be working on]

We are looking for a Forward-Deployed Product Lead to be embedded within the Attorney-General's Chambers to drive the modernisation of case management system

AGC is modernising its case management system, used by every officer and supporting every type of work it handles advisory, litigation, legislative drafting, prosecution and international matters. You will shape the product's direction and lead its delivery.

The platform will help officers:

  • Track their work from intake to completion, with clear status, ownership and links across divisions.

  • Review and clear work products quickly, in the tools they already use every day.

  • See workload and deadlines so supervisors can assign and prioritise with confidence.

  • Find what they need, including precedents and past work, through modern, AI-assisted search.

  • Work with external systems, such as the courts, law enforcement agencies and whole-of-government platforms.

Where you'll work

This is a hybrid, forward-deployed role based at the Attorney-General's Chambers PARKROYAL COLLECTION Pickering.

In this role, you will

  • Own the product strategy and roadmap. Turn AGC's priorities and officers' needs into a sequenced roadmap, and adjust it as evidence comes in.

  • Use metrics to drive product decisions. Define meaningful measures such as turnaround time, officer adoption and reduced manual data entry, and use them to prioritise the roadmap, assess progress and adjust course.

  • Lead the transition off the legacy platform. Plan for old and new systems running side by side, and work with delivery partners so officers can trust the data throughout.

  • Make build, buy and reuse decisions with Engineering and Design, keeping the platform modular and replaceable.

  • Partner with legal and operational leadership across divisions. Understand why processes work the way they do, and propose changes where the process, not the system, is the constraint.

  • Guide and develop the product team. Work closely with and mentor the product managers and product operations staff on the team and help AGC build its own product capability over time.

You'll thrive in this role if...

  • You have taken a legacy system through replacement before. You know the hard parts are running two systems at once, migrating data and winning over reluctant users.

  • You think in platforms, not modules. You would rather solve a common problem once for every division than build it five times.

  • You are comfortable being hands-on. You write the acceptance criteria and sit with users yourself, not only through a team.

  • You earn trust with expert users. You can hold a credible conversation with senior legal officers about how their workflows.

  • You think in outcomes. You start with what problem you are solving and how you will know it is solved.

Experience in legal, justice or other regulated domains is helpful but not essential. We value product judgement and the ability to learn a complex domain over industry background.

What you'll bring

  • 8–12 years of product management experience, including owning a complex platform or enterprise system end to end.

  • Experience/Exposure in replacing or modularising a legacy system incrementally, including data migration.

  • Experience with case management, workflow or document management systems, and with integrating across systems.

  • Experience working with and holding delivery partners and vendors to account.

  • Strong facilitation and stakeholder skills with senior, specialist users.

Bonus points: experience in legal, justice or regulatory tech; exposure to AI-assisted search or information retrieval; familiarity with SharePoint or Microsoft 365 integration.

What success looks like

In your first year, you will have succeeded when:

  • The first release is live and used by officers, and there is evidence it reduced the time and effort involved in their work.

  • The platform is measured by outcomes. Leadership reviews progress through agreed measures, not only milestone dates.

  • The transition is on track. Officers can rely on data across the old and new systems, and there is a credible path to retiring the legacy platform.

  • Shared capabilities are being reused. New releases build on what was built for earlier ones, rather than each division getting its own version.

Why this role is different

This is not a greenfield build. You will be modernising a system that every officer in AGC relies on daily, while their work carries on uninterrupted.

Some problems will need strong new product capabilities. Others will need a process simplified or a policy revisited, and some will need a deliberate decision not to rebuild something at all. The platform and ways of working you establish will shape how AGC's officers work for years to come.
