As a Lead Product Manager, you will hold significant ownership over your product domain, driving it from concept to reality while aligning with the broader programme goals. The role blends deep, hands-on product ownership with leadership of a small and growing team of product managers, working day-to-day alongside agency stakeholders, policy owners, and design and engineering teams.

What you will be working on

Lead Product Manager — Access to Justice & Regulation, Ministry of Law (MLAW)

As Lead Product Manager for Access to Justice and Regulation at the Ministry of Law (MinLaw), you will lead the product strategy and transformation of two of MinLaw's major business verticals.

Your portfolio will span four product domains:

Assess to Justice

  • Legal — helping people who need legal assistance obtain and navigate representation.
  • Community — helping people resolve disputes early and turn legal outcomes into real-world resolution and compliance.

Regulation

  • Licensing — enabling legitimate operators to receive timely permission to operate without compromising regulatory safeguards.
  • Enforcement — helping regulatory teams detect and address risks before they cause serious harm.

Together, these products touch important moments for individuals, businesses and professionals — from seeking legal help and resolving disputes to entering and operating within regulated sectors.

You will help MinLaw rethink how these services should work, organise technology around enduring user problems and policy outcomes, and build the product teams and common capabilities required to deliver them.

In This Role, You Will

  • Own the product strategy across two domains: Access to Justice and Regulation, translating MinLaw's policy outcomes, user needs, operational challenges and technology opportunities into a coherent portfolio direction.
  • Lead and coach Product Managers, giving teams sufficient autonomy to solve their respective problems while ensuring that product strategies reinforce the outcomes of the wider vertical.
  • Define and use outcome measures, establishing meaningful measures of product success and using evidence to understand whether interventions are improving outcomes rather than simply delivering features.
  • Drive the transition from projects to products, establishing enduring ownership and continuous discovery and development instead of treating digitalisation primarily as a sequence of fixed-scope system implementations.
  • Partner deeply with policy and operations, understanding the intent behind legislation, regulation and government programmes while challenging historical processes that unnecessarily constrain user experience or operational effectiveness.
  • Work in close partnership with Engineering and Design leadership, ensuring that product strategy is desirable for users, feasible to build, operationally viable and technically sustainable.
  • Navigate complex product trade-offs, balancing accessibility, regulatory safeguards, policy intent, operational realities, security, cost, delivery risk and long-term sustainability.

You'll Thrive in This Role If...

  • You can lead at multiple levels of abstraction. You are comfortable moving from a conversation about MinLaw's strategic outcomes to a product strategy, an investment decision or a specific user problem — without losing sight of how they connect.
  • You think in portfolios, not just products. You understand that good product leadership sometimes means investing in one product, sharing capabilities across several, consolidating existing solutions or deciding not to build something at all.
  • You are an experienced product leader. You have led complex digital products or platforms and can coach Product Managers rather than needing to personally make every product decision.
  • You bring clarity to ambiguity. You can take complex policy, operational and user problems and turn them into clear product choices that multidisciplinary teams can act on.
  • You think in outcomes rather than systems. You naturally ask what problem we are solving and how we will know whether people's lives or regulatory outcomes have improved, rather than starting with a system, feature or predetermined solution.

Experience in government, legal services, regulation or similarly complex domains is advantageous, but not essential. We value demonstrated product leadership, judgement and the ability to learn complex domains over familiarity with a particular industry.

What Success Looks Like

You will have succeeded when:

  • MinLaw is managing Access to Justice and Regulation as products, not collections of systems and projects. Teams have clear ownership of enduring problems and outcomes, with strategies that persist beyond individual initiatives or technology refreshes.
  • There is evidence that the products are making a difference. Teams have meaningful measures of success and can demonstrate how their work is improving outcomes for the people, businesses and officers who rely on MinLaw's services.
  • MinLaw makes better portfolio choices. Investment decisions are increasingly driven by user and policy outcomes, evidence and strategic priorities — including deliberate decisions about what to build, reuse, consolidate, change or stop.
  • The portfolio becomes simpler over time. Common needs across products and regulatory regimes are solved through shared capabilities and platforms where appropriate, reducing unnecessary duplication and fragmentation.
  • Product teams can respond more quickly to change. New policies and emerging needs can increasingly be addressed by evolving existing products and capabilities rather than starting new technology projects from scratch.

Why This Role Is Different

This role sits at an unusual intersection of product leadership, law, regulation, public policy and technology.

You will not be responsible for a single application or transformation programme.

You will lead product strategy across two major areas of MinLaw's mission and work with multiple Product Managers and multidisciplinary teams to transform how those outcomes are delivered.

Some of the problems will require excellent individual products. Others will require common platforms or capabilities spanning several products. Some may be solved through data or AI. And sometimes the right product decision will be to simplify a process or change an operating model rather than build more technology.

The challenge is to see these connections and make deliberate choices about where product teams and technology can create the greatest public value.

The product portfolio, teams and practices you establish will shape how MinLaw delivers access to justice and regulation for years to come.

This role will lead discovery, strategy and experimentation efforts for a suite of products to rethink how individuals could strengthen their career health, and make better training and career decisions that support their career goals.

  • Develop the product vision, strategy for SWDA’s suite of products for individuals, with buy-in from senior stakeholders.

  • Balance between development of new capabilities, migration of re-usable components, and maintenance of existing tools, while ensuring stakeholder alignment and operational continuity.

AI is being adopted across government at pace — and with that comes real risk. Models hallucinate. Prompts get injected. Outputs can be unsafe. And AI-generated media is getting harder to spot and easier to produce at scale.

We’re looking for a product manager to contribute to our work in making AI safer and more accountable across government. You’ll be part of AssuranceAI — the AI Programme’s function focused on AI behaviour and AI risk — and you’ll own an assigned product area spanning evaluation, runtime safeguards, assurance reporting, and AI manipulation detection.

You’ll work within a team led by a lead product manager, and you’ll be expected to operate with a high degree of independence within your scope. This means getting into the details with engineers and policy teams, translating direction into concrete requirements, and seeing things through to delivery.


[What you will be working on]

1. AI Evaluation

  • Execute on the product roadmap for AI evaluation — covering groundedness, citation quality, safety and adversarial testing, and regression evaluation.

  • Work with engineering to build and maintain reusable evaluation sets that product teams across the AI Programme can rely on, reducing duplicated effort.

  • Use AI observability data to support groundedness evaluation, unsafe output analysis, and AI risk reporting.

2. Runtime Safeguards

  • Contribute to the development of runtime safeguarding capabilities — including unsafe prompt and output detection, sensitive-content controls, prompt-injection indicators, and policy-based AI controls.

  • Work with engineering to embed safeguards into development workflows, following the assurance-by-design approach established by the team.

  • Support real-time monitoring for model drift, unsafe outputs, and prompt-injection attempts — flagging issues and working with engineering to resolve them.

3. Assurance Reporting

  • Maintain and improve AI assurance reporting — evaluation history, risk and remediation records, and assurance status — contributing to the team’s overall view of AI risk posture.

  • Track and report on defined KPIs: evaluation coverage, guardrail efficacy, mean time to detect vulnerabilities, and policy coverage.

4. AI Manipulation and Online Safety

  • Execute on the product roadmap for a whole-of-government platform that benchmarks and integrates AI detection solutions across image, video, and audio.

  • Support continuous evaluation as the deepfake threat landscape evolves — gathering performance data, surfacing findings, and contributing to decisions on which detection capabilities to onboard, refresh, or retire.

  • Work with capability developers and partner agencies to keep the platform operationally effective as a shared government service.

  • Participate in the Community of Practice across government — sharing benchmarking lessons, datasets, and evaluation insights.

Shape the future of justice in Singapore

Justice is one of Singapore's most important public services. Every year, almost 200,000 cases pass through our courts, involving individuals, families, businesses, lawyers and public agencies. Behind every case is someone seeking a fair, timely and accessible resolution.

The Judiciary's transformation into One Judiciary brought together the Supreme Court, State Courts and Family Justice Courts under a shared vision of delivering justice that is trusted, accessible and ready for the future.

Realising this vision requires more than organisational change. It requires rethinking the digital systems, processes and services that underpin how justice is delivered.

The Future Courts Management System (fCMS) is the Judiciary's flagship digital transformation programme, developed in close partnership with GovTech. You will join GovTech's product management community while working deeply with the Judiciary to shape products that support the administration of justice across Singapore's Courts.

This is not simply a like-for-like replacement of legacy systems. It is an opportunity to reimagine how court services should work: making them easier to use, more responsive to changing legislation and policies, and better able to serve everyone who depends on them.

This is a rare opportunity to help shape how justice will be delivered in Singapore for years to come.

The Role

As a Product Manager, you will be close to these problems and the people experiencing them. You will turn that understanding into product decisions and work with your team to make those decisions real.

You will work as part of a product trio with Engineering and Design, you will own a product problem space within fCMS — understanding the people and processes involved, discovering what should be built, prioritising what matters most, and working with your team to deliver measurable improvements.

As part of GovTech, you will be supported by a wider product, design and engineering community while working deeply with the Judiciary to build long-term digital capability.

In this role, you will:

  • Discover what problems are worth solving, working directly with judges, judicial officers, lawyers, court administrators, partner agencies and members of the public to understand their needs and pain points.

  • Prioritise based on evidence and outcomes, making decisions about what to build now, what to learn more about and what not to build.

  • Deliver value incrementally using modern product and engineering practices that reduce delivery risk, support learning from real usage and avoid big-bang replacement.

  • Measure whether the product is working, defining meaningful measures of success and using qualitative and quantitative evidence to understand where the product should improve.

  • Build alignment around product decisions, communicating the problem, evidence, priorities and trade-offs clearly to stakeholders and your delivery team.

You'll Thrive in This Role If...

  • You are curious about users and their problems. You want to understand why something works the way it does before deciding what should be built.

  • You think beyond requirements. When someone asks for a feature, you naturally want to understand the underlying problem and whether there might be a better way to solve it.

  • You use evidence to make decisions. You are comfortable combining user research, operational knowledge, product data and technical input rather than relying only on stakeholder opinion.

  • You make thoughtful product trade-offs — balancing user value, operational needs, technical sustainability, security, compliance and delivery risk.

  • You communicate clearly. You can explain a complicated problem, the evidence behind a decision and the trade-offs involved in a way that different audiences can understand.

  • You want to develop your product craft. You actively seek feedback, learn from more experienced Product Managers and reflect on how you can make better product decisions.

You should have experience working on digital products or services and have participated meaningfully in activities such as product discovery, user research, prioritisation, delivery or product analytics. Experience in government, justice, legal services or other complex domains is advantageous, but not essential.

What Success Looks Like

You will have succeeded when:

  • You understand your problem space deeply — not only the system, but the users, court processes and outcomes it exists to support.

  • Your team is solving problems rather than processing requirements, with clear reasoning behind what it chooses to build and what it chooses not to build.

  • You make increasingly independent product decisions, using evidence and good judgement while knowing when to seek guidance or escalate wider strategic decisions.

  • Your product improves through learning, with user feedback, product data and operational evidence influencing what the team does next.

  • Your team delivers useful improvements incrementally, creating value and reducing uncertainty throughout the transformation rather than only at the end.

  • People trust you as the product owner for your space, because you understand the problem, communicate decisions clearly and follow through on outcomes.

Why This Role Is Different

Few product management roles offer the opportunity to be part of the team that redesigns a digital system that underpin an entire national institution.

As part of GovTech, you will bring modern product, design and engineering practices to one of the Judiciary's most important transformation programmes. As part of the fCMS, you will help shape how justice is delivered in Singapore — not just by building better technology, but by helping create a Judiciary that is more accessible, more responsive and better prepared for the future.

GovTech is seeking a strategic and mission-driven Lead/Senior Product Manager to spearhead the AI Safety and Governance pillar within PlatformAI. As AI adoption scales across the public sector, your mission is to ensure that every AI-enabled application is secure, fair, and accountable by design.

You will own a dual-track roadmap:

  • For Developers: Building the "Safety Stack"—a suite of automated Evals, Guardrails, and Red-teaming tools that allow teams to deploy LLMs with speed and confidence.
  • For Governance and Observability: Architecting the "Governance Layer"—observability tools and risk-posture dashboards that provide a unified view of AI compliance across the whole-of-government (WOG) ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

1. Defining the Sovereign Safety Standard

  • Define the long-term strategy for AI Safety-as-a-Service, transitioning governance from a manual checklist to an automated platform feature.
  • Synthesize emerging global frameworks and local AI governance policies into platform features that make compliance "invisible" for developers.
  • Establish the government’s standard for AI risk levels, determining the safety benchmarks required for different use cases (e.g., citizen-facing vs. internal productivity).

2. Building the Guardrails & Audit Trails

  • Lead the development of automated evaluation engines that stress-test products and models for prompt injection, PII leakage, toxicity, and hallucination before and after deployment.
  • Partner with Engineering to integrate safety checks directly into CI/CD pipelines, ensuring that "Safety-by-Design" accelerates rather than hinders deployment.
  • Build real-time monitoring tools to detect "jailbreak" attempts and model drift, ensuring rapid mitigation of live AI risks.

3. Bridging Policy & Code

  • Act as the primary liaison between Policy/Legal teams and Engineering teams to ensure technical tools meet policy and legal intent.
  • Cultivate a culture of safety across GovTech by publishing playbooks, standardizing red-teaming exercises, and educating teams on the evolving LLM vulnerability landscape.

4. Trust-Centric Metrics & Accountability

  • Define and track KPIs such as Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) vulnerabilities, Policy Coverage %, and Guardrail Efficacy Rates.

  • AI Safety Domain Expertise: Deep understanding of Generative AI risks (e.g., prompt injection, training data poisoning, algorithmic bias) and the current state of AI safety research.
  • The "Translator" Skillset: Exceptional ability to distil abstract ethical principles into concrete technical requirements and APIs.
  • Analytical Rigor: A background in using data-driven evaluation frameworks (e.g., RAG evaluation, perplexity scoring, or model benchmarking) to measure performance and risk.
  • Developer Empathy: A deep understanding of developer workflows and a commitment to making safety tools an "accelerant" rather than a "roadblock."

The Singapore Judiciary plays a fundamental role in upholding the rule of law and ensuring that justice is accessible, effective and trusted.

For many people, navigating the justice system can be unfamiliar and complex. They may be representing themselves, dealing with a difficult personal situation, or interacting with the Courts for the first time. For lawyers, judicial officers and court staff, complex processes and systems can create a different set of challenges that affect how efficiently and effectively justice is delivered.

As the Senior Designer, you will help make the justice system easier to understand, navigate and participate in — while respecting the legal and procedural safeguards that underpin it.

You will work across the Judiciary with judges, judicial officers, court staff, lawyers, members of the public, self-represented persons, policy and technology teams to understand where people encounter barriers and design better ways for them to interact with the justice system.

This is not simply a role designing digital products. You will help shape how the Judiciary administers, adjudicates and delivers justice, using design, technology and service thinking to improve outcomes for both the people who use the system and the people who operate it.

The Opportunity

The opportunity is to make the justice system easier to understand, navigate and participate in — for the people who use it and the professionals who help deliver it.

This includes members of the public and self-represented persons who may have little or no experience with the Courts, as well as lawyers, paralegals, judges, judicial officers, court administrators and other agencies that interact with the justice system.

For users, accessibility can mean being able to find the right information, understand what they need to do, complete processes with greater confidence, and know what to expect next. For those delivering justice, it can mean having systems and processes that reduce unnecessary administrative burden and allow them to focus on the work that matters.

The challenge is not simply to make every process simpler. Some complexity is necessary because of legal, procedural and institutional requirements. The opportunity for design is to distinguish necessary complexity from accidental complexity — removing avoidable barriers while preserving the safeguards and integrity of the justice system.

Technology, digital services and the systems that support the Judiciary are important enablers of this transformation. By improving how information, processes and services work together, they can help the Judiciary respond more effectively to changing needs, procedures and legislation.

Ultimately, the goal is not the technology itself. The goal is a justice system that works better for the people who depend on it.

What you would do

Understand people and the system

You will research how people and professionals experience the justice system, identifying barriers, pain points and opportunities across services, processes and organisational boundaries. You will use research, workshops and prototyping to turn complex problems into clear opportunities and practical solutions.

Shape better ways of delivering justice

You will work with judicial, legal, policy, operational and technology stakeholders to shape how justice services should work in the future. You will identify whether problems are best addressed through technology, service or process redesign, information, policy or a combination of these. You will design systems and services that help the Judiciary administer, adjudicate and deliver justice more effectively, while making the experience easier to understand and navigate.

Bring people together

You will facilitate co-design and working sessions with judicial, legal, operational, technology and user groups to build alignment around better solutions. You will challenge assumptions constructively, communicate design decisions using research, data, prototypes and user perspectives, and create shared artefacts that help teams work from a common understanding.

Raise the bar for design

You will enforce design standards, patterns and practices that enable consistent, accessible experiences across Judiciary services. You will coach and mentor designers while improving how the team researches, designs, critiques and communicates its work. You will champion responsible use of AI and emerging tools to accelerate design while maintaining quality, accuracy and human judgement.

Experience and craft

  • Strong portfolio demonstrating research, synthesis, interaction design, prototyping and delivery.

  • Experience designing complex workflows, professional users or high-stakes environments.

  • Strong systems-thinking ability and experience connecting user needs with organisational, operational and technology considerations.

  • You think in systems but move quickly when the opportunity calls for it.

  • You maintain clear and accessible design artefacts so teams and stakeholders can work from a shared understanding of the current state.

About the Role

We are looking for Product Designers who are problem solvers first.

Our users include policy makers, economists and senior leaders working with complex information, workflows and decisions. Your role is to understand how they work, identify the right problems to solve, and design products and services that make their work simpler and more effective. This is not just about designing screens.

You will work across: Problem Framing · Service Design · UX Design from discovery and validation through to build and continuous improvement.

You Are Able To

  • Work in the field and in the boardroom, from understanding how users work to engaging senior stakeholders.
  • Make sense of messy problems and turn ambiguity into clear problems and opportunities.
  • Zoom out and zoom in, understand the wider system, then get the important experience details right.
  • Understand users' workflows, information needs and decision-making processes.
  • Turn research and insights into better product and service experiences.
  • Design across digital touchpoints, processes, people and systems.
  • Simplify complex information and workflows without losing important context.
  • Make ideas tangible through journeys, flows, wireframes and prototypes.
  • Test ideas early, learn and iterate.
  • Work with Product Managers and Engineers to see solutions through from discovery to delivery.

What You'll Do

Discover & Define

  • Understand users, their goals, workflows, pain points and information needs.
  • Conduct appropriate user research.
  • Separate the real problem from assumptions and proposed solutions.
  • Synthesise research and evidence into clear insights and opportunities.
  • Frame problems so multidisciplinary teams have a shared understanding of what we are solving.

Validate & Improve

  • Turn assumptions into hypotheses and prototypes that can be tested.
  • Conduct concept and usability testing with users.
  • Iterate based on qualitative and quantitative evidence.
  • Stay involved during build to ensure the intended experience is delivered.
  • Use user feedback, product usage and outcomes to continuously improve the product.

Collaborate & Influence

  • Facilitate workshops and conversations that help teams make progress.
  • Make complex problems understandable through clear visualisation and storytelling.
  • Communicate design rationale and trade-offs without relying on design jargon.
  • Build strong relationships with policy teams, economists, Product Managers, Engineers and senior stakeholders.
  • Advocate for users while understanding policy, operational and technical constraints.

[What we are looking for]

Product Designer: Around 2 to 4 + years of relevant professional experience.

Senior Product Designer: Around 5+ years, with experience independently framing complex problems, leading design work and engaging senior stakeholders.

You should have:

  • Strong problem-framing and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong foundations in human-centred design.
  • Experience with user research and synthesis.
  • Service design skills, including journey mapping and understanding end-to-end experiences.
  • Strong UX fundamentals: user flows, information architecture, interaction design and prototyping.
  • Ability to simplify complex workflows and information.
  • Experience prototyping, testing and iterating with users.
  • Strong facilitation and communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with Product Managers and Engineers.
  • Ability to navigate ambiguity and learn complex domains quickly.

Nice to Have

  • Experience designing for knowledge workers, analysts or professional users.
  • Information-heavy or data-heavy products.
  • Information or data visualisation.
  • Service and process redesign.
  • Product analytics and experimentation.
  • Design systems and UI/visual design.
  • AI or emerging technologies.
  • Government, public service or other complex environments.

You do not need to be a policy or economics expert. You need to be curious, ask good questions and be able to learn from people who are.

Our designers use problem framing, service design and UX to help teams understand the right problem, make better decisions and build better products.

About Ministry of Transport (MOT)

The Mission of Ministry of Transport is to develop Singapore's land, sea and air transport sectors to enhance our economic competitiveness and quality of life in a knowledge-based economy. MOT oversees the development and regulation of the following sectors:

  • Civil Aviation and Air Transport
  • Maritime and Ports
  • Land Transport

Besides providing an efficient and cost-effective transportation in Singapore, it also strives to make Singapore an international civil aviation and maritime centre for the region. The ministry sets the strategic and policy direction while operations and regulatory works are carried out by the statutory boards under its charge. There are four statutory boards which are established by Acts of Parliament: the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS), the Land Transport Authority (LTA), the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and the Public Transport Council (PTC). The ministry also oversees the operation of the Transport Safety Investigation Bureau (TSIB).

We are seeking a skilled Designer to lead the end-to-end user experiences for various products in the Ministry of Transport (MOT). This role spans employer-facing workflows, internal operational processes, and platform constraints within a regulated environment. This role may also cover design work for the Public Transport Council (PTC).

As the main designer for MOT’s digital products, you will shape problem framing, user journeys, and design direction from discovery through delivery, while contributing to and evolving design patterns and standards aligned with Government Digital Service Standards. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact on how businesses and internal users interact with government digital services.

You will work as part of a cross-functional product team, partnering closely with Product and Engineering, with autonomy over design direction and professional mentorship from the Design Lead.

  • Outcome focus: Work closely with product managers to own outcomes continuously improving the products feedback and iteration

  • UX/UI design: Translate complex user, business and regulatory requirements into smart, engaging, modern flows and elegant interfaces

  • Design quality: Work to consistently improve the user experience and quality of all the products you work on, helping to uplift the quality of design across government in line with Government Digital Service Standards

  • Digital and data savvy: Work with our engineering and data leads make smart decisions that get the most out of technology and data and work through constraints

  • Stakeholder management: Work closely with product managers to deliver on business outcomes and help facilitate through inevitable conflicts and constraints, acting as an advocate for humans in the system

About TradeNet

TradeNet is Singapore’s National Single Window for trade permit processing. It processes over 9 million permit applications annually across import, export and transshipment. As one of Singapore’s key trade systems, TradeNet is being brought in-house to strengthen technology ownership and long-term sustainability.

How we build

Designated as critical IT infrastructure, we favor simple, durable technology choices over the latest trends. We prioritize systems that are easy to reason about, operate, and maintain for the long term.

We operate with high autonomy. Engineers are expected to think deeply, exercise sound judgement, and take ownership of technical decisions. You own the code from technical design through to production. We practice and value honest feedback, practical decision-making and real impact.

We are seeking a Lead Cybersecurity Engineer to oversee technical design and execution for the TradeNet CII modernization—driving architectural security, secure coding, DevSecOps practices, and platform reliability.

In this role, you will write code, implement CI/CD security controls, embed protective mechanisms into system blueprints, delineate core infrastructure requirements, and partner with the Customs ACISO to meet CSA CII obligations

Success in this role means deploying a platform that is defensible and reliable by design, rather than relying on reactive fixes.

Secure and resilient architecture (core mandate)

  • Own the reference security architecture for the TradeNet CII: trust boundaries, identity architecture, segmentation and trust-zone strategy, east-west controls, encryption and key management, and blast-radius containment for the CII boundary.
  • Embed secure-by-design controls by working inside product and engineering teams through the delivery lifecycle — at design, solutioning and implementation time, not as post-build validation.
  • Maintain a living threat model per system and trust boundary, referenced to MITRE ATT&CK and to relevant adversary classes (including supply-chain and nation-state), and use it to drive architecture and segmentation decisions — not merely to prioritise remediation.

Resilience and national trade continuity

We're looking for a Product Manager to own Data Provisioning Standards (DPS) — the rules, schemas, contracts, and governance processes that determine how data enters, moves through, and gets consumed across our platform. This is a foundational, cross-cutting role: you won't own a single user-facing feature, you'll own the standards that every data producer and consumer downstream depends on to trust the data they're working with.

[What you will be working on]

This role sits at the intersection of product, data engineering, and governance. You see policy as a product — DPS is a government mandate, but mandates don't implement themselves.

You'll work closely with Policy stakeholders to shape & operationalise standards, Data Providing Agencies (DPAs) to implement DPS, GovTech's engineering team to build toolings & systems, and Data Consuming Agencies (DCAs) to ensure the data reaching them is consistent, well-documented, and trustworthy for their operations and service delivery.


If you've worked on data contracts, schema governance, API standards, data quality/observability tooling, or consent-and-compliance-driven data exchange, this role will feel familiar.


What You'll Do

  • Define and own what good data provisioning looks like across WOG — spanning Data Quality, Data Delivery Performance and Data Interfacing Standards — and iterate those standards in close collaboration with policy stakeholders, ensuring they remain grounded in what agencies can realistically implement as the ecosystem matures.

  • Design and own the agency support packages for DPS implementation — matching the right level of guidance, tooling, and support to each agency's technical maturity so that compliance is achievable for every agency regardless of where they start.

  • Work with data engineering team to translate standards into tooling that data providers can actually use — spanning data quality validation, metrics computation, pipeline integration, and centralised monitoring.

  • Own the roadmap for data quality and provisioning tooling, prioritizing against data provider pain points through requirements-gathering sessions, downstream consumer needs, and adoption risk (e.g., silent schema drift, incomplete metadata, inconsistent semantics across providers).

  • Define and track success metrics for provisioning health: onboarding time, data quality incident rate, schema compliance rate, time-to-detect for drift/anomalies.

  • Write and maintain clear, versioned documentation of every standard — the standard itself, the rationale, migration guidance for changes, and worked examples.

  • Where standards intersect with regulatory or consent requirements, work with legal/compliance to ensure provisioning rules satisfy consent, data minimization, and audit requirements.

  • Represent the provisioning standards function in cross-team and (where relevant) external/industry forums.

[What we are looking for]

  • 4+ years of product management experience, with meaningful time spent on a data platform, data infrastructure, API platform, or developer-facing product

  • Demonstrated experience defining standards, contracts, or schemas that other teams had to adopt — and successfully driving that adoption across teams you didn't manage.

  • Strong technical fluency with data concepts: schemas, APIs, data contracts, ETL/ELT pipelines, data quality dimensions (completeness, timeliness, accuracy). You don't need to write production code, but you need to be credible in a room with data engineers.

  • A track record of balancing governance rigor against provider/developer experience — you know that a standard nobody can practically comply with is worse than no standard at all. So you'll be as invested in the tooling, templates, and any support that make compliance achievable by data providing agencies.

  • Excellent written communication — this role lives and dies by documentation quality. Comfortable writing specs, migration guides, and decision records that other teams will follow without you in the room.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills: you'll be negotiating with data provider teams who don't report to you and don't always want to change how they work.

  • Comfortable operating with ambiguity in a space that's still maturing — you'll be building some of these standards from scratch, not just maintaining existing ones.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with data quality/observability tooling (e.g., Monte Carlo, Validio, Great Expectations, or an in-house equivalent).

  • Background in a regulated or consent-driven data-sharing environment (open banking, health data exchange, gov data platforms, or similar).

jobTitle: Senior / Manager, IT Strategy and Planning (MOM)
jobDescription:
The Government Technology Agency (GovTech) aims to transform the delivery of Government digital services by taking an "outside-in" view, putting citizens and businesses at the heart of everything we do. We also develop the Smart Nation infrastructure and applications, and facilitate collaboration with citizens and businesses to co-develop technologies.
Join us as we support Singapore’s vision of building a Smart Nation - a nation of possibilities empowered through info-communications technology and related engineering.

Background

As part of the IT Strategy and Planning team, you will play a pivotal role in shaping MOM’s digital transformation, ensuring that initiatives are strategically structured, future-ready, and relevant MOM’s business priorities. You will drive the effective use of digital technology and data, ensuring that digital initiatives are seamlessly integrated into MOM’s policy, business and organisational tech strategies. By leveraging MOM’s Tech Strategy Map (TSM), you will ensure digital transformation efforts deliver measurable impact and achieve business outcomes.

What the role is

We are seeking an independent and self-motivated strategic thinker to join us in advancing MOM transformation journey. If you have got good appreciation of both technology and business landscapes and passionate in architecting MOM’s digital future, we welcome you to apply and be part of the IT Strategic & Planning team.

What you will be working on

1. Strategic and Organisational Planning for Digital Investments
Drive the development of MOM’s long-term digital investment roadmap, ensuring that resources, funding, and capabilities are strategically organised and allocated to maximise business impact.
Drive agency-wide digital capability building, ensuring that technology adoption is meaningful, structured, and impactful.
Establish a structured approach for evaluating emerging technologies, ensuring that digital tools and platforms deliver tangible benefits to MOM, citizens and relevant stakeholders.
2. Digital Performance Measurement & Impact Assessment
Define and track strategic metrics to focus, align, and measure the impact of MOM’s digital transformation efforts.
Ensure data-informed decision-making, providing actionable insights on digital adoption trends, challenges, and areas for improvement.
Conduct impact assessments to ensure that MOM’s digital investments achieve intended business outcomes.
3. Digital Strategy & Whole-of-Government (WOG) Alignment
Develop and drive MOM’s digital strategy and priority initiatives, ensuring a cohesive approach to digital transformation across the ministry.
Ensure MOM’s digital transformation initiatives are strategically positioned to leverage WOG platforms and national AI capabilities, enhancing learning, teaching, and operational effectiveness.
Align MOM’s digital priorities with WOG initiatives, including the Public Service Transformation (PST), Digital Government Blueprint (DGB), and Smart Nation.

Other ad-hoc tasks/projects where needed.

What we are looking for

  • At least 5 years of experience in digital strategy, technology planning, or public sector transformation.
  • Proven experience in digital strategy planning, investment prioritisation, and data-driven decision-making.
  • Experience in steering committee leadership, stakeholder engagement, and cross-division collaboration.
  • Strong ability to translate digital and data strategies into actionable plans that drive business outcomes.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, with experience engaging senior government officials, policy & operational teams.
  • Proactively monitor transformation progress, identifying risks and challenges and recommend mitigation strategies.
  • Support internal teams, including development and presentation of transformation updates and facilitate strategic planning.
  • Ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment, with strong multitasking and time management skills.
  • Strong communication skills, both verbal and written, comfortable engaging Senior Management Leaders.
  • Personal Attributes
  • Strong influence, able to navigate complex digital transformation landscapes.
  • Strategic and forward-thinking, with the ability to drive long-term digital planning.
  • Results-oriented, ensuring digital initiatives drive measurable impact.
  • Collaborative and adaptable, able to engage diverse stakeholders and bridge digital planning with operational needs.
  • Curious and adaptable, with a strong ability to challenge the status quo and drive meaningful change.

GeBIZ X is the MOF product that would transform the procurement and business experience for WOG public officers and external suppliers.

[Who we are looking for]

The Ministry of Finance is transforming government procurement through the Whole of Government Procurement initiative. GeBIZ X will revolutionise the procurement experience for WOG public officers and external suppliers.

We are seeking a Senior Platform Infrastructure Engineer to oversee the Enterprise Infrastructure of the GeBIZ X Product. You will demonstrate technical leadership in infrastructure engineering, designing, building, and operating the infrastructure ecosystem that comprises Ivalua SaaS as the Base Solution, seamlessly integrated with Extended Solutions including COTS and SaaS applications, connecting to government agency systems and the Singapore Government Tech Stack (SGTS). This orchestration layer, hosted on AWS Government Commercial Cloud (GCC) using API Gateway and SFTP protocols, serves as the critical integration hub.

You will be expected to navigate technical complexity across GovTech, Government agencies and technology partners, ensuring the interoperability of GeBIZ X and the wider network of systems whilst maintaining resilience, security, scalability, and compliance with government standards.

Core Values

Decision-making

  • When making important decisions, we identify overarching goals, weigh up our options, identify impact, and clearly communicate and manage the risks and trade-offs of our decision.

Ownership

  • In addition to technical responsibilities, this means having opinions on what is being done and having ideas on what should be done next. Building something that you believe in is the best way to build something good.

Continuous Learning

  • Working on new ideas often means not fully understanding what you are working on. Taking time to learn new architectures, frameworks, technologies, and even languages is not just encouraged but essential.

[What you will be working on]

Key Responsibilities

  • Full-Stack Infrastructure Engineering (AWS/GCC)
    Lead hands-on design and implementation of the complete platform ecosystem in AWS/GCC, including compute, storage, and specialised networking. Architect and manage API Gateway as central orchestrator governing traffic between external SaaS and internal government services.
  • COTS Implementation & SaaS Integration
    Lead installation, configuration, and maintenance of COTS products (e.g., e-Signature solutions like Sign with Singpass) within AWS/GCC. Engineer secure, high-performance bridges to external SaaS environments and establish monitoring standards across all layers.
  • DevSecOps & SHIP-HATS Integration
    Champion DevSecOps practices by driving SHIP-HATS ecosystem adoption (GitLab, SonarQube, etc.) to automate infrastructure delivery. Ensure strict adherence to IM8 policies and GovTech's "Security-by-Design" principles whilst building automation tools to reduce manual operations.
  • Strategic Alignment & Technical Leadership
    Develop roadmaps for complex infrastructure initiatives, coordinate across teams and external partners, manage technical risks proactively, and invest in team growth through mentorship and knowledge sharing.
  • Core Competencies
    Systems thinking for scalable ecosystem design spanning multiple environments, analytical leadership translating business problems to infrastructure solutions, effective stakeholder management across project teams and vendors, and self-driven ownership committed to leveraging technology for public good.

Technical Leadership Expectations

  • Engineer Resilient Platform Infrastructure at Scale
    Engineer resilient systems through deep understanding of infrastructure engineering and user behaviour. Tackle cross-cutting technical issues elegantly, establish high monitoring standards, and engineer systems with observability in mind to evaluate behaviour at scale.
  • Lead Complex Platform Infrastructure Transformations
    Apply systems thinking to improve efficiency, repeatability, and scale. Evolve infrastructure practices based on feedback and failure mode observations. Lead design, implementation, and launch of platform infrastructure services across multiple teams, navigating technical and organisational complexity with sound judgement.
  • Technical Leadership with Agency or WOG Impact
    Coordinate delivery across divisions ensuring alignment and quality. Proactively address potential failure points, collaborate with PMs/EMs at scale, and help unify organisational technical standards across teams.

Leadership Responsibilities

  • Strategic Execution
    Support divisional strategic agenda and drive key projects. Independently identify projects supporting strategic objectives, provide direction with strong outcome measurement ability, and develop roadmaps for complex initiatives.
  • Team Leadership
    Align team goals with departmental objectives, contribute to hiring standards, conduct regular 1:1s, provide growth opportunities, and create productive environments by removing barriers and motivating teams.
  • Cross-Team Collaboration
    Lead cross-functional collaboration across multiple teams, resolve stakeholder conflicts, facilitate solutions to achieve strategic outcomes, and champion continuous improvement whilst building capability in areas of expertise.
  • Mentorship
    Actively invest in peer and junior member growth through mentorship, sponsorship, and knowledge sharing. Mentor L3 and below officers beyond immediate team, measurably improving colleague capabilities.

[What we are looking for]

Experience & Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related technical discipline. 8–10 years in Infrastructure Engineering, DevOps, or SRE with proven AWS/GCC and enterprise COTS experience.

Technical Skills

  • Infrastructure Orchestration: AWS API Gateway mastery including secure endpoints, rate limiting, and traffic routing
  • COTS Management: Commercial software installation and operationalisation in cloud environments
  • Infrastructure as Code: Expert Terraform proficiency for GCC-side ecosystem
  • Cloud & GCC: Deep AWS services (EKS, Lambda, RDS, IAM) and GCC landing zone expertise
  • Hybrid Integration: Secure connectivity patterns (VPNs, PrivateLink) and API-first architectures

Please note that this will be a 2-year fixed term contract.

About MOT

The Mission of Ministry of Transport is to develop Singapore's land, sea and air transport sectors to enhance our economic competitiveness and quality of life in a knowledge-based economy. MOT oversees the development and regulation of the following sectors:

  • Civil Aviation and Air Transport
  • Maritime and Ports
  • Land Transport

Besides providing an efficient and cost-effective transportation in Singapore, it also strives to make Singapore an international civil aviation and maritime centre for the region. The ministry sets the strategic and policy direction while operations and regulatory works are carried out by the statutory boards under its charge. There are four statutory boards which are established by Acts of Parliament: the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS), the Land Transport Authority (LTA), the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and the Public Transport Council (PTC). The ministry also oversees the operation of the Transport Safety Investigation Bureau (TSIB).

  • Own the comparison/catalogue UX, the surface where an agency sees candidate central and commercial options side by side, understands trade-offs (cost, complexity, lock-in), and can act on a recommendation.

  • Define feature-level success metrics for this slice, feeding into the Evaluate stage's broader North Star Metric once defined.

  • Work closely with the Product Portal and the Console team, so this product sits coherently within the wider discovery → evaluate → start onboarding funnel, rather than as a disconnected surface.

  • Running structured discovery with agency CIO offices, delivery leads, and architects to validate what information they need to give and receive during evaluation, building on existing agency research.

  • Defining and validating the MVP scope for the context-capture and comparison surfaces before committing to build, working with your UX researcher and engineer to test assumptions early.

  • Curating the underlying product knowledge needed to power credible comparisons across GovTech's central products, partnering with individual product teams to keep this current.

You will ultimately be responsible for making the Evaluate journey the point where agencies stop guessing and start comparing with confidence.

You develop operational strategies and work closely with cross-functional teams to deliver on product goals. At the senior level, you operate with high autonomy across a large or multi-product problem space — addressing complex, often unprecedented challenges, guiding others, and influencing practices beyond your immediate team.

[What you will be working on]

The AI Programme builds shared AI infrastructure that agencies can run in production, instead of rebuilding the same foundations independently. It sits within Government Digital Products, and it owns a small number of central products that a lot of other people's work now depends on.

Three of them shape the job. There's the agent surface public officers use to get through the day: it reaches into their mail, their documents and their case systems, so it has to be quick, honest about what it just did on their behalf, and safe to point at real records. Underneath sits the developer platform, where teams across government bring their own agents, MCP servers and skills and move them into production through review, approval and audit. And there's the model and capability layer that most agencies meet first: a compliant gateway to multiple production-approved models behind an OpenAI-compatible API, alongside shared speech, vision and document capabilities (live transcription, image and video classification, key information extraction) that every agency would otherwise go and procure separately, with guardrails, quotas and cost attribution already attached.

Building an agent demo is easy now, and that's fine, because it means the hard parts have moved. Most of what we work on lives after the demo. An agent decides to call a tool that sends an email on someone's behalf, and the approval gate for that has to be enforced by the runtime, not requested politely in a system prompt. A tool loop needs a stop condition that doesn't depend on the model deciding it's done. Token spend has to trace back to the team that caused it, and when an agency's agent gets slower this week, someone has to be able to say why. Rollback gets interesting when the artefact is a prompt, a tool schema and a model version rather than a binary. Very little of that is model work. It's orchestration, platform and operations, which is roughly the job.
You'll work across all of it: the surfaces officers see, the runtime underneath, the platform other engineers build on, and the unglamorous business of keeping the whole thing up. Your user is a public officer with something to finish today. Your customer is often another engineering team in another agency.

  • Build the runtime beneath them: tool orchestration, approval gates enforced in code, loop limits, per-turn tool filtering, memory and checkpointing, model routing and fallback

  • Work on the platform half, where the job is to let other teams onboard their own agents, MCP servers, skills and models, with the policy checks and promotion workflows that let them move to production safely and repeatedly

  • Extend the shared capability APIs (speech, vision, document extraction) and keep them fast and cheap enough that agencies reach for them instead of building their own

  • Integrate with what government already runs: identity, mail and calendar, document stores, agency line-of-business systems, the existing CI/CD pipelines

  • Instrument the things you'll want to argue about later. Tool call traces, latency, error taxonomies, cost per team and per feature

  • Build evaluation into delivery, so changing a prompt, a tool or a model becomes a measurable decision instead of an argument

  • Run it. Deployments, incidents, capacity, cost, and the support queue of officers who found the case nobody thought of

  • Work with agency teams as users and as builders, and turn the third bespoke request into a platform feature

  • Take part in security and privacy reviews on the assumption that these systems get audited, because they do

The Government Digital Products (GDP) Team aims to spearhead the digital transformation of government. Our team designs and develops software applications that help government agencies to better serve the needs of the people of Singapore.

At the Engagement and Case Management Programme (ECMP), our products are the primary touchpoints through which residents interact with the Singapore Government. We design and develop a suite of high-impact software applications including FileSG, Signify, PersonaliseSG, CrowdTask SG, and BookingSG.

The Challenge: Elevating FileSG

FileSG is a central, secure file management system designed to streamline the issuance and distribution of official documents to Singapore residents. Beyond simple file transfer, it serves as a citizen-centric platform that supports the secure delivery of verified files—such as certificates, licenses, letters, and notices—directly to users. Trusted by agencies to replace inefficient legacy channels like physical mail and unencrypted emails, FileSG offers end-to-end traceability, confidentiality, and ease of access. Our mission is to consolidate document distribution onto a single, secure-by-design platform, eliminating the need for individual agencies to develop fragmented solutions and delivering a seamless, digital-first experience at a national scale. The Government Digital Products (GDP) Team aims to spearhead the digital transformation of government. Our team designs and develops software applications that help government agencies to better serve the needs of the people of Singapore.

The Challenge: Elevating BookingSG

BookingSG is a comprehensive Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution designed to unify, simplify, and manage appointments and resource scheduling across Whole-of-Government (WOG) agencies. Far from a simple calendar app, BookingSG is a highly customizable, multi-tenant platform built on a versatile architecture featuring Calendaring, Availability, Rostering, and Booking (CARB) capabilities.

Trusted by 50+ government agencies across 60+ distinct use cases, our platform handles over 1.5 million transactions—and we are just getting started. Whether it's high-volume facility bookings or complex citizen appointment routing, our mission is to turn fragmented legacy systems into elegant, out-of-the-box digital booking experiences at a national scale.

We are looking for a Technical Lead / Engineering Manager to spearhead the next evolution of this platform. You will take full engineering ownership of a nimble, cross-functional squad — balancing enterprise architecture and high-velocity shipping with hands-on coaching to level up our engineering practices.

We are looking for a Technical Programme Manager (TPM) to lead complex, cross-functional technical programmes across Singpass.

The role will initially have two main areas of focus:

  1. National Certification Authority (NCA): Driving the build, commissioning and transition into stable Day 2 operations.
  2. Strategic Technical Programmes: Steer initiatives such as Verifiable Digital Credentials (VDC), as well as smaller programmes that require dedicated coordination across engineering, product, policy, security, governance and external partners.

The TPM is expected to understand the technical and operational domain sufficiently to identify meaningful dependencies, surface risks early, challenge assumptions, drive decisions and bring multiple teams together around an outcome.

1. National Certification Authority

NCA is a high-assurance national trust infrastructure programme involving PKI, cryptographic hardware, on-premise infrastructure, vendors, procurement, security, compliance and operational processes.

You will:

  • Drive NCA milestones across Root CA build and commissioning, ICA and VA implementation, supporting infrastructure and transition into Day 2 operations.
  • Maintain an integrated view of timelines, dependencies, critical paths and risks across engineering and non-engineering workstreams.
  • Work closely with engineering on sprint and milestone planning, surfacing blockers and unresolved decisions early.
  • Coordinate across Engineering, Security, Governance & Risk, Assurity, Procurement, Legal, vendors and service providers.
  • Drive procurement workstreams, including requirements, RFQs, evaluations, approvals and vendor deliverables.
  • Coordinate operational readiness, i.e. runbooks, HSM and key-management processes, key ceremonies, data-centre procedures, incident processes, BCP/DR and operational vendor arrangements.
  • Coordinate internal and external audit readiness, including IM8, WebTrust, ETA and relevant internal controls.

The TPM is not the hands-on PKI engineer, but should develop enough domain understanding to recognise risks, ask the right questions and ensure the relevant experts are engaged.

2. Strategic Technical Programmes

Beyond NCA, the TPM will take on other technically complex programmes across Singpass. These may include initiatives such as Verifiable Digital Credentials (VDC), platform rollouts, security or infrastructure programmes, cross-domain integrations, or smaller initiatives that cut across multiple teams.

Depending on the programme, you may:

  • turn ambiguous objectives into clear outcomes, workstreams and milestones;
  • establish programme structure and ownership;
  • coordinate across engineering, product, design, policy, security and external stakeholders;
  • track risks, unblock execution and drive decisions;
  • coordinate pilot, rollout and operational-readiness activities;
  • transition programmes into steady-state ownership once delivered.

The programmes may vary significantly in size and domain.The common thread is that they require someone to operate across organisational boundaries and keep a technically complex outcome moving.

[What we are looking for]

Must have:

  • Experience leading technical programmes involving multiple teams and stakeholders.
  • Able to influence and drive accountability without direct reporting authority.
  • Strong programme management fundamentals across milestones, risks and decisions.
  • Comfortable working closely with engineers and understanding technical architecture, constraints and trade-offs.
  • Strong written and verbal communication.
  • Able to provide clear status, escalation and decision-making support to senior stakeholders.
  • Strong attention to detail while retaining sight of the overall programme outcome.
  • Comfortable operating in ambiguous environments and creating structures for progress

    Good to have:
  • Experience delivering infrastructure, platform, security or high-assurance systems.
  • Experience with on-premise infrastructure, hardware or data-centre environments.
  • Experience taking systems from build through commissioning and operational readiness.
  • Familiarity with government procurement and vendor management.
  • Experience operating in regulated or audited environments.
  • Exposure to PKI concepts such as CA hierarchies, HSMs, key ceremonies,
    certificate revocation or validation services.
  • Exposure to WebTrust, ISO, financial-services controls or comparable assurance regimes.

Hands-on PKI or cryptography expertise is not required.

[What Cybersecurity TAP is]

As a Technology Associate in Cybersecurity, you'll begin your career protecting the digital services and infrastructure that millions of people in Singapore rely on every day.

Over the three-year Technology Associate Programme (TAP), you'll build a strong foundation in cybersecurity principles while working alongside experienced engineers, security specialists and product teams on real systems that underpin Singapore's digital government. Through structured rotations, mentorship and hands-on project experience, you'll deepen your technical craft, grow your confidence and gain exposure to different security challenges across the public sector.

You'll have the opportunity to shape your own growth in a supportive and collaborative environment. Along the way, you'll receive guidance from experienced GovTech cybersecurity practitioners and technology leaders, learn alongside a cohort of like-minded associates, and benefit from curated development opportunities that help you build both your technical expertise and leadership potential.

You'll kickstart your career with one of three tracks based on your interests and strengths. On the Security Testing track, you'll hunt down vulnerabilities in critical government systems before adversaries can exploit them. On the Cyber Defence track, you'll work on the front lines of threat detection, analysing malware, tracking threat actors and uncovering the story behind security incidents. On the Product Engineering track, you'll design and build scalable security solutions that strengthen the government's cybersecurity posture across the board. Whichever path you take, you'll contribute meaningfully to Singapore's cyber resilience while learning from practitioners who are invested in your growth.

Whether you're conducting user research, shaping product experiences or designing intuitive and integrated service flows, you'll have opportunities to contribute meaningfully while learning from experienced practitioners who are invested in your growth.

[What Data Science TAP is]

As a Data Scientist, you will play an integral role in turning data into decisions - building and deploying the machine learning and AI that informs public policies and make public services more responsive, personalised and trustworthy for everyone in Singapore. The work spans a few key areas.

  • Turning real world challenges into data science problems. We start with the people we serve. Working closely with agencies, we translate real-world challenges into problems that data and machine learning can solve, finding the right data, shaping it, and choosing the approach that actually fits the question rather than the fanciest model.
  • Models that deliver public good to the real world. An insight is more meaningful when it changes something.   • Working at the frontier of AI. The field moves fast, and so do we. How do we work

Job overview

We have built a scrum team of technologists who have developed digital products to improve citizen's experience of using the agency's e-services.

As a UX designer, you will work with our scrum team and other government agencies to inform product and design decisions. You will get to influence the digital experience of the agency’s e-services. You will work closely with our designers, engineers, business analysts and product managers to continuously deliver features for transforming citizen experience and improving agency efficiency.

You will sit with the project scrum team, as a member of the UX team in GDP. The office will be located at the Punggol Digital District (PDD).

What to expect

Within your first month...

You have understood the overall product strategy, did a stock take on the UX status of the project, and contributed design screens for concurrent active sprints.

By the end of 3 months...

You should have run an inception, gathered requirements, co-create with stakeholders and scrum team, tested, prototyped, and shipped at least one new feature to the product backlog.

After 6 months...

You will have led research efforts to identify at least one opportunity for the product to grow or proposed enhancements for the existing tracks, in collaboration with designers, engineers, and product managers.

Beyond that...

You will continue to solve problems such as:

How can we...

  • create a seamless experience for citizen across e-services
  • help citizen complete the service with ease
  • resolve the agency pain point and improve ops efficiency
  • use data to improve government services
  • design for reusability across products

Product and user-centric mindset

  • You need to be able to grasp the use case and come up with the task flows in a short span of time

  • You are collaborative and understand that co-creating a product with the team

  • You find the quickest route to design, test, and ship a design prototype to 'prove'

  • You are data-driven yourself, with experience in user research, in order to use data to justify design decisions

  • You yearn to analyse user feedback and activity, and iterating the design to enhance user experience

Technologist at work

  • You are able to translate user research into design recommendations and findings

  • You are able to tackle complex tasks and transform them into intuitive, accessible, and easy-to-use designs

  • You are meticulous and possess good problem solving skills

  • Frontend development knowledge is a bonus

Strategist at heart

  • Strategists hardly work alone. You have to work well with your scrum team and agencies to strategise the product direction together.

  • Good organisational, presentation and listening skills

  • Be flexible, be a team player, solve problems, and contribute to the UX and product team’s success.

  • At least 4-5 years of professional experience in product design, working on end-to-end delivery. That would include experience in facilitating workshops, gathering requirements, usability testing, envisioning flows, and delivering hi-fidelity mockups.

  • Experience in Agile and UX development environment will be an added advantage

  • Previous experience leading a team in UX design will be an added advantage. You may be considered for a senior position if applicable.

Why Join Us

When you join PSD, you become part of a community that learns together and cares for one another. We look out for your well-being and partner you in your career growth. Being in the business of developing People and driving transformation makes our work deeply Purposeful. What you do will impact our public officers and agencies, and in turn make a difference to Singapore and Singaporeans.

If you share our passion in reimagining Possibilities and pushing boundaries to shape a first-class Public Service, we welcome you to join us!

People, Our Pride | Service, Our Pledge | Integrity, Our Core | Excellence, Our Quest
jobDescription:
The Public Service Division (PSD), a Centre of Government agency, shapes people and organisation strategies across Singapore's Public Service. As the steward of Public Service-wide HR policies, PSD is reimagining how performance is recognised, organisations are designed and managers lead — building an agile, future-ready people system for an AI-enabled, competency-based and multi-generational workforce.

Performance management and organisation design are two sides of the same coin. High-performing organisations are built not only through how work is organised, but also through how people are recognised, developed and enabled to perform. In this role, you will design HR policies, people systems and organisational structures that enable the Public Service to deliver for Singapore today and into the future.

Join a team shaping the future of Singapore’s largest employer — with more than 150,000 public officers — and the people systems and policies that enable it to deliver for Singapore. If you are excited by solving complex workforce challenges and reimagining HR policy, operations and technology to deliver lasting impact at scale, we would love to hear from you.

What You Will Do

You will be part of a high-performing team responsible for shaping Public Service-wide performance management and organisational design policies that strengthen both individual performance and organisational effectiveness.

Shape the Future of Performance Management

  • Lead the review, design and continuous evolution of Public Service-wide performance management frameworks, including appraisal, ranking and promotion.
  • Design policy, operational and digital solutions that keep performance management simple, effective and future-ready, supporting competency-based careers, diverse career pathways and a future-ready workforce.
  • Reimagine the employee and supervisor experience across the appraisal and development journey, strengthening manager capability, performance conversations and employee growth.
  • Partner across HR policy domains to build a coherent, integrated workforce policy ecosystem.

Design High-Performing and Future-Ready Organisations

  • Partner agencies to design organisation structures, job evaluation and workforce models that strengthen organisational effectiveness and build future-ready capabilities, aligned with strategic workforce plans.

jobDescription:
The Challenge

The Public Service operates in an increasingly complex environment shaped by changing citizen expectations, workforce shifts, technological disruption and greater interdependence across agencies. Public Sector Transformation (PST) seeks to ensure that the Singapore Public Service remains future-ready, effective and trusted by continually reimagining how the Public Service works, develops its workforce and organises itself.

The PST Cluster leads and coordinates Whole-of-Government transformation. Its role spans setting the vision and strategic direction for PST, catalysing deep organisational and business transformation, building the capabilities and ecosystem needed to sustain change, applying AI to the key challenges of today and mobilising leaders and officers around a shared transformation agenda.

As Senior Executive / Manager (Strategy), you will be involved in key PST strategic portfolios, covering sensemaking, conceptualising, catalyst and mobilising workstreams. You will play key roles in translating emerging priorities and senior leadership direction into coherent strategies, governance arrangements, programmes and resourcing approaches that enable transformation across the Public Service.

This is both a strategy and delivery role. You will work at the intersection of policy, organisational transformation, innovation, technology, workforce capability and public-sector governance.

Key Responsibilities

You will be part of a team of 3-5 officers who will be involved in some or all of the below:

A. Set and steward the strategic direction for Public Sector Transformation

  • Drive the development and continual refinement of the overarching PST strategy, identifying the major shifts required for the Public Service to remain effective and future-ready.
  • Synthesise emerging operating-environment trends, ground sentiment, organisational data and agency experience to surface strategic priorities and areas requiring Whole-of-Government intervention.
  • Support the translation of senior leadership direction into clear transformation outcomes, priorities, implementation pathways and narratives for agencies, leaders and officers.
  • Ensure PST priorities remain aligned with broader Whole-of-Government, Centre-of-Government and Public Service priorities.
  • Oversee the monitoring and reporting of PST progress, surfacing key achievements, implementation challenges and areas requiring leadership attention.

B. Drive cross-cutting and AI-enabled transformation

  • Shape and coordinate major cross-cutting transformation priorities requiring joint ownership across policy, technology, workforce and corporate-function stakeholders.
  • Support the driving of AI-enabled PST, ensuring technology adoption is connected to business and workflow redesign, organisational change, workforce implications and measurable outcomes.
  • Work with functional and mission leads to identify high-impact transformation opportunities, define the desired picture of success and establish coherent governance and tracking arrangements.
  • Develop proposals for the capabilities, funding, headcount and specialist support needed to implement transformation at scale.

C. Shape resourcing, governance and implementation arrangements

  • Design governance and operating arrangements that clarify accountability, enable timely decisions and provide progress assurance without imposing unnecessary process.
  • Develop and evaluate funding and manpower proposals for Whole-of-Government transformation initiatives, working with finance and policy partners to align transformation funding with strategic outcomes.
  • Establish portfolio-level measures, review mechanisms and reporting arrangements that support learning and course correction.

D. Mobilise and align Whole-of-Government partners

  • Build trusted relationships with Centre-of-Government partners, ministries, statutory boards, transformation offices and delivery agencies.
  • Convene stakeholders around shared outcomes, particularly where responsibilities and resources are distributed across organisations.
  • Develop engagement approaches across multiple levels, from senior leadership forums to working-level communities and agency visits.
